rules.rule_name: Detect No Change When Both New and Previously Stored Type Code Filters Are Blank
rules.rule_description: When the user leaves the Type Code filter field empty and no Type Code filter was previously stored in the session, the system recognises that no filter change has occurred and does not reset paging.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is new Type Code filter blank AND previously stored filter was also blank/empty?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type list screen and the new Type Code filter input field is blank (empty, low-values, or zeros), AND the previously stored Type Code filter value in the session is also blank (zeros, low-values, or spaces)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates whether the Type Code filter has changed after the user submits the screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system marks the Type Code filter status as UNCHANGED, and no paging variables are reset, allowing the current page position to be preserved

rules.rule_name: Detect No Change When New Type Code Filter Value Is Identical to Previously Stored Filter Value
rules.rule_description: When the user enters a Type Code filter value that is exactly the same as the one already stored in the session from the previous screen interaction, the system recognises no filter change has occurred and preserves the current page position.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is new Type Code filter value identical to previously stored filter value?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type list screen and has entered a Type Code filter value, AND the previously stored Type Code filter value in the session is not blank
acceptance_criteria.When: The system compares the newly entered Type Code filter value against the previously stored Type Code filter value in the session
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the new value is identical to the stored value, the system marks the Type Code filter status as UNCHANGED and no paging variables are reset, preserving the current page position

rules.rule_name: Mark Type Code Filter as Unchanged When No New Filter Is Applied
rules.rule_description: When the Type Code filter has not changed (either both are blank or the values are identical), the system explicitly marks the filter status as unchanged so that downstream processing knows not to reset paging or re-query data.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Mark Type Code Filter as UNCHANGED
No paging reset needed

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type list screen and either both the new and previously stored Type Code filter values are blank, OR the new Type Code filter value is identical to the previously stored value
acceptance_criteria.When: The system completes the Type Code filter change detection logic
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the Type Code filter change flag to UNCHANGED (FLG-TYPEFILTER-CHANGED-NO), and the current page number and paging position variables remain unaffected

rules.rule_name: Reset Paging Variables When a New Type Code Filter Is Applied
rules.rule_description: When the user applies a different Type Code filter value than what was previously stored, the system resets all paging variables so that the result list restarts from the first page, ensuring the user sees results relevant to the new filter from the beginning.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Reset Paging Variables
to start from beginning

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type list screen and has entered a Type Code filter value that is different from the previously stored Type Code filter value in the session
acceptance_criteria.When: The system detects that the Type Code filter value has changed
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system resets all paging variables (WS-CA-PAGING-VARIABLES) to their initial state, so that the next data retrieval will start from the first page of results matching the new filter

rules.rule_name: Save New Type Code Filter Value to Session Storage
rules.rule_description: When a new and different Type Code filter value is detected, the system saves the new filter value into the session communication area so it can be compared against future screen submissions to detect further changes.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Save new Type Code filter
value to session storage

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type list screen and has entered a Type Code filter value that is different from the previously stored Type Code filter value
acceptance_criteria.When: The system detects the Type Code filter has changed and resets paging variables
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system saves the newly entered Type Code filter value (WS-IN-TYPE-CD) into the session storage field (WS-CA-TYPE-CD) so that it becomes the reference value for future change detection on subsequent screen submissions

rules.rule_name: Mark Type Code Filter as Changed When a New Filter Value Is Applied
rules.rule_description: After detecting that the Type Code filter value has changed, resetting paging, and saving the new value, the system explicitly marks the filter status as CHANGED so that downstream processing (such as clearing row selections and re-querying data) is triggered appropriately.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Mark Type Code Filter
as CHANGED

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type list screen and has entered a Type Code filter value that differs from the previously stored value, AND the paging variables have been reset and the new filter value has been saved to session storage
acceptance_criteria.When: The system completes the Type Code filter change detection logic
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the Type Code filter change flag to CHANGED (FLG-TYPEFILTER-CHANGED-YES), which signals to subsequent processing steps that row selections should be cleared and data should be re-queried from the beginning using the new filter value

key_functionalities.title: Description Filter Validation
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Start: Description Filter Validation])
    B{Was a Description\nFilter entered by user?}
    C[Treat Description Filter\nas Blank - No filter applied\nAll records will be shown]
    D[Mark Description Filter\nas Valid]
    E[Wrap filter value with\nwildcard characters\nFormat: %entered-value%\nfor partial match search]
    F([End: Description Filter\nValidation Complete])

    A --> B
    B -->|No - Field is empty\nor blank| C
    C --> F
    B -->|Yes - Value was entered| D
    D --> E
    E --> F

rules.rule_name: Description Filter Treated as Blank When Not Supplied
rules.rule_description: When the user does not enter a description filter value (leaves it empty or blank), the system treats the description filter as not active, meaning no filtering by description will be applied and all transaction type records will be eligible for display.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Treat Description Filter as Blank - No filter applied
All records will be shown

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type maintenance screen and the Description Filter input field (WS-IN-TYPE-DESC) is either empty, contains only spaces, or contains low-values (no value entered)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system validates the Description Filter input
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Description Filter is marked as Blank (FLG-DESCFILTER-BLANK = TRUE), no description filter is applied to the data query, and all transaction type records are eligible to be displayed without any description-based restriction

rules.rule_name: Description Filter Marked as Valid When Value Is Supplied
rules.rule_description: When the user enters a description filter value, the system recognizes it as a valid filter input and marks it accordingly so that subsequent processing can apply the filter to the transaction type search.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Mark Description Filter as Valid

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type maintenance screen and the Description Filter input field (WS-IN-TYPE-DESC) contains a non-blank, non-empty value
acceptance_criteria.When: The system validates the Description Filter input
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Description Filter is marked as Valid (FLG-DESCFILTER-ISVALID = TRUE), indicating that a description-based filter should be applied when retrieving transaction type records

rules.rule_name: Description Filter Wrapped with Wildcard Characters for Partial Match Search
rules.rule_description: When a valid description filter value has been entered by the user, the system automatically wraps the entered value with wildcard characters (%) at both the beginning and end, enabling a partial/contains match search so that any transaction type whose description contains the entered text will be returned.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Wrap filter value with wildcard characters
Format: %entered-value%
for partial match search

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has entered a description filter value and the Description Filter has been marked as Valid (FLG-DESCFILTER-ISVALID = TRUE)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the description filter for use in the data query
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system constructs the filter value by concatenating a '%' wildcard character, followed by the trimmed user-entered description text, followed by another '%' wildcard character (format: %entered-value%), and stores this formatted value in WS-TYPE-DESC-FILTER for use in the LIKE search against the TR_DESCRIPTION column of the Transaction Type table

rules.rule_name: Description Filter Change Detection Against Previous Value
rules.rule_description: After validating the description filter, the system compares the newly entered filter value against the previously stored filter value to determine whether the user has changed the filter. This is used to decide whether paging state needs to be reset and whether row selections should be cleared.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Was a Description Filter entered by user?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Description Filter validation has completed and the system has a previously stored description filter value (WS-CA-TYPE-DESC) from the prior screen interaction
acceptance_criteria.When: The system compares the current description filter input (WS-IN-TYPE-DESC) with the previously stored value (WS-CA-TYPE-DESC)
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the current input equals the previously stored value, OR if the current filter is blank AND the previously stored value was also blank (empty, spaces, or low-values), then the Description Filter is marked as NOT changed (FLG-DESCFILTER-CHANGED-NO = TRUE) and paging state is preserved; otherwise the Description Filter is marked as CHANGED (FLG-DESCFILTER-CHANGED-YES = TRUE)

rules.rule_name: Paging State Reset When Description Filter Changes
rules.rule_description: When the user changes the description filter value from what was previously used, the system resets the paging position back to the beginning and saves the new filter value, ensuring that the results displayed reflect the new filter criteria starting from the first page.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Was a Description Filter entered by user?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has detected that the current description filter input (WS-IN-TYPE-DESC) is different from the previously stored description filter value (WS-CA-TYPE-DESC), meaning the user has modified the description filter
acceptance_criteria.When: The system processes the description filter change
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system resets all paging variables (WS-CA-PAGING-VARIABLES is initialized to starting values), saves the new description filter value (WS-IN-TYPE-DESC is moved to WS-CA-TYPE-DESC), and marks the Description Filter as Changed (FLG-DESCFILTER-CHANGED-YES = TRUE) so that the display will restart from the first page with the new filter applied

key_functionalities.title: Description Filter Change Detection
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    START([Description Filter Change Detection\nStart])
    COMPARE{Is current description filter\nthe same as previously\nstored filter value?}
    BLANKCHECK{Is current filter blank\nAND previously stored\nfilter was also blank?}
    NOCHANGE[Mark Description Filter\nas NOT Changed\nKeep existing paging position]
    CHANGED[Mark Description Filter\nas CHANGED]
    RESETPAGING[Reset Paging Variables\nReturn to first page\nof results]
    SAVENEW[Save new description filter\nvalue to session storage\nfor future comparison]
    END([Proceed to\nFilter Cross-Validation])

    START --> COMPARE
    COMPARE -->|Yes - Values Match| NOCHANGE
    COMPARE -->|No - Values Differ| BLANKCHECK
    BLANKCHECK -->|Yes - Both Blank| NOCHANGE
    BLANKCHECK -->|No - Genuinely Different| CHANGED
    CHANGED --> RESETPAGING
    RESETPAGING --> SAVENEW
    SAVENEW --> END
    NOCHANGE --> END

rules.rule_name: Description Filter Unchanged When Values Match
rules.rule_description: When the user submits a description filter value that is identical to the previously stored description filter, the system recognizes no change has occurred and retains the current paging position without resetting to the first page.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is current description filter the same as previously stored filter value?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has previously applied a description filter value stored in the session (WS-CA-TYPE-DESC), and the screen currently displays a page of transaction type results at a specific page position
acceptance_criteria.When: The user submits the screen with a description filter value (WS-IN-TYPE-DESC) that is exactly equal to the previously stored description filter value (WS-CA-TYPE-DESC)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The description filter is marked as NOT CHANGED (FLG-DESCFILTER-CHANGED-NO is set to TRUE), the existing paging position is preserved, and the system proceeds to filter cross-validation without resetting to the first page

rules.rule_name: Description Filter Unchanged When Both Current and Previous Filters Are Blank
rules.rule_description: When the user submits a blank description filter and the previously stored description filter was also blank (empty or unset), the system treats this as no change and retains the current paging position.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is current filter blank AND previously stored filter was also blank?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has not previously applied any description filter (the stored description filter value WS-CA-TYPE-DESC is either empty/blank spaces or uninitialized/low-values), and the screen currently displays a page of transaction type results at a specific page position
acceptance_criteria.When: The user submits the screen with a blank description filter (FLG-DESCFILTER-BLANK is TRUE, meaning WS-IN-TYPE-DESC contains only spaces or low-values) AND the previously stored description filter (WS-CA-TYPE-DESC) is also blank (equal to LOW-VALUES or SPACES)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The description filter is marked as NOT CHANGED (FLG-DESCFILTER-CHANGED-NO is set to TRUE), the existing paging position is preserved, and the system proceeds to filter cross-validation without resetting to the first page

rules.rule_name: Description Filter Changed - Reset Paging and Save New Filter Value
rules.rule_description: When the user submits a description filter value that is genuinely different from the previously stored filter (not a blank-to-blank transition and not an identical value), the system marks the filter as changed, resets all paging variables to return to the first page of results, and saves the new filter value for future comparison.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: No - Genuinely Different

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has previously applied a description filter value stored in the session (WS-CA-TYPE-DESC), and the screen currently displays a page of transaction type results at a specific page position
acceptance_criteria.When: The user submits the screen with a description filter value (WS-IN-TYPE-DESC) that is neither equal to the previously stored filter value (WS-CA-TYPE-DESC) nor a blank-to-blank transition (i.e., the new and old values are genuinely different)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The description filter is marked as CHANGED (FLG-DESCFILTER-CHANGED-YES is set to TRUE), all paging variables (WS-CA-PAGING-VARIABLES) are reset so the display returns to the first page of results, and the new description filter value (WS-IN-TYPE-DESC) is saved to session storage (WS-CA-TYPE-DESC) for future comparison, after which the system proceeds to filter cross-validation

key_functionalities.title: Filter Cross
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    START([Start Filter Cross-Validation])
    CHECKFILTERS{Is either Type Code Filter\nor Description Filter\nsupplied and valid?}
    SKIPVAL([Skip Validation\nNo filters to check])
    QUERYDB[Query Transaction Type table\nCount matching records using\napplied filter conditions]
    TRTYPE[(CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE\nDB2 Table)]
    RECORDSFOUND{At least one\nmatching record\nfound?}
    TYPEFILTERBAD{Was Type Code\nFilter supplied?}
    DESCFILTERBAD{Was Description\nFilter supplied?}
    MARKTYPEBAD[Mark Type Code Filter\nas Invalid]
    MARKDESCBAD[Mark Description Filter\nas Invalid]
    PROTECTROWS[Protect all row selection fields\nPrevent any row actions]
    SETERROR[Set Error Message:\n'No Records found for\nthese filter conditions']
    VALIDEND([Validation Passed\nProceed with filtered results])
    ERROREND([Validation Failed\nDisplay error to user])

    START --> CHECKFILTERS
    CHECKFILTERS -->|No filters supplied| SKIPVAL
    CHECKFILTERS -->|At least one filter supplied| QUERYDB
    QUERYDB --> TRTYPE
    TRTYPE -.->|Returns count of\nmatching records| RECORDSFOUND
    RECORDSFOUND -->|Records Found - Count > 0| VALIDEND
    RECORDSFOUND -->|No Records Found - Count = 0| TYPEFILTERBAD
    TYPEFILTERBAD -->|Yes| MARKTYPEBAD
    TYPEFILTERBAD -->|No| DESCFILTERBAD
    MARKTYPEBAD --> DESCFILTERBAD
    DESCFILTERBAD -->|Yes| MARKDESCBAD
    DESCFILTERBAD -->|No| PROTECTROWS
    MARKDESCBAD --> PROTECTROWS
    PROTECTROWS --> SETERROR
    SETERROR --> ERROREND

rules.rule_name: Skip Filter Cross-Validation When No Filters Are Supplied
rules.rule_description: Filter cross-validation against the Transaction Type table is only triggered when at least one filter (Type Code or Description) has been supplied and validated as a valid input. If neither filter is active, the cross-validation step is bypassed entirely.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is either Type Code Filter or Description Filter supplied and valid?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is on the Transaction Type maintenance screen and has not entered any value in the Type Code filter field and has not entered any value in the Description filter field
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates whether cross-validation of filters is required
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system skips the filter cross-validation step entirely and proceeds without querying the Transaction Type table for a record count

rules.rule_name: Query Transaction Type Table to Count Records Matching Active Filters
rules.rule_description: When at least one filter is active and valid, the system queries the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table to count how many records satisfy the supplied filter conditions. The Type Code filter applies an exact match on TR_TYPE, and the Description filter applies a partial (LIKE) match on TR_DESCRIPTION. Each filter is only applied when its corresponding flag indicates it is active.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Query Transaction Type table - Count matching records using applied filter conditions

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has supplied at least one valid filter — either a Type Code filter or a Description filter — on the Transaction Type maintenance screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The system performs cross-validation of the supplied filter conditions
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system executes a COUNT query against the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table applying the following conditions: if the Type Code filter is active (type flag = '1'), only records where TR_TYPE exactly equals the supplied type code are counted; if the Description filter is active (description flag = '1'), only records where TR_DESCRIPTION matches the supplied description text using a partial (LIKE) search are counted; both conditions are applied simultaneously when both filters are active; the resulting count is stored for subsequent validation

rules.rule_name: Mark Type Code Filter as Invalid When No Matching Records Found
rules.rule_description: When the count query returns zero matching records and the Type Code filter was supplied and valid, the Type Code filter field is marked as invalid to indicate to the user that the entered type code produced no results.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Mark Type Code Filter as Invalid

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has supplied a Type Code filter value that passed individual field validation, and the system has queried the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table using the active filter conditions
acceptance_criteria.When: The count of matching records returned by the query is zero AND the Type Code filter was supplied and marked as valid
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system marks the Type Code filter field as invalid (FLG-TYPEFILTER-NOT-OK) and sets the overall input status to error, indicating that the Type Code filter value produced no matching transaction type records

rules.rule_name: Mark Description Filter as Invalid When No Matching Records Found
rules.rule_description: When the count query returns zero matching records and the Description filter was supplied and valid, the Description filter field is marked as invalid to indicate to the user that the entered description text produced no results.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Mark Description Filter as Invalid

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has supplied a Description filter value that passed individual field validation, and the system has queried the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table using the active filter conditions
acceptance_criteria.When: The count of matching records returned by the query is zero AND the Description filter was supplied and marked as valid
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system marks the Description filter field as invalid (FLG-DESCFILTER-NOT-OK) and sets the overall input status to error, indicating that the Description filter value produced no matching transaction type records

rules.rule_name: Protect All Row Selection Fields When Filter Conditions Return No Records
rules.rule_description: When no records are found matching the supplied filter conditions, all row selection fields on the screen are locked (protected) to prevent the user from attempting to select, update, or delete any rows while the filter is in an error state.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Protect all row selection fields - Prevent any row actions

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has determined that no records in the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table match the supplied filter conditions
acceptance_criteria.When: The count of matching records is zero
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the row protection flag (FLG-PROTECT-SELECT-ROWS-YES) to true, which causes all row selection fields on the screen to be rendered as protected and non-enterable, preventing the user from performing any row-level actions such as update or delete

rules.rule_name: Set Error Message When No Records Found for Filter Conditions
rules.rule_description: When the filter cross-validation determines that no records exist in the Transaction Type table matching the supplied filter criteria, a specific error message is set to inform the user that their filter conditions produced no results.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Error Message: 'No Records found for these filter conditions'

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has evaluated the supplied filter conditions against the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table and found zero matching records
acceptance_criteria.When: The count of matching records is zero after querying with the active Type Code filter and/or Description filter
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error message to 'No Records found for these filter conditions' and displays it on the screen, and the overall input validation status is set to error so that no further processing of row actions is performed

rules.rule_name: Proceed with Filtered Results When Matching Records Exist
rules.rule_description: When the count query confirms that at least one record exists in the Transaction Type table matching the supplied filter conditions, the cross-validation passes and the system proceeds to display the filtered transaction type records.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Validation Passed - Proceed with filtered results

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has supplied at least one valid filter — either a Type Code filter or a Description filter — on the Transaction Type maintenance screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The count of records in CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE matching the supplied filter conditions is greater than zero
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system considers the filter cross-validation as passed, does not set any filter error flags, does not protect row selection fields, and proceeds to retrieve and display the matching transaction type records on the screen

key_functionalities.title: PF Key Validation
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    START([User Presses a Key])
    SETINVALID[Mark Key as Invalid\nby Default]
    CHECKKEY{Which Key\nWas Pressed?}
    ENTER[Enter Key]
    PF2[PF2 - Add New\nTransaction Type]
    PF3[PF3 - Exit to\nMain Menu]
    PF7[PF7 - Previous\nPage]
    PF8[PF8 - Next\nPage]
    PF10{PF10 - Confirm\nAction}
    DELETEPENDING{Is a Delete\nAction Pending?}
    UPDATEPENDING{Is an Update\nAction Pending?}
    VALIDKEY[Mark Key as Valid\nProceed with Action]
    INVALIDKEY[Key Not Permitted\nin Current Context\nTreat as Enter Key]

    START --> SETINVALID
    SETINVALID --> CHECKKEY
    CHECKKEY -->|Enter| ENTER
    CHECKKEY -->|PF2| PF2
    CHECKKEY -->|PF3| PF3
    CHECKKEY -->|PF7| PF7
    CHECKKEY -->|PF8| PF8
    CHECKKEY -->|PF10| PF10
    CHECKKEY -->|Any Other Key| INVALIDKEY
    ENTER --> VALIDKEY
    PF2 --> VALIDKEY
    PF3 --> VALIDKEY
    PF7 --> VALIDKEY
    PF8 --> VALIDKEY
    PF10 --> DELETEPENDING
    DELETEPENDING -->|Yes - Delete Pending| VALIDKEY
    DELETEPENDING -->|No| UPDATEPENDING
    UPDATEPENDING -->|Yes - Update Pending| VALIDKEY
    UPDATEPENDING -->|No - Nothing Pending| INVALIDKEY
    INVALIDKEY --> VALIDKEY
    VALIDKEY --> END([Proceed to\nProcess Action])

rules.rule_name: Default All Key Presses to Invalid Before Validation
rules.rule_description: Before any key validation logic is applied, every key press is initially marked as invalid. This ensures that only explicitly permitted keys are allowed to proceed, and no key is assumed valid by default.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Mark Key as Invalid by Default

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has pressed any key on the Transaction Type Maintenance screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The program begins processing the key press
acceptance_criteria.Then: The key is immediately marked as INVALID before any further validation is performed, ensuring no key is permitted by default

rules.rule_name: Recognize and Record the Function Key Pressed by the User
rules.rule_description: The program identifies which physical key the user pressed and records it as a logical key indicator. Keys PF13–PF24 are treated as equivalents to PF1–PF12 respectively, so the same logical action is triggered regardless of which shift-key variant is used.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Which Key Was Pressed?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is on the Transaction Type Maintenance screen and presses a key
acceptance_criteria.When: The program reads the key press from the terminal interface
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program records the logical key as one of: ENTER, PF2, PF3, PF4, PF5, PF6, PF7, PF8, PF9, PF10, PF11, PF12 — where PF13 through PF24 are treated as equivalent to PF1 through PF12 respectively — and sets the corresponding key indicator flag to TRUE

rules.rule_name: Mark ENTER Key as a Valid and Permitted Action
rules.rule_description: The ENTER key is always a permitted key on the Transaction Type Maintenance screen and is unconditionally marked as valid when pressed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Enter Key

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is on the Transaction Type Maintenance screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses the ENTER key
acceptance_criteria.Then: The key is marked as VALID and processing proceeds with the ENTER action

rules.rule_name: Mark PF2 as Valid to Navigate to Add Transaction Type Screen
rules.rule_description: PF2 is always a permitted key on the Transaction Type Maintenance screen. When pressed, it is marked as valid and the program proceeds to navigate the user to the Add New Transaction Type screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: PF2 - Add New Transaction Type

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is on the Transaction Type Maintenance screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses PF2
acceptance_criteria.Then: The key is marked as VALID and processing proceeds to navigate to the Add New Transaction Type screen

rules.rule_name: Mark PF3 as Valid to Exit to Main Menu
rules.rule_description: PF3 is always a permitted key on the Transaction Type Maintenance screen. When pressed, it is marked as valid and the program proceeds to navigate the user back to the calling program or Admin menu.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: PF3 - Exit to Main Menu

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is on the Transaction Type Maintenance screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses PF3
acceptance_criteria.Then: The key is marked as VALID and processing proceeds to exit to the calling program or Admin menu

rules.rule_name: Mark PF7 as Valid to Navigate to Previous Page
rules.rule_description: PF7 is always a permitted key on the Transaction Type Maintenance screen. When pressed, it is marked as valid and the program proceeds to scroll backward to the previous page of transaction types.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: PF7 - Previous Page

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is on the Transaction Type Maintenance screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses PF7
acceptance_criteria.Then: The key is marked as VALID and processing proceeds to display the previous page of transaction type records

rules.rule_name: Mark PF8 as Valid to Navigate to Next Page
rules.rule_description: PF8 is always a permitted key on the Transaction Type Maintenance screen. When pressed, it is marked as valid and the program proceeds to scroll forward to the next page of transaction types.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: PF8 - Next Page

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is on the Transaction Type Maintenance screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses PF8
acceptance_criteria.Then: The key is marked as VALID and processing proceeds to display the next page of transaction type records

rules.rule_name: Allow PF10 Only When a Delete Action is Pending Confirmation
rules.rule_description: PF10 is a conditional key. It is only permitted when the user has previously selected a Delete action on a transaction type row and is now confirming that deletion. If a delete is pending, PF10 is marked as valid.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is a Delete Action Pending?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is on the Transaction Type Maintenance screen and has previously selected the Delete action (D) on a transaction type row and pressed ENTER to initiate the confirmation step
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses PF10
acceptance_criteria.Then: The key is marked as VALID because a delete action is pending, and processing proceeds to execute the deletion of the selected transaction type

rules.rule_name: Allow PF10 Only When an Update Action is Pending Confirmation
rules.rule_description: PF10 is a conditional key. It is only permitted when the user has previously selected an Update action on a transaction type row and is now confirming that update. If an update is pending, PF10 is marked as valid.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is an Update Action Pending?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is on the Transaction Type Maintenance screen and has previously selected the Update action (U) on a transaction type row and pressed ENTER to initiate the confirmation step
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses PF10
acceptance_criteria.Then: The key is marked as VALID because an update action is pending, and processing proceeds to execute the update of the selected transaction type's description

rules.rule_name: Reject PF10 When No Delete or Update Action is Pending
rules.rule_description: PF10 is not permitted when neither a delete nor an update action is currently pending. In this context, pressing PF10 has no special meaning and is treated as if the user pressed ENTER, preventing accidental confirmations.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Key Not Permitted in Current Context
Treat as Enter Key

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is on the Transaction Type Maintenance screen and no delete or update action has been previously selected and initiated
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses PF10
acceptance_criteria.Then: PF10 is treated as an invalid key in the current context, the key indicator is overridden to ENTER, and the screen is refreshed as if the user pressed ENTER with no action pending

rules.rule_name: Reject Any Unrecognized Key and Treat as ENTER
rules.rule_description: Any key press that is not one of the explicitly permitted keys (ENTER, PF2, PF3, PF7, PF8, or PF10 with a pending action) is not a valid action on this screen. Such key presses are silently treated as ENTER to prevent unexpected behavior.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Key Not Permitted in Current Context
Treat as Enter Key

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is on the Transaction Type Maintenance screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses any key other than ENTER, PF2, PF3, PF7, PF8, or PF10 (with a pending delete or update) — for example PF1, PF4, PF5, PF6, PF9, PF11, PF12, PA1, PA2, or CLEAR
acceptance_criteria.Then: The key is marked as INVALID, the key indicator is overridden and set to ENTER, and the screen is refreshed as if the user pressed ENTER

rules.rule_name: Proceed with Processing After Key Validation is Complete
rules.rule_description: Once a key has been determined to be valid — either because it is an unconditionally permitted key or because the conditional requirements for PF10 are met — the program proceeds to execute the corresponding business action for that key.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Mark Key as Valid
Proceed with Action

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has pressed a key on the Transaction Type Maintenance screen and the key has passed all validation checks and is marked as VALID
acceptance_criteria.When: Key validation is complete
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program proceeds to execute the business action associated with the validated key: ENTER submits the screen, PF2 navigates to Add Transaction Type, PF3 exits to the menu, PF7 scrolls to the previous page, PF8 scrolls to the next page, and PF10 confirms the pending delete or update action

program as destination]
    F --> H[Update communication area
with current program context,
map name, and mapset name]
    G --> H
    H --> I[Transfer control to
Administration Menu Program
passing updated
communication area]
    I --> Z([Administration Menu
Screen Displayed])

rules.rule_name: Determine Destination Transaction When PF3 is Pressed
rules.rule_description: When the user presses PF3 to exit, the system determines which transaction to return to. If the session was started directly, started from the same transaction, or no originating transaction is recorded, the system defaults to the Administration Menu transaction. Otherwise, it returns to the originating transaction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Was the session started from another transaction?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type Maintenance screen and presses PF3 to exit
acceptance_criteria.When: The originating transaction ID is empty, blank, or is the same as the current Transaction Type Maintenance transaction ID
acceptance_criteria.Then: The destination transaction is set to the Administration Menu transaction ID; otherwise, the destination transaction is set to the originating transaction ID that launched this screen

rules.rule_name: Determine Destination Program When PF3 is Pressed
rules.rule_description: When the user presses PF3 to exit, the system determines which program to transfer control to. If the session was started directly, started from the same program, or no originating program is recorded, the system defaults to the Administration Menu program. Otherwise, it returns to the originating program.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Was the session started from another program?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type Maintenance screen and presses PF3 to exit, and the destination transaction has already been determined
acceptance_criteria.When: The originating program name is empty, blank, or is the same as the current Transaction Type Maintenance program name
acceptance_criteria.Then: The destination program is set to the Administration Menu program; otherwise, the destination program is set to the originating program that launched this screen

rules.rule_name: Update Communication Area Context Before Exiting via PF3
rules.rule_description: Before transferring control to the destination program, the communication area must be updated to record the current program as the originator, set the user type to Admin, mark the program state as entering, and record the current map and mapset names so the destination program has accurate context about where the user came from.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Update communication area with current program context, map name, and mapset name

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF3 and the destination transaction and program have been determined
acceptance_criteria.When: The system is preparing to transfer control to the destination program
acceptance_criteria.Then: The communication area is updated with: the current Transaction Type Maintenance transaction ID as the originating transaction, the current Transaction Type Maintenance program name as the originating program, user type set to Admin, program state set to Entering, and the current map name and mapset name recorded

rules.rule_name: Commit Pending Changes Before Exiting via PF3
rules.rule_description: Before transferring control to the destination program when PF3 is pressed, all pending database changes must be committed to ensure data consistency. This commit occurs prior to the program transfer so that no uncommitted work is carried over to the next program.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Transfer control to Administration Menu Program passing updated communication area

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF3, the destination has been determined, and the communication area has been updated
acceptance_criteria.When: The system is about to transfer control to the destination program
acceptance_criteria.Then: A synchronization point (commit) is issued to permanently save any pending database changes before the program transfer occurs

rules.rule_name: Transfer Control to Destination Program When PF3 is Pressed
rules.rule_description: After committing pending changes and updating the communication area, the system transfers control to the determined destination program (either the Administration Menu program or the originating program), passing the updated communication area so the destination program has full context of the user session.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Transfer control to Administration Menu Program passing updated communication area

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF3, the destination program has been determined, the communication area has been updated with current context, and pending changes have been committed
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the program transfer
acceptance_criteria.Then: Control is transferred to the destination program with the updated communication area passed along, and the Administration Menu screen (or originating program screen) is displayed to the user

rules.rule_name: Set Destination to Administration Menu When No Valid Originator Exists
rules.rule_description: When PF3 is pressed and the session has no valid originating transaction or program (i.e., the user started the session directly or from the same transaction/program), the system defaults both the destination transaction and destination program to the Administration Menu, ensuring the user always has a valid return destination.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set destination to Administration Menu Transaction

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user presses PF3 to exit the Transaction Type Maintenance screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The originating transaction ID is empty, contains only spaces, or matches the current Transaction Type Maintenance transaction ID, AND the originating program name is empty, contains only spaces, or matches the current Transaction Type Maintenance program name
acceptance_criteria.Then: The destination transaction is set to the Administration Menu transaction ID and the destination program is set to the Administration Menu program name

rules.rule_name: Use Originating Transaction and Program as Return Destination
rules.rule_description: When PF3 is pressed and the session was launched from another transaction and program, the system uses the recorded originating transaction ID and program name as the return destination, ensuring the user is returned to exactly where they came from.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Use the originating transaction as destination

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user presses PF3 to exit the Transaction Type Maintenance screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The originating transaction ID is not empty, not blank, and does not match the current Transaction Type Maintenance transaction ID, AND the originating program name is not empty, not blank, and does not match the current Transaction Type Maintenance program name
acceptance_criteria.Then: The destination transaction is set to the originating transaction ID and the destination program is set to the originating program name that originally launched the Transaction Type Maintenance screen

key_functionalities.title: Navigate to Add Transaction Type Screen
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([User Presses PF2\non Transaction Type List Screen])
    B{Is the current active program\nthe Transaction Type List program?}
    C[Record current program and\ntransaction context for return navigation]
    D[Set destination as\nAdd/Update Transaction Type program\nwith its map and mapset]
    E[Pass current session context\nvia communication area]
    F([Transfer control to\nAdd/Update Transaction Type Screen])
    G([No Action Taken\nContinue with current screen])

    A --> B
    B -->|Yes - Navigating from\nTransaction Type List| C
    B -->|No - Not from\nTransaction Type List| G
    C --> D
    D --> E
    E --> F

rules.rule_name: Restrict PF2 Navigation to Add Screen Only When on Transaction Type List
rules.rule_description: PF2 key to navigate to the Add Transaction Type screen is only honored when the user is currently active on the Transaction Type List program. If PF2 is pressed from any other context, no navigation action is taken.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is the current active program the Transaction Type List program?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is interacting with the Transaction Type maintenance application and presses the PF2 key
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates whether the currently active program is the Transaction Type List program (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM equals LIT-THISPGM)
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the current program IS the Transaction Type List program, the system proceeds with navigation to the Add Transaction Type screen. If the current program is NOT the Transaction Type List program, no navigation action is taken and the current screen remains unchanged.

rules.rule_name: Record Current Program and Transaction Context Before Navigating Away
rules.rule_description: Before transferring control to the Add Transaction Type screen, the system records the current transaction ID, program name, mapset, and map in the communication area so that the destination program knows where to return upon completion.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Record current program and transaction context for return navigation

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF2 and the system has confirmed the current active program is the Transaction Type List program
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to navigate to the Add Transaction Type screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system records the current Transaction Type List transaction ID (LIT-THISTRANID) as the originating transaction ID (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID), records the current Transaction Type List program name (LIT-THISPGM) as the originating program (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM), records the current mapset (LIT-THISMAPSET) as the last used mapset (CDEMO-LAST-MAPSET), and records the current map (LIT-THISMAP) as the last used map (CDEMO-LAST-MAP) in the communication area.

rules.rule_name: Set User Type to Regular User When Navigating to Add Transaction Type Screen
rules.rule_description: When navigating to the Add Transaction Type screen via PF2, the user context is set to regular user type (not admin), and the program entry mode is set to initial entry.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Record current program and transaction context for return navigation

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF2 and the system has confirmed the current active program is the Transaction Type List program
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the session context for transfer to the Add Transaction Type screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the user type to regular user (CDEMO-USRTYP-USER = TRUE) and sets the program mode to initial entry (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER = TRUE) in the communication area.

rules.rule_name: Set Destination Program and Map Details for Add Transaction Type Screen
rules.rule_description: The system designates the Add/Update Transaction Type program as the navigation destination, along with its associated map and mapset identifiers, so the correct screen is displayed upon transfer.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set destination as Add/Update Transaction Type program with its map and mapset

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF2, the current program is confirmed as the Transaction Type List program, and the return navigation context has been recorded
acceptance_criteria.When: The system sets up the destination for the screen transfer
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the destination program to the Add Transaction Type program (LIT-ADDTPGM stored in CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM), sets the next mapset to the Add Transaction Type mapset (LIT-ADDTMAPSET stored in CCARD-NEXT-MAPSET), and sets the next map to the Add Transaction Type map (LIT-ADDTMAP stored in CCARD-NEXT-MAP).

rules.rule_name: Transfer Control to Add Transaction Type Screen with Session Context
rules.rule_description: The system transfers full control to the Add Transaction Type program, passing the complete session communication area so that the destination program has all necessary context including user identity, return navigation details, and program state.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Transfer control to Add/Update Transaction Type Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The destination program has been set to the Add Transaction Type program, the return navigation context has been recorded, and the user type has been set to regular user
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the transfer of control
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the exit message indicator (WS-EXIT-MESSAGE = TRUE), sets program entry mode to initial entry (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER = TRUE), and transfers control to the Add Transaction Type program (LIT-ADDTPGM) passing the full communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) so the destination program receives all session context. Control does not return to the Transaction Type List program.

key_functionalities.description: Navigate to Add Transaction Type Screen

key_functionalities.title: Forward Paging
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    START([Forward Paging Triggered\nPF8 Pressed - Next Page])
    SETKEY[Set Start Key to\nLast Transaction Code\nof Current Page]
    INCPAGE[Increment Page Number by 1]
    CLEARROWS[Clear All Current\nScreen Row Data]
    OPENCURSOR[Open Forward Reading Cursor\non Transaction Type Table\nStarting from Last Key]
    DB2[(CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE\nDB2 Table)]
    INITROW[Initialize Row Counter to Zero]
    FETCHROW[Fetch Next Transaction Type Record\nType Code and Description]
    FETCHRESULT{Record\nFetched?}
    ADDROW[Add Record to Screen Row\nStore Type Code and Description]
    FIRSTROW{Is This the\nFirst Row?}
    STOREFIRSTKEY[Store This Type Code\nas First Key of New Page]
    MAXROWS{Maximum 7 Rows\nReached?}
    STORELASTKEY[Store This Type Code\nas Last Key of Current Page]
    EXTRAFETCH[Fetch One More Record\nto Check if More Pages Exist]
    MOREEXIST{Another Record\nExists?}
    SETNEXTYES[Mark: More Pages Exist\nUser Can Page Forward Again]
    SETNEXTNO[Mark: No More Pages\nThis is the Last Page]
    LASTPAGEFLAG[Set Last Page Indicator\nSo User is Informed]
    NORECORDS{Any Records\nReturned at All?}
    NORECORDSMSG[Display Message:\nNo Records Found\nfor Current Search Conditions]
    CLOSECURSOR[Close Forward Reading Cursor]
    DISPLAYPAGE[Display Up to 7 Transaction Type Records\nwith Type Codes and Descriptions\non List Screen]
    END([Screen Displayed\nto User])

    START --> SETKEY
    SETKEY --> INCPAGE
    INCPAGE --> CLEARROWS
    CLEARROWS --> OPENCURSOR
    OPENCURSOR --> DB2
    DB2 -.->|Forward Cursor Opened\nFiltered by Type Code\nand Description Filters| INITROW
    INITROW --> FETCHROW
    FETCHROW --> FETCHRESULT
    FETCHRESULT -->|Yes - Record Found| ADDROW
    ADDROW --> FIRSTROW
    FIRSTROW -->|Yes - First Record| STOREFIRSTKEY
    FIRSTROW -->|No| MAXROWS
    STOREFIRSTKEY --> MAXROWS
    MAXROWS -->|No - Continue Reading| FETCHROW
    MAXROWS -->|Yes - 7 Rows Filled| STORELASTKEY
    STORELASTKEY --> EXTRAFETCH
    EXTRAFETCH --> MOREEXIST
    MOREEXIST -->|Yes - More Records Exist| SETNEXTYES
    MOREEXIST -->|No - End of Data| SETNEXTNO
    SETNEXTNO --> LASTPAGEFLAG
    SETNEXTYES --> CLOSECURSOR
    LASTPAGEFLAG --> CLOSECURSOR
    FETCHRESULT -->|No - No More Records| NORECORDS
    NORECORDS -->|Records Were Shown| SETNEXTNO
    NORECORDS -->|Zero Records on Page 1| NORECORDSMSG
    NORECORDSMSG --> CLOSECURSOR
    CLOSECURSOR --> DISPLAYPAGE
    DISPLAYPAGE --> END

rules.rule_name: Set Start Key to Last Transaction Code of Current Page for Forward Navigation
rules.rule_description: When the user presses PF8 to navigate to the next page, the system uses the last transaction type code displayed on the current page as the starting point for reading the next set of records.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Start Key to Last Transaction Code of Current Page

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is viewing a page of transaction type records and a next page exists beyond the current display
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses PF8 to scroll forward to the next page
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the start key for the next database read to the last transaction type code that was displayed on the current page, ensuring the next page begins immediately after the current page's last record

rules.rule_name: Increment Page Number When Navigating Forward
rules.rule_description: Each time the user navigates forward to the next page, the current page number is incremented by 1 to reflect the new page position in the result set.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Increment Page Number by 1

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on a page of transaction type records and presses PF8 to go to the next page
acceptance_criteria.When: The forward paging operation is triggered
acceptance_criteria.Then: The page number counter is increased by exactly 1, and the updated page number is displayed on the screen to inform the user of their current position in the result set

rules.rule_name: Clear All Screen Row Data Before Loading New Page
rules.rule_description: Before reading and displaying a new page of transaction type records, all previously displayed row data on the screen must be cleared to prevent stale data from appearing alongside new records.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Clear All Current Screen Row Data

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen currently displays transaction type records from the previous page
acceptance_criteria.When: A forward page read operation is initiated
acceptance_criteria.Then: All existing row data (transaction type codes and descriptions) stored for screen display are cleared to empty/low values before any new records are fetched from the database

rules.rule_name: Clear Row Selection Flags When Moving to Next Page
rules.rule_description: When the user navigates to the next page, any previously selected row actions (delete or update selections) from the prior page are cleared so that no unintended actions carry over to the new page.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Clear All Current Screen Row Data

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user may have had row selections (delete or update flags) set on the current page
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses PF8 and the system moves to the next page
acceptance_criteria.Then: All row selection flags are reset to blank/empty, ensuring no prior page selections are retained on the new page

rules.rule_name: Read Transaction Type Records Forward from Start Key with Active Filters
rules.rule_description: The system reads transaction type records from the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table in ascending order by transaction type code, starting from the specified start key, and applies any active type code or description filters.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Open Forward Reading Cursor on Transaction Type Table Starting from Last Key

acceptance_criteria.Given: A start key has been set to the last transaction type code of the current page, and optional filters for type code and/or description may be active
acceptance_criteria.When: The forward reading cursor is opened against the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system retrieves records where the transaction type code is greater than or equal to the start key, AND if the type code filter is active, only records with an exact match on the type code are included, AND if the description filter is active, only records whose description contains the filter text (partial match) are included, with results ordered ascending by transaction type code

rules.rule_name: Store First Transaction Type Code of New Page
rules.rule_description: The transaction type code of the very first record fetched for a new page is stored as the first key of that page, enabling backward navigation to return to this page later.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Store This Type Code as First Key of New Page

acceptance_criteria.Given: The forward reading cursor has been opened and records are being fetched
acceptance_criteria.When: The first record is successfully fetched from the database (row counter equals 1)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The transaction type code of that first record is stored as the first transaction type code for the current page, and if the page number is currently zero it is set to 1

rules.rule_name: Populate Screen Rows with Fetched Transaction Type Records Up to Maximum of 7
rules.rule_description: Each successfully fetched transaction type record is added to the screen display, storing both the transaction type code and its description, until the maximum number of displayable rows (7) is reached.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Add Record to Screen Row - Store Type Code and Description

acceptance_criteria.Given: The forward reading cursor is open and records are being fetched from CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE
acceptance_criteria.When: A record is successfully fetched (transaction type code and description are returned)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The row counter is incremented by 1, the transaction type code is stored in the corresponding screen row position, and the transaction type description text is stored in the corresponding screen row position, continuing until either no more records exist or 7 rows have been filled

rules.rule_name: Stop Reading After Maximum 7 Rows Are Filled
rules.rule_description: The screen can display a maximum of 7 transaction type records per page. Once 7 rows have been populated, the system stops the main fetch loop regardless of how many more records may exist in the database.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Maximum 7 Rows Reached?

acceptance_criteria.Given: Records are being fetched from the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table and added to screen rows
acceptance_criteria.When: The row counter reaches the maximum screen lines value of 7
acceptance_criteria.Then: The fetch loop is flagged to exit, the transaction type code of the 7th record is stored as the last transaction type code of the current page, and the system proceeds to perform an extra fetch to determine if additional pages exist

rules.rule_name: Store Last Transaction Type Code of Current Page
rules.rule_description: When the maximum number of rows for a page is reached, the transaction type code of the last displayed record is stored as the last key of the current page, which will serve as the start key for the next forward page navigation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Store This Type Code as Last Key of Current Page

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen has been filled with the maximum 7 transaction type records
acceptance_criteria.When: The 7th record is added to the screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: The transaction type code of the 7th (last) record is stored as the last transaction type code for the current page, to be used as the starting point if the user presses PF8 again

rules.rule_name: Perform Extra Fetch to Determine if Additional Pages Exist
rules.rule_description: After filling all 7 screen rows, the system performs one additional database fetch beyond the displayed records to determine whether more transaction type records exist, enabling the system to correctly indicate whether further forward paging is possible.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Fetch One More Record to Check if More Pages Exist

acceptance_criteria.Given: All 7 screen rows have been filled with transaction type records
acceptance_criteria.When: The system performs one additional fetch from the forward reading cursor
acceptance_criteria.Then: If an additional record is found, the system marks that more pages exist and updates the last transaction type code to this extra record's type code; if no additional record is found (end of data), the system marks that no more pages exist

rules.rule_name: Mark Next Page as Available When More Records Exist Beyond Current Page
rules.rule_description: When the extra fetch after filling 7 rows returns a record, the system marks that a next page is available, allowing the user to continue pressing PF8 to see more transaction type records.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Mark: More Pages Exist - User Can Page Forward Again

acceptance_criteria.Given: All 7 screen rows have been filled and an extra fetch has been performed
acceptance_criteria.When: The extra fetch returns a valid record (more data exists in the database beyond the current page)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the next-page-exists indicator to TRUE and stores the extra fetched record's transaction type code as the new last transaction type code for the current page, so that the next PF8 press will start from the correct position

rules.rule_name: Mark No More Pages When End of Data Reached After Full Page
rules.rule_description: When the extra fetch after filling 7 rows returns no record, the system marks that the current page is the last page and no further forward navigation is possible.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Mark: No More Pages - This is the Last Page

acceptance_criteria.Given: All 7 screen rows have been filled and an extra fetch has been performed
acceptance_criteria.When: The extra fetch returns no record (end of data reached, SQL code +100)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the next-page-does-not-exist indicator to TRUE, and if the user pressed PF8 to get here, a message is set to inform the user that no more records are available

rules.rule_name: Mark No More Pages When End of Data Reached During Page Fill
rules.rule_description: When the database returns no more records before all 7 screen rows are filled, the system marks that no further pages exist and the current page is the last page.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Mark: No More Pages - This is the Last Page

acceptance_criteria.Given: The forward reading cursor is open and records are being fetched to fill screen rows
acceptance_criteria.When: The database returns end-of-data (no more records) before 7 rows are filled
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the next-page-does-not-exist indicator to TRUE, stores the last fetched transaction type code as the last key, and if the user pressed PF8 to trigger this read, a message is set indicating no more records are available

rules.rule_name: Display No Records Found Message When Zero Records Returned on First Page
rules.rule_description: If the database returns no records at all when reading the first page (page number equals 1 and row count is zero), the system displays a message informing the user that no transaction type records were found matching the current search conditions.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Message: No Records Found for Current Search Conditions

acceptance_criteria.Given: The forward reading cursor has been opened and a fetch is attempted on page 1
acceptance_criteria.When: The database returns no records at all (end-of-data on the very first fetch, row counter is zero, and screen number is 1)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the no-records-found message indicator so that the screen displays a message informing the user that no transaction type records exist for the current filter conditions

rules.rule_name: Display Up to 7 Transaction Type Records on List Screen
rules.rule_description: After reading records from the database, the system sends the screen to the user displaying up to 7 transaction type records, each showing the transaction type code and its description.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Up to 7 Transaction Type Records with Type Codes and Descriptions on List Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The forward read operation has completed and screen rows have been populated with transaction type records
acceptance_criteria.When: The send map operation is executed to display the screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: The screen is displayed to the user showing up to 7 rows of transaction type data, each row containing the transaction type code and its description, along with the current page number, date, time, and any applicable informational messages

key_functionalities.title: Backward Paging
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    START([PF7 Pressed - Navigate to Previous Page])
    CLEARROWS[Clear all current row data\nfrom the display area]
    SETCOUNTER[Set row counter to maximum\n7 rows - filling from bottom up]
    OPENCURSOR[Open Backward Database Cursor\nRead records with Type Code LESS THAN\ncurrent first key on screen\nOrdered by Type Code DESCENDING]
    TRTYPE_BWD[(CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE\nDB2 Table)]
    FETCHROW[Fetch next record\nfrom backward cursor]
    FETCHRESULT{Record\nFetched?}
    FILLROW[Fill current row position\nwith fetched Type Code\nand Description]
    DECREMENTROW[Move to next row position\nupward - decrement row counter]
    ROWCOUNTERZERO{All 7 rows\nfilled?}
    SAVEFIRSTKEY[Save this Type Code as\nthe new First Key of the page]
    DECREMENTPAGE[Decrement Page Number\nby 1]
    CLOSECURSOR[Close Backward Cursor]
    DISPLAYPAGE[Display the previous page\nwith records now ordered\ncorrectly top to bottom]
    END([Return to Send Map])

    START --> CLEARROWS
    CLEARROWS --> SETCOUNTER
    SETCOUNTER --> OPENCURSOR
    OPENCURSOR --> TRTYPE_BWD
    TRTYPE_BWD -.->|Backward Cursor Opened| FETCHROW
    FETCHROW --> FETCHRESULT
    FETCHRESULT -->|Record Found| FILLROW
    FILLROW --> DECREMENTROW
    DECREMENTROW --> ROWCOUNTERZERO
    ROWCOUNTERZERO -->|No - Continue Filling| FETCHROW
    ROWCOUNTERZERO -->|Yes - Page Full| SAVEFIRSTKEY
    SAVEFIRSTKEY --> DECREMENTPAGE
    FETCHRESULT -->|No More Records| DECREMENTPAGE
    DECREMENTPAGE --> CLOSECURSOR
    CLOSECURSOR --> DISPLAYPAGE
    DISPLAYPAGE --> END

rules.rule_name: Clear Display Area Before Loading Previous Page
rules.rule_description: Before reading and displaying the previous page of transaction type records, all currently displayed row data must be cleared to ensure no stale data remains on screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Clear all current row data from the display area

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is viewing a page of Transaction Type records and presses PF7 to navigate to the previous page
acceptance_criteria.When: The backward paging process is initiated
acceptance_criteria.Then: All currently displayed row data (Transaction Type Codes and Descriptions for all rows) in the display area are cleared before any new records are loaded

rules.rule_name: Initialize Row Counter to Maximum for Bottom-Up Fill
rules.rule_description: When reading records in reverse order (descending by Type Code), the row counter must be initialized to the maximum number of displayable rows (7) so that records are placed from the bottom of the screen upward, resulting in correct top-to-bottom ascending order when displayed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set row counter to maximum 7 rows - filling from bottom up

acceptance_criteria.Given: The backward paging process has been initiated and the display area has been cleared
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to fetch records from the database in descending order
acceptance_criteria.Then: The row position counter is set to the maximum number of screen rows (7), so that the first record fetched is placed in the last row position and subsequent records fill upward toward row 1

rules.rule_name: Open Backward Database Cursor with Filter Conditions
rules.rule_description: The backward cursor must be opened to retrieve Transaction Type records that come before the current page's first record, applying any active Type Code or Description filters, and ordering results in descending Type Code order to enable bottom-up screen filling.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Open Backward Database Cursor - Read records with Type Code LESS THAN current first key on screen - Ordered by Type Code DESCENDING

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is preparing to display the previous page of Transaction Type records, and the current page's first Transaction Type Code (start key) is known, and optional Type Code filter and/or Description filter may be active
acceptance_criteria.When: The backward database cursor is opened against the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table
acceptance_criteria.Then: The cursor retrieves records where the Transaction Type Code is strictly LESS THAN the current page's first Transaction Type Code, AND if the Type Code filter is active, only records with an exact match on Transaction Type Code are included, AND if the Description filter is active, only records whose Description contains the filter text (partial match) are included, AND all qualifying records are ordered by Transaction Type Code in DESCENDING order

rules.rule_name: Fetch Each Record from Backward Cursor
rules.rule_description: Each record is fetched one at a time from the backward cursor, retrieving the Transaction Type Code and Description for placement into the display rows.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Fetch next record from backward cursor

acceptance_criteria.Given: The backward database cursor has been successfully opened and the row counter is positioned at the current fill position
acceptance_criteria.When: The system fetches the next record from the backward cursor
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction Type Code (TR_TYPE) and Transaction Type Description (TR_DESCRIPTION) are retrieved from the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table for the current record in the result set

rules.rule_name: Fill Current Row Position with Fetched Record Data
rules.rule_description: When a record is successfully fetched from the backward cursor, its Transaction Type Code and Description are stored into the current row position of the display area.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Fill current row position with fetched Type Code and Description

acceptance_criteria.Given: A record has been successfully fetched from the backward cursor (fetch returned a valid record)
acceptance_criteria.When: The fetched record data is placed into the display area
acceptance_criteria.Then: The fetched Transaction Type Code is stored in the current row position's Type Code output field, AND the fetched Transaction Type Description text is stored in the current row position's Description output field

rules.rule_name: Move Row Position Upward After Each Record Placed
rules.rule_description: After placing a fetched record into the current row position, the row counter is decremented by 1 to move the fill position one row upward, enabling the next fetched record to be placed in the row above.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Move to next row position upward - decrement row counter

acceptance_criteria.Given: A fetched record has been successfully placed into the current row position in the display area
acceptance_criteria.When: The system advances to the next row position
acceptance_criteria.Then: The row position counter is decremented by 1, moving the fill position one row upward toward row 1

rules.rule_name: Detect When All Display Rows Are Filled
rules.rule_description: After each record is placed and the row counter is decremented, the system checks whether all available display rows have been filled (row counter reaches zero), which signals that the page is complete.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: All 7 rows filled?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A record has been placed into a row position and the row counter has been decremented
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates whether the page is full
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the row counter equals zero, the page is considered full and the fetch loop is exited; if the row counter is greater than zero, the system continues fetching the next record to fill the next row upward

rules.rule_name: Save First Transaction Type Code of the New Page
rules.rule_description: When all 7 rows have been filled (row counter reaches zero), the Transaction Type Code of the last record placed (which is the topmost row on screen after display) is saved as the new first key of the page, enabling correct forward and backward navigation from this page.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Save this Type Code as the new First Key of the page

acceptance_criteria.Given: The row counter has reached zero, indicating all display rows have been filled with records fetched in descending order
acceptance_criteria.When: The system records the page boundary key
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction Type Code of the record just placed into row position 1 (the last record fetched that caused the counter to reach zero) is saved as the new First Transaction Type Code for the current page

rules.rule_name: Decrement Page Number When Navigating Backward
rules.rule_description: When the user navigates to the previous page using PF7 and the current page is not the first page, the page number displayed on screen is decremented by 1 to reflect the correct page position.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Decrement Page Number by 1

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF7 to navigate to the previous page AND the current page is NOT the first page
acceptance_criteria.When: The backward read operation is performed
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current page number is decremented by 1 before the backward read is executed, so the displayed page number correctly reflects the previous page

rules.rule_name: Handle No More Records Available During Backward Read
rules.rule_description: If the backward cursor returns no more records before all display rows are filled, the fetch loop is exited and the page is displayed with however many rows were successfully populated.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: No More Records

acceptance_criteria.Given: The backward cursor has been opened and the system is fetching records to fill the display rows
acceptance_criteria.When: The backward cursor returns no more records (end of result set reached before all rows are filled)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The fetch loop is immediately exited, and the page is displayed with only the rows that were successfully populated; any remaining row positions stay empty

rules.rule_name: Close Backward Cursor After Page Read Completes
rules.rule_description: After the backward fetch loop completes (either all rows filled or no more records), the backward database cursor must be closed to release database resources.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Close Backward Cursor

acceptance_criteria.Given: The backward fetch loop has completed, either because all display rows were filled or because no more records were available in the cursor
acceptance_criteria.When: The system finalizes the backward read operation
acceptance_criteria.Then: The backward database cursor (C-TR-TYPE-BACKWARD) is closed

rules.rule_name: Clear Row Selections When Navigating to Previous Page
rules.rule_description: When the user navigates to the previous page, all previously entered row action selections (Delete or Update flags) are cleared so that no prior selections carry over to the newly displayed page.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display the previous page with records now ordered correctly top to bottom

acceptance_criteria.Given: The backward read has completed and the previous page records have been loaded into the display area
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to display the previous page
acceptance_criteria.Then: All row selection flags for every display row are cleared (reset to blank/no action) before the page is sent to the screen, ensuring no action selections from the previous page view are retained

rules.rule_name: Display Previous Page Records in Ascending Type Code Order
rules.rule_description: Although records are fetched from the database in descending order and placed into the display area from bottom to top, the final display presents the records in ascending Transaction Type Code order from top to bottom, providing a consistent and intuitive view to the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display the previous page with records now ordered correctly top to bottom

acceptance_criteria.Given: Records have been fetched in descending Transaction Type Code order and placed into display rows from the bottom row upward (row 7 down to row 1)
acceptance_criteria.When: The completed page is sent to the screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: The records appear on screen in ascending Transaction Type Code order from top (row 1) to bottom (row 7), because the bottom-up fill of descending records naturally produces ascending top-to-bottom display order

rules.rule_name: Use Current Page First Key as Backward Read Boundary
rules.rule_description: The backward navigation uses the first Transaction Type Code currently displayed on screen as the exclusive upper boundary for the backward read, ensuring the previous page contains only records that precede the current page.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Open Backward Database Cursor - Read records with Type Code LESS THAN current first key on screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user presses PF7 to navigate to the previous page and the current page's first Transaction Type Code is stored as the start key
acceptance_criteria.When: The system sets up the backward cursor query
acceptance_criteria.Then: The backward cursor retrieves only records where the Transaction Type Code is strictly LESS THAN (not equal to) the current page's first Transaction Type Code, so the current page's records are excluded from the previous page results

key_functionalities.title: First Page Boundary Check
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([User Presses PF7\nBackward Page Request])
    B{Is the current page\nthe First Page?}
    C[Use the same first record key\nas the starting point]
    D[(CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE\nDB2 Table)]
    E[Re-read the same page of records\nstarting from the first record key]
    F[Set message:\n'No previous pages to display']
    G[Re-display the Transaction Type\nList screen with same records]
    H([Wait for Next\nUser Interaction])

    A --> B
    B -->|Yes - Already on First Page| C
    C --> E
    E --> D
    D -.->|Forward read from\nsame starting key| E
    E --> F
    F --> G
