rules.rule_name: Detect Backward Navigation Attempt on First Page
rules.rule_description: When a user requests to scroll backward (PF7) while already viewing the first page of Transaction Types, the system must detect this boundary condition and prevent any further backward navigation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is the current page the First Page?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is viewing the Transaction Type List screen and the current page is the first page of results (CA-FIRST-PAGE is TRUE)
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses PF7 (backward scroll key) to navigate to a previous page
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system identifies that the current page is the first page and no backward navigation is possible; the same first record key (WS-CA-FIRST-TR-CODE) is retained as the starting point for re-display, and no page number decrement occurs

rules.rule_name: Retain First Record Key as Starting Point on First Page Boundary
rules.rule_description: When backward navigation is blocked because the user is already on the first page, the system must use the stored first transaction type code of the current page as the starting key for re-reading, ensuring the same page content is displayed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Use the same first record key as the starting point

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the first page of the Transaction Type List and has pressed PF7, and the system has determined that no previous page exists
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to re-read the Transaction Type records for display
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the query start key (WS-START-KEY) to the first transaction type code stored for the current page (WS-CA-FIRST-TR-CODE), so that the same set of records will be retrieved from the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table

rules.rule_name: Re-Read Transaction Type Records from Same Starting Position
rules.rule_description: When the first page boundary is reached on a PF7 request, the system re-reads the Transaction Type records from the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table starting from the same first record key, applying any active filters, to refresh and re-display the current page content.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Re-read the same page of records starting from the first record key

acceptance_criteria.Given: The start key (WS-START-KEY) has been set to the first transaction type code of the current page (WS-CA-FIRST-TR-CODE), and the user is on the first page after pressing PF7
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes a forward read of the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table using cursor C-TR-TYPE-FORWARD, selecting TR_TYPE and TR_DESCRIPTION where TR_TYPE is greater than or equal to the start key, applying any active type code filter (exact match) and/or description filter (partial contains match), ordered by TR_TYPE ascending, up to the maximum number of screen lines
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system populates the screen rows with the retrieved transaction type records (TR_TYPE and TR_DESCRIPTION), sets the first and last transaction type codes for the page, and determines whether a next page exists by attempting to fetch one additional record beyond the page limit

rules.rule_name: Set Informational Message When No Previous Pages Exist
rules.rule_description: When the user attempts to scroll backward while already on the first page, the system must inform the user that there are no previous pages available by setting a specific boundary message for display on the screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set message: 'No previous pages to display'

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF7 and the system has determined that the current page is the first page (CA-FIRST-PAGE is TRUE)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the informational message for the screen during the message setup phase (2500-SETUP-MESSAGE)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the return message (WS-RETURN-MSG) to exactly 'No previous pages to display', which is then moved to the error message output field (ERRMSGO) on the Transaction Type List screen for the user to see

rules.rule_name: Re-Display Transaction Type List Screen with Same Page Content
rules.rule_description: After detecting the first page boundary on a PF7 request, re-reading the same records, and setting the boundary message, the system must send the fully prepared screen back to the user showing the same transaction type records along with the informational message.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Re-display the Transaction Type List screen with same records

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has re-read the same page of Transaction Type records from CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE, set the message 'No previous pages to display' in the error message field (ERRMSGO), initialized screen header fields (current date, current time, page number, program name, transaction ID), and set up all screen field attributes and row data
acceptance_criteria.When: The system sends the Transaction Type List screen (CTRTLIAO) to the user via CICS SEND MAP with ERASE and cursor positioning
acceptance_criteria.Then: The user sees the same Transaction Type List screen with the identical set of transaction type records (TR_TYPE and TR_DESCRIPTION) that were displayed before the PF7 key was pressed, along with the message 'No previous pages to display' in the message area, and the program returns control awaiting the next user interaction with the same transaction ID

rules.rule_name: Detect Delete Action on Enter Key Press
rules.rule_description: When the Enter key is pressed, the system checks whether at least one row on the current screen has a delete action selected. This determines whether the delete confirmation workflow should be initiated.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Enter Key Pressed → Delete Action Selected on a Row?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is viewing the Transaction Type list screen and has previously submitted the screen from the same program
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses the Enter key and at least one row has a Delete action flag (D) entered in its selection field
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system routes processing into the delete confirmation workflow, reading the current page of Transaction Type records starting from the first transaction code of the current page, and proceeds to re-display the screen with the selected row highlighted

rules.rule_name: Reject Multiple Simultaneous Row Actions
rules.rule_description: The system enforces that only one action (delete or update) can be selected across all displayed rows at the same time. If more than one row has an action selected, the submission is rejected with an error.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Exactly One Action Selected Across All Rows?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type list screen and has entered action codes in the row selection fields
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses Enter and more than one row has an action code (D or U) entered in the selection fields
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets an input error condition, sets the message flag to 'More Than 1 Action', marks each row that has a selection with an error indicator, highlights those selection fields in RED, and re-displays the screen with the error message — no delete confirmation prompt is shown

rules.rule_name: Reject Invalid Row Action Code
rules.rule_description: Each row selection field only accepts valid action codes (D for Delete, U for Update). Any other value entered is treated as an invalid action and triggers an error.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Exactly One Action Selected Across All Rows?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type list screen and has entered a value in a row selection field
acceptance_criteria.When: The value entered in a row selection field is not blank, not a Delete flag (D), and not an Update flag (U)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets an input error condition, marks that specific row's selection field with an error indicator, highlights the selection field in RED with cursor positioned on it, sets the message to 'Invalid Action Code', sets the bad-actions flag to YES, and re-displays the screen with the error — no delete confirmation prompt is shown

rules.rule_name: Re-Read Current Page Before Delete Confirmation Display
rules.rule_description: Before displaying the delete confirmation screen, the system re-reads the current page of Transaction Type records from the database to ensure the displayed data is current. The read uses the first transaction code of the current page as the starting key.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Read Current Page of Transaction Type Records from Database

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Enter key was pressed, exactly one delete action is selected, and no input errors exist on filters
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to display the delete confirmation screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the database read start key to the first transaction code of the current page (WS-CA-FIRST-TR-CODE), then reads forward through the TRANSACTION_TYPE table only if both the type code filter and the description filter are in a valid state (not flagged as invalid), populating the screen rows with current data

rules.rule_name: Highlight Selected Row for Delete Confirmation
rules.rule_description: When a single valid delete action is selected on a row, the system visually highlights that row by changing the transaction type code and description fields to a neutral color, drawing the user's attention to the record pending deletion.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Highlight Selected Row - Set Row Color to Neutral to Draw User Attention

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen is being prepared for delete confirmation display and exactly one valid delete action is selected with no bad action selections
acceptance_criteria.When: The system sets up screen attributes for the row that has the delete action selected
acceptance_criteria.Then: The transaction type code field color for that row is set to neutral (DFHNEUTR), the transaction description field color for that row is set to neutral (DFHNEUTR), and the cursor length for the selection field of that row is set to highlight it — making the pending-delete row visually distinct from other rows

rules.rule_name: Preserve Delete Pending State in Session
rules.rule_description: When a single valid delete action is selected and the delete has not yet been confirmed, the system preserves the delete-requested state in the session so that a subsequent PF10 key press can execute the actual deletion.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Mark Row as Pending Delete in Session State

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen is being populated with row data for delete confirmation and exactly one valid delete action is selected with no bad action selections
acceptance_criteria.When: The system processes the row that has the delete action selected and the deletion has not yet been completed
acceptance_criteria.Then: The session state flag CA-DELETE-REQUESTED is set to TRUE for that row, preserving the pending delete intent so that when the user subsequently presses PF10, the system knows a delete confirmation is expected for that transaction type

rules.rule_name: Display Delete Confirmation Prompt When Filters Are Unchanged
rules.rule_description: The delete confirmation prompt message is only displayed when the filter criteria (type code filter and description filter) have not changed since the last screen display. This ensures the user is confirming deletion of the correct record in the correct filter context.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Are Filter Criteria Unchanged Since Last Display? → Set Delete Confirmation Prompt Message

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Enter key was pressed, exactly one delete action is selected, exactly one total action is selected across all rows, and the screen is being prepared for display
acceptance_criteria.When: Both the type code filter value and the description filter value are unchanged from the previous screen submission (FLG-TYPEFILTER-CHANGED-NO is TRUE and FLG-DESCFILTER-CHANGED-NO is TRUE) and no informational message has already been set
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the informational message flag to WS-INFORM-DELETE, which triggers the display of the delete confirmation prompt message (e.g., 'Press PF10 to Confirm Deletion') centered on the screen — prompting the user to press PF10 to proceed with the deletion

rules.rule_name: Suppress Delete Confirmation Prompt When Filters Have Changed
rules.rule_description: If the user has changed either the type code filter or the description filter at the same time as selecting a delete action, the delete confirmation prompt is suppressed. The screen is re-displayed with the new filter results but without a confirmation prompt.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Are Filter Criteria Unchanged Since Last Display? → Re-display Screen without Confirmation Prompt

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Enter key was pressed and a delete action is selected on a row
acceptance_criteria.When: Either the type code filter value has changed from the previous submission (FLG-TYPEFILTER-CHANGED-YES is TRUE) or the description filter value has changed from the previous submission (FLG-DESCFILTER-CHANGED-YES is TRUE)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system does NOT set the delete confirmation prompt message (WS-INFORM-DELETE is not set), all row selections are cleared (WS-EDIT-SELECT-FLAGS is initialized), and the screen is re-displayed showing the updated filter results without any delete confirmation prompt

rules.rule_name: Send Updated Screen with Highlighted Row and Confirmation Prompt
rules.rule_description: After preparing all screen attributes, row data, and messages, the system sends the fully composed screen to the user. The screen includes the current page of transaction type records, the highlighted pending-delete row, and (when applicable) the delete confirmation prompt.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Send Updated Screen to User with: Highlighted Selected Row, Confirmation Prompt, Current Page Data

acceptance_criteria.Given: All screen initialization, row attribute setup, row data population, screen field attributes, and message setup have been completed for the delete confirmation scenario
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the send-map sequence (2000-SEND-MAP) which includes screen initialization, array attribute setup, screen array data population, screen field attribute setup, and message setup
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sends the composed screen map to the user terminal with: the current date and time displayed, the current page number displayed, all transaction type rows populated with their codes and descriptions, the selected delete-pending row highlighted in neutral color, the confirmation prompt message centered on the screen (if filters are unchanged), and the keyboard unlocked awaiting the user's next input (PF10 to confirm or another key to cancel)

key_functionalities.title: Delete Record Execution
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([PF10 Pressed to\nConfirm Deletion])
    B[Retrieve Type Code\nof Selected Row]
    C[(CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE\nDB2 Table)]
    D[Execute DELETE\nWHERE TR_TYPE = Selected Type Code]
    E{Deletion\nOutcome?}
    F[Commit Transaction\nSet Delete Succeeded Flag]
    G[23: Display Success Message\nReset Session State\nReturn to First Page of List]
    H[24: Child Records Exist\nCannot Delete\nInform User to Delete\nAssociated Child Records First]
    I[Deletion Failed\nDisplay Error Message\nKeep Delete Pending State]
    B --> C
    A --> B
    C -.->|DELETE Statement| D
    D --> E
    E -->|Success| F
    E -->|Child Records\nAssociated - Error -532| H
    E -->|Other Failure| I
    F --> G
    H --> I

rules.rule_name: Retrieve Type Code of Selected Row Before Deletion
rules.rule_description: Before executing a delete operation, the system must identify and retrieve the Transaction Type Code of the row the user has selected for deletion, so that the correct record is targeted in the database.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Retrieve Type Code of Selected Row

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF10 to confirm deletion and a valid row with a Transaction Type Code has been selected on the screen (identified by the selected row index I-SELECTED)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to execute the delete operation
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction Type Code (TR_TYPE) from the selected screen row is retrieved and set as the key value to be used in the DELETE statement targeting the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table

rules.rule_name: Execute Delete of Transaction Type Record from Database
rules.rule_description: The system executes a DELETE operation against the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table using the Transaction Type Code of the selected row as the exact match key, permanently removing that transaction type record.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Execute DELETE WHERE TR_TYPE = Selected Type Code

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Code of the selected row has been retrieved and the system is ready to perform the deletion
acceptance_criteria.When: The DELETE statement is executed against the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table with the condition WHERE TR_TYPE equals the selected Transaction Type Code
acceptance_criteria.Then: The matching transaction type record is deleted from the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table and the outcome (success, child record constraint violation, or other failure) is captured for subsequent processing

rules.rule_name: Commit Transaction and Confirm Successful Deletion
rules.rule_description: When the DELETE operation completes successfully, the system must immediately commit the database change to make it permanent and record that the deletion succeeded so that downstream processing can display a success message and reset the screen state.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Commit Transaction Set Delete Succeeded Flag

acceptance_criteria.Given: The DELETE statement executed against CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE completed without any errors (SQL return code equals zero)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the outcome of the DELETE operation
acceptance_criteria.Then: The database transaction is committed immediately (SYNCPOINT) to permanently save the deletion, the Delete Succeeded flag is set to TRUE, and a delete success informational message is queued for display to the user

rules.rule_name: Prevent Deletion When Associated Child Records Exist
rules.rule_description: A Transaction Type record cannot be deleted if other records in the system reference it as a foreign key (child records). The system must detect this constraint violation and inform the user that they must first remove all associated child records before the transaction type can be deleted.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Child Records Exist Cannot Delete Inform User to Delete Associated Child Records First

acceptance_criteria.Given: The DELETE statement was executed against CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE for the selected Transaction Type Code
acceptance_criteria.When: The deletion fails because one or more child records in the database are associated with (reference) this Transaction Type Code, resulting in a referential integrity constraint violation (equivalent to SQL error -532)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The deletion is not performed, the Delete Requested state is preserved (kept as pending, not succeeded), and the user is presented with the error message: 'Please delete associated child records first' — the user must delete all associated child records before this Transaction Type can be deleted

rules.rule_name: Handle General Deletion Failure
rules.rule_description: When the DELETE operation fails for any reason other than a child record constraint violation, the system must inform the user of the failure and preserve the delete-pending state so the user can retry or take corrective action.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Deletion Failed Display Error Message Keep Delete Pending State

acceptance_criteria.Given: The DELETE statement was executed against CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE for the selected Transaction Type Code
acceptance_criteria.When: The deletion fails for any reason other than a child record constraint violation (i.e., any error condition that is not a referential integrity violation)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The deletion is not performed, the error details are captured and formatted into a message beginning with 'Delete failed with message:' followed by the specific error information, the error message is displayed to the user, and the delete-pending state is preserved so the user is aware the deletion did not complete

rules.rule_name: Display Success Message and Reset Session to First Page After Deletion
rules.rule_description: After a transaction type record is successfully deleted, the system must display a confirmation message to the user, reset all session state (filters, selections, page position), and return the user to the first page of the transaction type list so they see a refreshed, accurate view of remaining records.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Success Message Reset Session State Return to First Page of List

acceptance_criteria.Given: The DELETE operation completed successfully, the transaction was committed, and the Delete Succeeded flag is set to TRUE
acceptance_criteria.When: The system processes the post-deletion screen update
acceptance_criteria.Then: A delete success message is displayed on the screen; then all session state is fully reset — including the communication area, program communication area, and miscellaneous storage — the program is set to Enter mode, the display is repositioned to the first page, and the last-page-shown indicator is reset to 'not shown', effectively returning the user to a fresh first-page view of the remaining transaction type records

key_functionalities.title: Delete Success Handling
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Delete Execution Completed]) --> B{Was Deletion\nSuccessful?}
    B -->|Yes| C[Mark Deletion as Successful]
    B -->|No| Z([End - Handle Failure])
    C --> D[Clear the Action Selection\nfor the Deleted Row on Screen]
    D --> E[Set Success Message:\nDelete completed successfully]
    E --> F[Send Updated Screen\nto User with Success Message]
    F --> G[Reset All Session Data\nto Initial State]
    G --> H[Reset Page Position\nto First Page]
    H --> I[Mark Last Page\nas Not Yet Shown]
    I --> J([End - User Sees Success Message\nand Returns to First Page of List])

rules.rule_name: Determine Delete Operation Outcome
rules.rule_description: After executing a delete operation on a Transaction Type record, the system evaluates whether the deletion was completed successfully and routes to the appropriate success or failure handling path.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Was Deletion Successful?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A delete operation has been executed against the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table for the selected Transaction Type Code (TR_TYPE)
acceptance_criteria.When: The delete operation completes and the system evaluates the result
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the deletion completed without error, the system marks the deletion as succeeded and proceeds to success handling; if the deletion failed (due to child records existing or any other failure), the system routes to failure handling without marking success

rules.rule_name: Mark Deletion as Successful and Commit Transaction
rules.rule_description: When a Transaction Type record is successfully deleted from the database, the system commits the change permanently and sets the internal state to reflect that the deletion succeeded.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Mark Deletion as Successful

acceptance_criteria.Given: A delete operation has been executed on the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table for the selected Transaction Type Code (TR_TYPE) and the deletion completed without any errors
acceptance_criteria.When: The system confirms the deletion was successful (no database errors returned)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system immediately commits the deletion to the database (making it permanent and visible to all users), sets the deletion status to 'succeeded', and sets an informational flag to display a delete success message to the user

rules.rule_name: Clear Action Selection for Deleted Row on Screen
rules.rule_description: After a successful deletion, the selection field of the row that was deleted is cleared on the screen so that the deleted record no longer appears as having a pending action.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Clear the Action Selection for the Deleted Row on Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: A Transaction Type record has been successfully deleted and the screen is being prepared for display
acceptance_criteria.When: The system processes the row that had the delete action selected and the deletion flag is marked as successful
acceptance_criteria.Then: The selection field for that specific row is blanked out (cleared), removing the delete action indicator from the display so the row no longer shows a pending delete selection

rules.rule_name: Display Delete Success Message to User
rules.rule_description: After a successful deletion of a Transaction Type record, the system sets and displays a success confirmation message to inform the user that the delete operation completed successfully.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Success Message: Delete completed successfully

acceptance_criteria.Given: A Transaction Type record has been successfully deleted and the screen message area is being prepared
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the deletion outcome flag and finds the deletion was successful (FLG-DELETED-YES is true)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the informational message to the delete success message and displays it on the screen in the message area, confirming to the user that the deletion was completed

rules.rule_name: Send Updated Screen with Success Message After Deletion
rules.rule_description: After a successful deletion, the system sends the refreshed screen to the user displaying the success message and the updated list with the deleted row's selection cleared.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Send Updated Screen to User with Success Message

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen has been prepared with the delete success message and the deleted row's selection has been cleared
acceptance_criteria.When: The system is ready to present the result of the delete operation to the user
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sends the fully prepared screen map to the user's terminal, displaying the success message and the updated transaction type list with the deleted row's action selection removed

rules.rule_name: Reset All Session Data to Initial State After Successful Deletion
rules.rule_description: After a successful deletion and the success screen has been sent, the system resets all session-level data including filters, selections, paging state, and program communication areas back to their initial values to prepare for a fresh start.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Reset All Session Data to Initial State

acceptance_criteria.Given: A Transaction Type record has been successfully deleted and the success screen has been sent to the user
acceptance_criteria.When: The system processes the post-deletion cleanup after confirming the deletion flag is marked as successful
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system clears all session data by reinitializing: the main communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA), the program-specific communication area (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA), and all miscellaneous working storage (WS-MISC-STORAGE), effectively removing all filter values, row selections, paging keys, and any other session state accumulated during the current session

rules.rule_name: Reset Page Position to First Page After Successful Deletion
rules.rule_description: After a successful deletion and session reset, the system sets the page navigation state so that the next screen display will start from the very first page of the Transaction Type list.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Reset Page Position to First Page

acceptance_criteria.Given: All session data has been reset following a successful deletion of a Transaction Type record
acceptance_criteria.When: The system sets the navigation state for the next program entry
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the program entry mode to 'entering' (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER) and sets the page position indicator to 'first page' (CA-FIRST-PAGE), ensuring the next display will begin from the first record in the Transaction Type list

rules.rule_name: Mark Last Page as Not Yet Shown After Deletion Reset
rules.rule_description: As part of the post-deletion reset, the system marks that the last page of the Transaction Type list has not yet been reached or shown, resetting the end-of-list tracking for the fresh navigation session.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Mark Last Page as Not Yet Shown

acceptance_criteria.Given: The page position has been reset to the first page following a successful deletion of a Transaction Type record
acceptance_criteria.When: The system completes the full post-deletion state reset
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the last-page indicator to 'not yet shown' (CA-LAST-PAGE-NOT-SHOWN), ensuring that end-of-list messages such as 'No more pages to display' will not appear prematurely when the user begins navigating the refreshed Transaction Type list

rules.rule_name: Attempt to Delete Transaction Type Record
rules.rule_description: When a user confirms deletion by pressing PF10, the system attempts to permanently remove the selected transaction type record from the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table using the transaction type code of the selected row.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Attempt to Delete Transaction Type Record from Database

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has selected a transaction type row with action code 'D' (Delete) on the Transaction Type List screen, and the user has pressed PF10 to confirm the deletion
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes a DELETE operation against the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table targeting the record whose TR_TYPE matches the transaction type code of the selected row
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system evaluates the outcome of the delete operation to determine whether it succeeded, failed due to associated child records, or failed for another reason, and routes processing accordingly

rules.rule_name: Detect Referential Integrity Violation on Delete - Child Records Exist
rules.rule_description: When a deletion attempt fails because the transaction type is still referenced by associated child records (referential integrity constraint), the system must detect this specific condition and prevent the deletion from proceeding.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Child Records Exist Referential Integrity Violation

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has pressed PF10 to confirm deletion of a selected transaction type record, and the DELETE operation has been executed against the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table
acceptance_criteria.When: The deletion fails because the transaction type code is still referenced by one or more associated child records in the database (referential integrity violation)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system marks the delete action as still pending (CA-DELETE-REQUESTED remains active), indicating the deletion was not completed and the user must take further action before the record can be deleted

rules.rule_name: Prepare Error Message for Child Records Constraint Violation
rules.rule_description: When a transaction type cannot be deleted because associated child records exist, the system must prepare a specific, user-friendly error message instructing the user to remove the child records first before retrying the deletion.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Prepare Error Message: 'Please delete associated child records first'

acceptance_criteria.Given: The deletion of a transaction type has failed due to a referential integrity violation (child records are associated with the transaction type), and no prior error message has already been set for this transaction
acceptance_criteria.When: The system processes the referential integrity violation outcome
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error message context to 'Please delete associated child records first:' and formats a complete error message combining this context with the database error details, which is stored in the return message field for display to the user

rules.rule_name: Preserve Selected Row Highlight After Delete Failure
rules.rule_description: After a failed deletion due to child records, the selected transaction type row must remain visually highlighted on the screen with the delete action still indicated, so the user can clearly see which record still needs attention.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Re-display Transaction Type List Screen with Selected Row Still Highlighted

acceptance_criteria.Given: A deletion attempt has failed because child records exist, and the delete action is still marked as pending (CA-DELETE-REQUESTED is active) for the selected row
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the Transaction Type List screen for redisplay by populating each row's display data
acceptance_criteria.Then: The selected row retains its delete-requested state (the row is NOT cleared/blanked), the transaction type code and description for that row are displayed in neutral highlight color to indicate the pending delete action, and the selection field remains visible — so the user can clearly identify which record still requires child record removal

rules.rule_name: Redisplay Transaction Type List Screen with Child Records Error Message
rules.rule_description: After a failed deletion due to child records, the system must redisplay the full Transaction Type List screen including the error message, so the user is informed of the reason for failure and can take corrective action.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Show Error Message Informing User to Remove Child Records First

acceptance_criteria.Given: The deletion of a transaction type has failed due to associated child records, the delete action is still marked as pending, and the error message 'Please delete associated child records first:' has been prepared
acceptance_criteria.When: The system sends the Transaction Type List screen back to the user
acceptance_criteria.Then: The screen is redisplayed with: (1) the selected transaction type row still highlighted showing the pending delete action, (2) the error message 'Please delete associated child records first:' visible on the screen, (3) the delete outcome flag set to 'not deleted' (FLG-DELETED-NO), and (4) the screen reflects that the deletion did NOT succeed — the record remains in the database and the user must first delete all associated child records before the transaction type can be removed

rules.rule_name: Block Transaction Type Deletion When Associated Child Records Exist
rules.rule_description: A transaction type record cannot be deleted from the system as long as other records in the database reference it. This is a data integrity policy that protects against orphaned child records.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: User Must Delete Associated Child Records Before Retrying

acceptance_criteria.Given: A transaction type record exists in the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table and one or more other records in the database reference this transaction type (child records exist)
acceptance_criteria.When: A user attempts to delete the transaction type by selecting it with action code 'D' and confirming with PF10
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system blocks the deletion, does not remove the transaction type record from the database, keeps the delete action as pending on the screen, displays the message 'Please delete associated child records first:', and requires the user to first delete all associated child records before the transaction type deletion can be successfully retried

key_functionalities.title: Update Confirmation Request
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Enter Key Pressed\nwith Update Action Selected])
    B{Is exactly one\nUpdate action selected\nand no bad selections?}
    C[Read current page of Transaction Type\nrecords from database\nusing existing filter and start key]
    D{Are current\nfilter conditions\nvalid?}
    E[Skip database read\ndue to invalid filters]
    F[Mark the selected row\nas Update Requested\nfor screen display]
    G[Highlight selected row\nin neutral color]
    H[Set description field\non selected row as editable\nso user can modify it]
    I[Display current description\nvalue in the editable field]
    J[Display prompt message\nto user: Press PF10 to\nconfirm the update]

    A --> B
    B -->|Yes - One valid update| D

rules.rule_name: Trigger Update Confirmation Flow on Enter Key with Update Action
rules.rule_description: When the user presses the Enter key and at least one Update action has been selected on the Transaction Type maintenance screen, the system initiates the update confirmation flow by re-reading the current page and re-displaying the screen for user confirmation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Enter Key Pressed with Update Action Selected

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type maintenance screen and has previously selected the Update action (U) on one or more rows
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses the Enter key and the screen was submitted from the Transaction Type maintenance program itself (same program re-entry) and at least one Update action is recorded as requested
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the start key to the first transaction code of the current page, re-reads the current page of transaction type records from the database applying existing filters, and re-displays the screen to prompt the user for confirmation

rules.rule_name: Validate Single Update Action Before Confirmation Display
rules.rule_description: The system verifies that exactly one valid Update action is selected across all rows and that no invalid selection codes exist before proceeding to highlight the selected row and prompt for PF10 confirmation. If multiple actions or invalid selections exist, the confirmation display is bypassed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is exactly one Update action selected and no bad selections?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has entered action codes in the row selection fields on the Transaction Type maintenance screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the row selections after Enter is pressed with updates requested
acceptance_criteria.Then: If exactly one action is selected (WS-ONLY-1-ACTION), exactly one valid action exists (WS-ONLY-1-VALID-ACTION), and no bad/invalid action codes are present (FLG-BAD-ACTIONS-SELECTED-NO), then the system proceeds to highlight the selected row and enable the description field for editing; otherwise the confirmation display steps are skipped and the screen is re-displayed without the update confirmation prompts

rules.rule_name: Conditionally Read Current Page Based on Filter Validity
rules.rule_description: Before re-displaying the screen for update confirmation, the system checks whether the current filter conditions (type code filter and description filter) are valid. If both filters are valid, the system reads the current page of transaction type records from the database. If either filter is invalid, the database read is skipped.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Are current filter conditions valid?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The update confirmation flow has been triggered by the user pressing Enter with an update action selected
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the validity of the current type code filter and description filter
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the type code filter is NOT in an invalid state (NOT FLG-TYPEFILTER-NOT-OK) AND the description filter is NOT in an invalid state (NOT FLG-DESCFILTER-NOT-OK), the system performs a forward database read (8000-READ-FORWARD) using the current start key and active filters; if either filter is invalid, the database read is skipped entirely and the screen is re-displayed with existing data

rules.rule_name: Read Current Page of Transaction Type Records for Update Confirmation
rules.rule_description: The system reads the current page of Transaction Type records from the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table using the existing start key and any active filter conditions, to populate the screen before re-displaying it for update confirmation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Read current page of Transaction Type records from database using existing filter and start key

acceptance_criteria.Given: Both the type code filter and description filter are in a valid state
acceptance_criteria.When: The system performs a forward read of Transaction Type records
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system opens the forward cursor (C-TR-TYPE-FORWARD) and fetches records from CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE where TR_TYPE is greater than or equal to the current start key (WS-START-KEY), applying the type code filter as an exact match on TR_TYPE if the type filter flag is active, and applying the description filter as a LIKE (contains) match on TR_DESCRIPTION if the description filter flag is active, ordering results by TR_TYPE ascending, filling up to the maximum number of screen rows, and storing the first and last transaction codes of the page for paging navigation

rules.rule_name: Mark Selected Row as Update Requested for Screen Display
rules.rule_description: When exactly one valid Update action is selected and the update has not yet been completed, the system marks the communication area state as 'Update Requested' so the screen correctly reflects the pending update action on the selected row.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Mark the selected row as Update Requested for screen display

acceptance_criteria.Given: A row on the Transaction Type maintenance screen has the Update action (U) selected, exactly one valid action is selected, and no bad selections exist
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the screen array data for display during the update confirmation flow
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the update has NOT already been completed (NOT FLG-UPDATE-COMPLETED), the system sets the communication area flag to 'Update Requested' (CA-UPDATE-REQUESTED = TRUE) for the selected row, preserving the update intent for the next user interaction; if the update has already been completed, the selection field for that row is cleared (SELECT-BLANK)

rules.rule_name: Highlight Selected Row in Neutral Color for Update Confirmation
rules.rule_description: When an Update action is selected on a row and the update is pending confirmation, the system highlights the transaction type code field of the selected row in neutral color to visually indicate that the row is the target of the pending update action.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Highlight selected row in neutral color

acceptance_criteria.Given: A row has the Update action selected, exactly one valid action is selected, and no bad selections exist
acceptance_criteria.When: The system sets up the screen field attributes for display
acceptance_criteria.Then: The transaction type code field (TRTTYPC) for the selected row is set to neutral color (DFHNEUTR), visually distinguishing the selected row from other rows on the screen

rules.rule_name: Enable Description Field for Editing on Selected Update Row
rules.rule_description: When an Update action is pending confirmation (not yet confirmed with PF10), the system makes the description field of the selected row editable so the user can modify the transaction description before confirming the update.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set description field on selected row as editable so user can modify it

acceptance_criteria.Given: A row has the Update action selected, exactly one valid action is selected, no bad selections exist, and the update has NOT yet been completed
acceptance_criteria.When: The system sets up the screen field attributes for the selected row
acceptance_criteria.Then: The description field attribute (TRTYPDA) for the selected row is set to unprotected/editable (DFHBMFSE), the cursor length for the description field (TRTYPDL) is set to -1 to position the cursor there, allowing the user to modify the transaction description; if the description field has a validation error, it is additionally highlighted in RED (DFHRED)

rules.rule_name: Display Current Description Value in Editable Field
rules.rule_description: The system populates the editable description field of the selected update row with the appropriate description value — either the newly entered value, an asterisk placeholder if the new value is blank, or the original stored description if no changes have been made.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display current description value in the editable field

acceptance_criteria.Given: A row has the Update action selected, exactly one valid action is selected, no bad selections exist, and the update has NOT yet been completed
acceptance_criteria.When: The system populates the screen array data for the selected row
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the user has made changes to the description (CHANGES-HAVE-OCCURRED): if the new description is blank (FLG-ROW-DESCRIPTION-BLANK), display an asterisk (*) in the description field (TRTYPDO); otherwise display the newly entered description value (WS-ROW-TR-DESC-IN(I)); if no changes have been made (NO-CHANGES-FOUND), display the original stored description from the communication area (WS-CA-ROW-TR-DESC-OUT(I))

rules.rule_name: Display Update Confirmation Prompt Message to User
rules.rule_description: When the user has selected exactly one valid Update action and pressed Enter, and the filters have not changed, the system displays an informational prompt message instructing the user to press PF10 to confirm and save the update.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display prompt message to user: Press PF10 to confirm the update

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has pressed Enter with exactly one Update action selected (WS-UPDATES-REQUESTED > 0), exactly one total action is selected (WS-ONLY-1-ACTION), exactly one valid action is selected (WS-ONLY-1-VALID-ACTION), no informational message is already set (WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE), the type code filter has not changed (FLG-TYPEFILTER-CHANGED-NO), and the description filter has not changed (FLG-DESCFILTER-CHANGED-NO)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the informational message for screen display
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the update confirmation prompt flag (WS-INFORM-UPDATE = TRUE), which causes an informational message to be displayed on the screen instructing the user to press PF10 to confirm the update action

rules.rule_name: Protect All Other Rows from Selection Changes During Update Confirmation
rules.rule_description: While an update action is pending confirmation, rows that have no data or are in a protected state have their selection fields locked so the user cannot select additional rows or change selections on other rows during the confirmation step.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Protect all other rows from selection changes

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen is being prepared for display during the update confirmation flow
acceptance_criteria.When: The system sets up the screen field attributes for each row in the display array
acceptance_criteria.Then: For each row where the row data is empty (WS-CA-EACH-ROW-OUT(I) equals LOW-VALUES) OR the row selection protection flag is active (FLG-PROTECT-SELECT-ROWS-YES), the selection field attribute (TRTSELA) is set to protected/read-only (DFHBMPRO), preventing the user from entering a selection code on those rows; rows with data and no protection flag have their selection fields set to unprotected/editable (DFHBMFSE)

rules.rule_name: Display Filter Fields in Blue to Indicate Pending Action
rules.rule_description: When one or more row actions are requested (an update or delete is pending), the system displays the type code filter and description filter fields in blue color and sets them as auto-skip fields, visually communicating to the user that an action is in progress and the filters are not the current focus.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display filter values in blue to indicate an action is pending

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen is being prepared for display and at least one row action has been requested (WS-ACTIONS-REQUESTED > 0)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system sets up the screen field attributes for the filter input fields
acceptance_criteria.Then: The type code filter field (TRTYPEO) is populated with the current type code input value (WS-IN-TYPE-CD), its color attribute (TRTYPEC) is set to blue (DFHBLUE), and its field attribute (TRTYPEA) is set to auto-skip (DFHBMASF); similarly, the description filter field (TRDESCO) is populated with the current description input value (WS-IN-TYPE-DESC), its color attribute (TRDESCC) is set to blue (DFHBLUE), and its field attribute (TRDESCA) is set to auto-skip (DFHBMASF)

key_functionalities.title: Update Record Execution
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    START([PF10 Pressed with\nUpdate Requested])
    PREPDATA[Prepare Update Data\nGet selected row's Type Code\nand new Description entered by user]
    EXECUPDATE[Execute Update\nUpdate TR_DESCRIPTION in\nCARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE\nWHERE TR_TYPE = selected type code]
    TRTYPE_UPD[(CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE\nDB2 Table)]
    SQLRESULT{Update\nResult?}
    SUCCESS[Update Succeeded\nCommit transaction\nMark update as completed]
    NOTFOUND[Record Not Found\nRecord may have been\ndeleted by another user\nKeep update pending]
    DEADLOCK[Deadlock Detected\nAnother user may be\nupdating the same record\nKeep update pending]
    OTHERFAIL[Update Failed\nUnexpected error occurred\nKeep update pending]
    REFRESHLIST[Refresh Transaction Type List\nRead current page of records\nfrom database]
    TRTYPE_READ[(CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE\nDB2 Table)]
    SENDSCREEN[Display Updated Screen\nShow updated list with\nsuccess or error message]
    END([Return - Wait for\nNext User Interaction])

    START --> PREPDATA
    PREPDATA --> EXECUPDATE
    EXECUPDATE --> TRTYPE_UPD
    TRTYPE_UPD -.->|SQL Result| SQLRESULT
    SQLRESULT -->|Success| SUCCESS
    SQLRESULT -->|Record Not Found| NOTFOUND
    SQLRESULT -->|Deadlock| DEADLOCK
    SQLRESULT -->|Other Failure| OTHERFAIL
    SUCCESS --> REFRESHLIST
    NOTFOUND --> REFRESHLIST
    DEADLOCK --> REFRESHLIST
    OTHERFAIL --> REFRESHLIST
    REFRESHLIST --> TRTYPE_READ
    TRTYPE_READ -.->|Fetch current page records| SENDSCREEN
    SENDSCREEN --> END

rules.rule_name: Prepare Update Data from Selected Row
rules.rule_description: Before executing the database update, the system retrieves the Transaction Type Code and the new Description value entered by the user from the selected row on the screen to prepare the update payload.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Prepare Update Data
Get selected row's Type Code
and new Description entered by user

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has selected a row with action 'U' (Update) and entered a new description value, and PF10 has been pressed to confirm the update
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the data for the update operation
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system retrieves the Transaction Type Code (TR_TYPE) from the selected row's input field (WS-ROW-TR-CODE-IN for the selected row index), trims and stores the new Description text (up to 50 characters) entered by the user from WS-ROW-TR-DESC-IN for the selected row index, and computes the length of the new description to be stored alongside the description text

rules.rule_name: Execute Description Update on Transaction Type Record
rules.rule_description: The system updates only the description field of the matching Transaction Type record in the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table using the Transaction Type Code as the unique identifier. The Transaction Type Code itself is never modified.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Execute Update
Update TR_DESCRIPTION in
CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE
WHERE TR_TYPE = selected type code

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Code and new Description have been prepared from the selected row
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the update against the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE database table
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system updates the TR_DESCRIPTION column to the new description value for the record where TR_TYPE exactly matches the selected Transaction Type Code; no other fields or records are modified

rules.rule_name: Commit Transaction on Successful Update
rules.rule_description: When the database update completes successfully, the system commits the change permanently to the database and marks the update as completed so the screen can reflect the success state.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Update Succeeded
Commit transaction
Mark update as completed

acceptance_criteria.Given: The update of TR_DESCRIPTION in CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE has been executed
acceptance_criteria.When: The database confirms the update was successful (no errors returned)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system immediately commits the transaction to make the change permanent, marks the update status as 'succeeded' (CA-UPDATE-SUCCEEDED), sets the update-completed flag (FLG-UPDATE-COMPLETED) to TRUE so the screen reflects completion, and sets an informational success message (WS-INFORM-UPDATE-SUCCESS) if no other informational message is already set

rules.rule_name: Handle Record Not Found During Update
rules.rule_description: If the Transaction Type record no longer exists at the time of the update attempt, the system informs the user that the record may have been deleted by another user and keeps the update in a pending state.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Record Not Found
Record may have been
deleted by another user
Keep update pending

acceptance_criteria.Given: The update of TR_DESCRIPTION in CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE has been executed
acceptance_criteria.When: The database returns a 'record not found' result (no rows were updated)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system keeps the update action in a pending/requested state (CA-UPDATE-REQUESTED remains active), displays the message 'Record not found. Deleted by others ?' to inform the user that the record may have been removed by another user, and does not commit any changes

rules.rule_name: Handle Deadlock During Update
rules.rule_description: If a deadlock is detected during the update attempt, indicating another user may be simultaneously updating the same record, the system treats this as an input error, informs the user, and keeps the update in a pending state.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Deadlock Detected
Another user may be
updating the same record
Keep update pending

acceptance_criteria.Given: The update of TR_DESCRIPTION in CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE has been executed
acceptance_criteria.When: The database returns a deadlock error (resource contention with another user's transaction)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system marks the overall input as an error (INPUT-ERROR), keeps the update action in a pending/requested state (CA-UPDATE-REQUESTED remains active), and displays the message 'Deadlock. Someone else updating ?' to inform the user that another user may be updating the same record; no changes are committed

rules.rule_name: Handle Unexpected Update Failure
rules.rule_description: If the update fails due to any unexpected database error other than record-not-found or deadlock, the system informs the user of the failure and keeps the update in a pending state without committing any changes.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Update Failed
Unexpected error occurred
Keep update pending

acceptance_criteria.Given: The update of TR_DESCRIPTION in CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE has been executed
acceptance_criteria.When: The database returns any negative error code that is not a deadlock error (i.e., any database failure other than record-not-found or deadlock)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system keeps the update action in a pending/requested state (CA-UPDATE-REQUESTED remains active), displays the message 'Update failed with' along with the database error details to inform the user of the unexpected failure, and does not commit any changes

rules.rule_name: Refresh Transaction Type List After Update Attempt
rules.rule_description: Regardless of whether the update succeeded or failed, the system always refreshes the displayed list of Transaction Types by re-reading the current page of records from the database, ensuring the screen reflects the latest data.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Refresh Transaction Type List
Read current page of records
from database

acceptance_criteria.Given: The update operation on CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE has completed with any result (success, not found, deadlock, or other failure)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system proceeds to refresh the screen after the update attempt
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system always re-reads the current page of Transaction Type records from the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table starting from the first Transaction Type Code of the current page (WS-CA-FIRST-TR-CODE used as the start key WS-START-KEY), applying any active filters, and populates the screen rows with the latest data from the database

rules.rule_name: Display Updated Screen with Outcome Message
rules.rule_description: After refreshing the data, the system sends the updated screen to the user showing the current list of Transaction Types along with an appropriate success or error message reflecting the outcome of the update operation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Display Updated Screen
Show updated list with
success or error message

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type list has been refreshed from the database after the update attempt
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares and sends the screen to the user
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system displays the refreshed Transaction Type list on screen; if the update succeeded, a success message (WS-INFORM-UPDATE-SUCCESS) is shown and the selection field for the updated row is cleared; if the update failed (record not found, deadlock, or other error), the corresponding error message is displayed and the row remains in its update-pending state with the description field still editable; the screen is sent with cursor positioning and keyboard unlocked

sub_functionalities.title: Execute Update
sub_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    START([26.1: Execute Update])
    PREPARE[Prepare selected row data\nGet Type Code from selected row\nGet updated Description from selected row]
    DBUPDATE[Run Database Update\nUpdate Description for the\nmatching Transaction Type Code\nin CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE]
    OUTCOME{What was the\nUpdate Outcome?}
    SUCCESS[Commit the Update\nMark Update as Succeeded\nPrepare Update Success Message]
    NOTFOUND[Mark Update as Still Pending\nRecord no longer exists -\npossibly deleted by another user]
    DEADLOCK[Mark Update as Still Pending\nMark Input as Error\nAnother user may be\nupdating the same record]
    OTHERFAIL[Mark Update as Still Pending\nPrepare failure details\nfor error message]
    END_SUCCESS([Proceed to\nRefresh List Screen])
    END_FAIL([Proceed to\nRe-display Screen\nwith Error Message])

    START --> PREPARE
    PREPARE --> DBUPDATE
    DBUPDATE --> OUTCOME
    OUTCOME -->|Update Successful| SUCCESS
    OUTCOME -->|Record Not Found| NOTFOUND
    OUTCOME -->|Deadlock Detected| DEADLOCK
    OUTCOME -->|Other Failure| OTHERFAIL
    SUCCESS --> END_SUCCESS
    NOTFOUND --> END_FAIL
    DEADLOCK --> END_FAIL
    OTHERFAIL --> END_FAIL

rules.rule_name: Prepare Transaction Type Data for Update
rules.rule_description: Before executing the database update, the system retrieves the Transaction Type Code and the new Description entered by the user from the selected screen row, and calculates the length of the new description to pass to the database.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Prepare selected row data
Get Type Code from selected row
Get updated Description from selected row

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has selected a row with action 'U' (Update) on the Transaction Type maintenance screen, and the selected row index (I-SELECTED) identifies the specific row
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares data for the database update operation
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction Type Code (TR_TYPE) is taken from the selected row's type code input field (WS-ROW-TR-CODE-IN at position I-SELECTED); the new Transaction Description is taken from the selected row's description input field (WS-ROW-TR-DESC-IN at position I-SELECTED) with leading and trailing spaces trimmed; and the description length is computed as the full field length of the description input

rules.rule_name: Execute Database Update for Transaction Type Description
rules.rule_description: The system updates the TR_DESCRIPTION field in the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table for the specific Transaction Type Code selected by the user. Only the description is updated; the type code itself is never changed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Run Database Update
Update Description for the
matching Transaction Type Code
in CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Code (DCL-TR-TYPE) and the new Description (DCL-TR-DESCRIPTION) have been prepared from the selected screen row
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the database update against the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table
acceptance_criteria.Then: The TR_DESCRIPTION column is updated to the new description value for the record where TR_TYPE exactly matches the selected Transaction Type Code; the Transaction Type Code (TR_TYPE) itself is never modified

rules.rule_name: Commit and Confirm Successful Transaction Type Update
rules.rule_description: When the database update completes successfully, the system immediately commits the change to make it permanent, marks the update as succeeded, and prepares a success confirmation message for the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Commit the Update
Mark Update as Succeeded
Prepare Update Success Message

acceptance_criteria.Given: The database update for the Transaction Type Description has been executed
acceptance_criteria.When: The update completes successfully (database returns a success status with no errors)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system immediately commits the transaction to make the change permanent (SYNCPOINT); the update status is marked as 'Update Succeeded' (CA-UPDATE-SUCCEEDED); and if no other informational message is already set, an 'Update Success' informational message (WS-INFORM-UPDATE-SUCCESS) is prepared for display to the user

rules.rule_name: Handle Transaction Type Record Not Found During Update
rules.rule_description: If the Transaction Type record targeted for update cannot be found in the database at the time of the update attempt, the system treats the update as still pending (not completed) and informs the user that the record may have been deleted by another user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Mark Update as Still Pending
Record no longer exists -
possibly deleted by another user

acceptance_criteria.Given: The database update for the Transaction Type Description has been executed
acceptance_criteria.When: The database reports that no matching record was found (record not found condition, equivalent to SQLCODE +100)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The update status remains as 'Update Still Requested/Pending' (CA-UPDATE-REQUESTED is set, meaning the update did NOT succeed); an error message is prepared stating 'Record not found. Deleted by others?' along with the database status details; the screen is re-displayed with the error message so the user is informed the record no longer exists

rules.rule_name: Handle Deadlock Conflict During Transaction Type Update
rules.rule_description: If a deadlock is detected during the update attempt — meaning another user is simultaneously trying to update the same Transaction Type record — the system marks the update as still pending, flags the input as an error, and informs the user of the concurrent access conflict.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Mark Update as Still Pending
Mark Input as Error
Another user may be
updating the same record

acceptance_criteria.Given: The database update for the Transaction Type Description has been executed
acceptance_criteria.When: The database detects a deadlock condition (SQLCODE -911), indicating another user is concurrently updating the same Transaction Type record
acceptance_criteria.Then: The update status remains as 'Update Still Requested/Pending' (CA-UPDATE-REQUESTED is set, meaning the update did NOT succeed); the overall input is flagged as an error (INPUT-ERROR is set to TRUE); an error message is prepared stating 'Deadlock. Someone else updating?' along with the database status details; the screen is re-displayed with the error message so the user is aware of the concurrent conflict

rules.rule_name: Handle General Update Failure for Transaction Type
rules.rule_description: If the database update fails for any reason other than record-not-found or deadlock (such as a constraint violation or other database error), the system marks the update as still pending and prepares a detailed failure message for the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Mark Update as Still Pending
Prepare failure details
for error message

acceptance_criteria.Given: The database update for the Transaction Type Description has been executed
acceptance_criteria.When: The database returns any failure condition other than record-not-found or deadlock (any negative database error code other than -911)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The update status remains as 'Update Still Requested/Pending' (CA-UPDATE-REQUESTED is set, meaning the update did NOT succeed); an error message is prepared with the text 'Update failed with' followed by the database error details; the screen is re-displayed with the error message so the user is informed of the failure reason

key_functionalities.title: Update Success Handling
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Update Record Execution\nCompleted Successfully])
    B[Mark Update as Succeeded\nSet Update Completed Flag]
    C[Read Forward from Current Page Start Key\nRefresh list with updated data\nfrom CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE]
    D[Build Refreshed Screen\nwith up to 7 Transaction Type records]
    E[Clear Action Selection Field\non the updated row]
    F[Highlight Updated Row\nin Neutral Color]
    G[Set Success Message:\nUpdate completed successfully]
    H[Center the Success Message\non the screen]
    I[Display Refreshed Transaction Type List\nwith Success Message]
    J([Return - Wait for\nNext User Interaction])

    A --> B
    B --> C
    C --> D
    D --> E
    E --> F
    F --> G
    G --> H
    H --> I
    I --> J

rules.rule_name: Mark Transaction Type Update as Successfully Completed
rules.rule_description: When the database update of a Transaction Type description completes without error, the system marks the update as succeeded and sets the update-completed flag so downstream screen-building steps can reflect the completed state.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Mark Update as Succeeded
Set Update Completed Flag

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has confirmed an update action (PF10) on a selected Transaction Type row, and the UPDATE statement against CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE executes without any database error (SQL code = 0)
acceptance_criteria.When: The database successfully updates the TR_DESCRIPTION for the matching TR_TYPE record and commits the transaction
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system marks the update operation as succeeded (CA-UPDATE-SUCCEEDED = TRUE), and subsequently sets the Update Completed Flag (FLG-UPDATE-COMPLETED = TRUE) in the main processing flow so that all subsequent screen-building steps treat the update as finished

rules.rule_name: Refresh Transaction Type List After Successful Update
rules.rule_description: After a successful update, the system re-reads the Transaction Type records from the database starting from the same page position the user was on, so the refreshed list reflects the newly saved description.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Read Forward from Current Page Start Key
Refresh list with updated data
from CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE

acceptance_criteria.Given: The update of a Transaction Type description has been marked as succeeded and the Update Completed Flag is set to TRUE
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to redisplay the Transaction Type list
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the database read start key to the first Transaction Type code of the current page (WS-CA-FIRST-TR-CODE) and reads forward through CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE using the forward cursor (C-TR-TYPE-FORWARD), applying any active Type Code filter (exact match on TR_TYPE) and/or Description filter (LIKE match with wildcard characters), ordered ascending by TR_TYPE, to populate up to the maximum number of screen rows with refreshed data

rules.rule_name: Build Refreshed Screen with Up to Maximum Transaction Type Records
rules.rule_description: The system assembles the full screen output by initializing screen fields, setting row attributes, populating row data, configuring field attributes, preparing messages, and sending the screen — displaying up to the maximum number of Transaction Type records per page.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Build Refreshed Screen
with up to 7 Transaction Type records

acceptance_criteria.Given: The forward read from CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE has completed and row data is available in the working storage output array (WS-CA-ALL-ROWS-OUT)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system builds the screen to be sent to the user
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sequentially: (1) initializes screen header fields including current date, current time, page number, program name, and transaction ID; (2) sets display attributes for each row up to the maximum screen lines; (3) populates each row with TR_TYPE and TR_DESCRIPTION from the refreshed data; (4) configures filter field attributes; (5) prepares the appropriate informational or status message; and (6) sends the completed screen to the user's terminal, displaying up to the maximum number of Transaction Type records

rules.rule_name: Clear Action Selection Field on the Updated Row After Successful Update
rules.rule_description: Once an update has been successfully completed, the action selection field (U) on the row that was updated is cleared so the row returns to a neutral, unselected state on the refreshed screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Clear Action Selection Field
on the updated row

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen row array is being populated and a specific row had an Update action (U) selected, exactly one valid action was selected across all rows, and the Update Completed Flag is TRUE
acceptance_criteria.When: The system sets the display values for that row during screen construction
acceptance_criteria.Then: The action selection field for that row is cleared to blank (SELECT-BLANK), removing the 'U' indicator so the row appears unselected on the refreshed screen

rules.rule_name: Highlight Updated Transaction Type Row in Neutral Color
rules.rule_description: After a successful update, the Transaction Type code field and the description field of the updated row are displayed in neutral color to visually indicate the row that was just updated, and the cursor length indicator is set to position focus.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Highlight Updated Row
in Neutral Color

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen attribute setup is processing a row that had an Update action (U) selected, exactly one valid action was selected across all rows, no bad action selections exist, and the Update Completed Flag is TRUE
acceptance_criteria.When: The system assigns display color attributes to the fields of that row
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction Type code field (TRTTYPC) for that row is set to neutral color (DFHNEUTR), the Transaction Type description field (TRTYPDC) for that row is set to neutral color (DFHNEUTR), and the selection field length indicator (TRTSELL) is set to -1 to position the cursor

rules.rule_name: Set Update Success Informational Message
rules.rule_description: When an update has been successfully completed, the system sets an informational success message to be displayed on the screen, confirming to the user that the Transaction Type description was updated.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set Success Message:
Update completed successfully

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen message setup step is executing and the Update Completed Flag (FLG-UPDATE-COMPLETED) is TRUE
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates which message to display
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the informational message indicator to 'Update Success' (WS-INFORM-UPDATE-SUCCESS = TRUE), which causes the predefined update success message text to be placed into the screen's informational message field (INFOMSGO)

rules.rule_name: Center the Update Success Message on the Screen
rules.rule_description: The update success message is centered within the informational message display area on the screen by calculating the midpoint position based on the trimmed message length and the total available message field width.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Center the Success Message
on the screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The update success message text has been determined and is stored in WS-INFO-MSG, and the message is not a 'no information' message and not a 'no records found' message
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the message for display in the screen's informational message area
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system calculates the trimmed length of the message (WS-STRING-LEN = length of trimmed WS-INFO-MSG), calculates the starting position to center it (WS-STRING-MID = (total field length minus trimmed length) divided by 2, plus 1), places the trimmed message text into the output string at the calculated center position (WS-STRING-OUT), and moves the centered output string to the screen informational message field (INFOMSGO) displayed in neutral color (DFHNEUTR)

rules.rule_name: Display Refreshed Transaction Type List with Update Success Message
rules.rule_description: The fully built screen — containing the refreshed Transaction Type list and the centered update success message — is sent to the user's terminal, erasing the previous screen content and freeing the keyboard for the next interaction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Display Refreshed Transaction Type List
with Success Message

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen output area (CTRTLIAO) has been fully populated with refreshed Transaction Type data, row attributes, and the centered update success message
acceptance_criteria.When: The system sends the screen to the user's terminal
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system transmits the complete screen map (LIT-THISMAP from LIT-THISMAPSET) to the terminal, erasing the previous screen content, positioning the cursor as specified, and freeing the keyboard so the user can interact with the refreshed Transaction Type list showing the update success confirmation

key_functionalities.title: No Change Detection for Update
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([User Enters Update Action\non a Transaction Type Row])
    B[Retrieve the description\nentered by the user\nfor the selected row]
    C[Retrieve the existing description\ncurrently stored for that row\nfrom session memory]
    D{Are both descriptions\nidentical?\nSame text and same length\ncase-insensitive comparison}
    E[No Changes Detected\nSet informational message:\nNo changes were detected]
    F[Display screen with\nNo Changes Detected message\nto inform the user]
    G([User sees message and\nmay re-enter a different\ndescription to update])
    H[Changes Have Occurred\nProceed to validate\nthe new description entered]
    I([Continue with\nUpdate Validation Process])

    A --> B
    B --> C
    C --> D
    D -->|Yes - Descriptions Match| E
    E --> F
    F --> G
    D -->|No - Descriptions Differ| H
    H --> I

rules.rule_name: Detect No Changes When Update Description Matches Existing Description
rules.rule_description: When a user selects the Update action on a Transaction Type row and enters a new description, the system compares the entered description against the description currently stored in session memory. If both descriptions are identical in text (case-insensitive, ignoring leading and trailing spaces) and identical in trimmed length, the system informs the user that no changes were detected and does not proceed with the update validation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Are both descriptions identical? Same text and same length case-insensitive comparison

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has selected the Update action (U) on a Transaction Type row on the maintenance screen, and the system has retrieved both the description entered by the user for that row (WS-ROW-TR-DESC-IN for the selected row index) and the existing description currently stored in session memory for that same row (WS-CA-ROW-TR-DESC-OUT for the selected row index)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system compares the two descriptions by: (1) trimming leading and trailing spaces from both values, (2) converting both to uppercase for case-insensitive comparison, and (3) comparing the trimmed lengths of both values — and finds that the trimmed, uppercased text of the entered description is EQUAL TO the trimmed, uppercased text of the stored description AND the trimmed length of the entered description is EQUAL TO the trimmed length of the stored description
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the status to 'No Changes Detected' and sets an informational message indicating no changes were detected, then exits the description validation without proceeding to further description field validation, effectively preventing an unnecessary update operation

rules.rule_name: Proceed with Update Validation When Description Has Changed
rules.rule_description: When a user selects the Update action on a Transaction Type row and the entered description differs from the existing stored description (either in text content or trimmed length), the system recognises that a change has occurred and proceeds to validate the new description value for correctness before allowing the update to continue.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Changes Have Occurred - Proceed to validate the new description entered

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has selected the Update action (U) on a Transaction Type row, and the system has compared the entered description (WS-ROW-TR-DESC-IN for the selected row) against the existing stored description (WS-CA-ROW-TR-DESC-OUT for the selected row) using case-insensitive, trimmed comparison of both text and length
acceptance_criteria.When: The trimmed, uppercased entered description is NOT EQUAL TO the trimmed, uppercased stored description, OR the trimmed length of the entered description is NOT EQUAL TO the trimmed length of the stored description — meaning at least one difference exists between the two values
