rules.rule_name: Display Type Code Filter Field in Blue and Protected When Row Actions Are Pending
rules.rule_description: When a user has selected a delete or update action on any row in the transaction type list, the Type Code filter field must be displayed in blue and made read-only (protected) to prevent the user from changing the filter while an action is in progress.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Show entered type code value in the filter field
Display in BLUE color
Field is PROTECTED - user cannot edit

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is being prepared for display, and the user has previously entered a value in the Type Code filter field
acceptance_criteria.When: One or more row actions (delete or update) are pending — meaning the count of requested actions is greater than zero
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Type Code filter field must display the previously entered type code value, the field color must be set to BLUE to visually indicate it is locked, and the field must be set to PROTECTED so the user cannot modify the filter value while an action is in progress

rules.rule_name: Display Type Code Filter Field as Modifiable When a Filter Value Has Been Entered
rules.rule_description: When no row actions are pending but the user has entered a type code filter value — whether that value passed validation or failed validation — the filter field must display the entered value and remain editable so the user can correct or change it.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Show entered type code value in the filter field
Field is MODIFIABLE
User can change the filter

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is being prepared for display, no row actions (delete or update) are pending, and the user has entered a value in the Type Code filter field
acceptance_criteria.When: The Type Code filter is in a valid state (a valid numeric 2-digit code was entered) OR the Type Code filter is in an invalid state (a non-numeric or otherwise unacceptable value was entered)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Type Code filter field must display the entered type code value as-is, and the field must be set to MODIFIABLE so the user can edit or correct the filter value

rules.rule_name: Clear Type Code Filter Field When Filter Value Is Zero or Empty
rules.rule_description: When no row actions are pending, no filter value has been entered or the filter value is zero, the Type Code filter field must be cleared so that no value is shown to the user, indicating no active filter is applied.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Clear the type code filter field
Show nothing to the user

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is being prepared for display, no row actions (delete or update) are pending, and the Type Code filter is neither in a valid nor invalid state
acceptance_criteria.When: The Type Code filter value is zero or empty (no filter has been entered by the user)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Type Code filter field must be cleared — no value is displayed to the user — indicating that no type code filter is currently active. No field attribute change is applied beyond clearing the displayed value.

rules.rule_name: Clear Type Code Filter Field and Keep It Modifiable for All Other Conditions
rules.rule_description: When no row actions are pending, no recognized filter state applies, and the filter value is not zero or empty, the Type Code filter field must be cleared and kept editable so the user can freely enter a new filter value.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Clear the type code filter field
Field is MODIFIABLE
User can enter a filter

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is being prepared for display, no row actions (delete or update) are pending, the Type Code filter is neither valid nor invalid, and the filter value is not zero or empty
acceptance_criteria.When: None of the specific type code filter conditions (actions pending, filter valid, filter invalid, value zero or empty) are met — a catch-all other condition applies
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Type Code filter field must be cleared so no value is displayed, and the field must be set to MODIFIABLE so the user can freely enter a new type code filter value

sub_functionalities.title: Set Description Filter Field Display
sub_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    START([Set Description Filter\nField Display])
    ACTIONSCHECK{Are any row actions\npending on screen?\nDelete or Update requested?}
    SHOWBLUE[Display entered description value\nin the filter field\nMark field as PROTECTED\nShow in BLUE color]
    VALIDCHECK{Is description filter\nvalid OR invalid/error?}
    SHOWMODIFIABLE[Display entered description value\nin the filter field\nMark field as MODIFIABLE\nfor user editing]
    DEFAULTMOD[No description filter supplied\nMark field as MODIFIABLE\nfor user entry\nNo value displayed]
    FILTERNOTOK{Is description filter\nmarked as invalid/error?}
    HIGHLIGHTERROR[Override field color to RED\nPosition cursor on\ndescription filter field\nto indicate error to user]
    DONE([Description Filter\nField Display Set])

    START --> ACTIONSCHECK
    ACTIONSCHECK -->|Yes - Actions Pending| SHOWBLUE
    ACTIONSCHECK -->|No - No Actions Pending| VALIDCHECK
    VALIDCHECK -->|Yes - Filter Valid or Invalid| SHOWMODIFIABLE
    VALIDCHECK -->|No - No Filter Supplied| DEFAULTMOD
    SHOWBLUE --> FILTERNOTOK
    SHOWMODIFIABLE --> FILTERNOTOK
    DEFAULTMOD --> FILTERNOTOK
    FILTERNOTOK -->|Yes - Filter Has Error| HIGHLIGHTERROR
    FILTERNOTOK -->|No - No Error| DONE
    HIGHLIGHTERROR --> DONE

rules.rule_name: Display Description Filter Field in Blue and Protected When Row Actions Are Pending
rules.rule_description: When a user has selected a delete or update action on any row currently displayed on the Transaction Type maintenance screen, the description filter field must be displayed in blue color and set to protected (read-only), showing the previously entered description filter value. This prevents the user from changing filter criteria while an action is in progress.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Display entered description value in the filter field
Mark field as PROTECTED
Show in BLUE color

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is displayed and the user has previously entered a description filter value, and at least one row on the screen has a pending action (delete or update) requested by the user
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen is being prepared for display and the system evaluates the display attributes for the description filter field
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must display the previously entered description filter value in the description filter field, set the field attribute to PROTECTED (skip-enabled, auto-skip) so the user cannot modify it, and set the field color to BLUE to visually indicate it is locked during the pending action

rules.rule_name: Display Description Filter Field as Modifiable with Entered Value When Filter Is Active or Has Validation Error
rules.rule_description: When no row actions are pending and the description filter field either contains a valid filter value or has been flagged as invalid due to a validation error, the system must display the entered description value in the field and allow the user to edit it. This applies both when the filter successfully returned records and when the filter produced an error condition.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Display entered description value in the filter field
Mark field as MODIFIABLE
for user editing

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is being prepared for display, no row-level actions (delete or update) are currently pending, and the description filter field either contains a valid filter value that was accepted by the system OR the description filter has been marked as invalid due to a validation error (no records found for the filter)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the display attributes for the description filter field
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must display the previously entered description filter value in the description filter field and set the field attribute to MODIFIABLE (field send enable) so the user can edit or clear the filter value

rules.rule_name: Display Description Filter Field as Empty and Modifiable When No Filter Has Been Supplied
rules.rule_description: When no row actions are pending and no description filter has been supplied by the user (the field is blank), the description filter field must be presented as an empty, editable field ready for user input. No value is pre-populated in the field.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
No description filter supplied
Mark field as MODIFIABLE
for user entry
No value displayed

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is being prepared for display, no row-level actions (delete or update) are currently pending, and the description filter field has not been supplied with any value (it is blank, low-values, or spaces — neither a valid filter nor an invalid filter condition exists)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the display attributes for the description filter field and none of the specific filter conditions (actions pending, filter valid, filter invalid) are met
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must set the description filter field attribute to MODIFIABLE (field send enable) so the user can freely enter a description filter value, and no prior value is displayed in the field

rules.rule_name: Override Description Filter Field to Red with Cursor Positioning When Filter Validation Has Failed
rules.rule_description: Regardless of the initial display state set for the description filter field, if the description filter has been marked as invalid (e.g., no records were found matching the filter criteria), the system must override the field color to RED and position the cursor on the description filter field. This error highlight applies after all other display attribute decisions have been made and acts as a final override to draw the user's attention to the problematic filter.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Override field color to RED
Position cursor on
description filter field
to indicate error to user

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is being prepared for display and the description filter field has been marked as invalid or in error — specifically because no records were found in the Transaction Type table matching the entered description filter criteria
acceptance_criteria.When: The system applies the final display attribute overrides after the initial field display state has been determined
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must override the description filter field color to RED to visually signal the error condition to the user, and must position the screen cursor on the description filter field so the user's attention is immediately directed to correct the invalid filter value

key_functionalities.title: Informational Message Display
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    START([Informational Message Display\nDetermine message to show])

    DELOK{Delete just\nSucceeded?}
    DELMSG[Display:\nDelete Success Message]

    UPDOK{Update just\nCompleted?}
    UPDMSG[Display:\nUpdate Success Message]

    FILTERERR{Filter Validation\nErrors Present?}
    SKIPINFO[No informational message\nError message already shown]

    ENTERDEL{Enter pressed +\nDelete pending +\nOnly 1 valid action?}
    FILTERCHANGED1{Filter criteria\nchanged?}
    DELPROMPT[Display:\nConfirmation Prompt\n'Press PF10 to confirm Delete']

    ENTERUPD{Enter pressed +\nUpdate pending +\nOnly 1 valid action?}
    FILTERCHANGED2{Filter criteria\nchanged?}
    UPDPROMPT[Display:\nConfirmation Prompt\n'Press PF10 to confirm Update']

    PF7FIRST{PF7 pressed and\nalready on First Page?}
    NOPREVMSG[Display:\n'No previous pages to display']

    PF8NOLAST{PF8 pressed +\nNo next page +\nLast page already shown?}
    NOMOREMSG[Display:\n'No more pages to display']

    PF8NOSHOW{PF8 pressed +\nNo next page +\nLast page not yet shown?}
    LASTPAGEMARK[Mark last page as shown\nDisplay: Instructions to\ntype U or D to select actions]

    DEFAULT[Display:\nInstructions to\ntype U or D to select actions]

    CENTER[40: Center the message\nCalculate message length\nCompute midpoint offset\nPosition message on screen]

    SHOWMSG[Display final centered\ninformational message on screen\nin neutral color]

    END([Message Display Complete])

    START --> DELOK
    DELOK -->|Yes| DELMSG
    DELOK -->|No| UPDOK
    DELMSG --> CENTER

    UPDOK -->|Yes| UPDMSG
    UPDOK -->|No| FILTERERR
    UPDMSG --> CENTER

    FILTERERR -->|Yes - Filter Error| SKIPINFO
    FILTERERR -->|No| ENTERDEL
    SKIPINFO --> END

    ENTERDEL -->|Yes| FILTERCHANGED1
    FILTERCHANGED1 -->|No Change| DELPROMPT
    FILTERCHANGED1 -->|Filter Changed| ENTERUPD
    DELPROMPT --> CENTER

    ENTERDEL -->|No| ENTERUPD
    ENTERUPD -->|Yes| FILTERCHANGED2
    FILTERCHANGED2 -->|No Change| UPDPROMPT
    FILTERCHANGED2 -->|Filter Changed| PF7FIRST
    UPDPROMPT --> CENTER

    ENTERUPD -->|No| PF7FIRST
    PF7FIRST -->|Yes| NOPREVMSG
    PF7FIRST -->|No| PF8NOLAST
    NOPREVMSG --> CENTER

    PF8NOLAST -->|Yes| NOMOREMSG
    PF8NOLAST -->|No| PF8NOSHOW
    NOMOREMSG --> CENTER

    PF8NOSHOW -->|Yes| LASTPAGEMARK
    PF8NOSHOW -->|No| DEFAULT
    LASTPAGEMARK --> CENTER
    DEFAULT --> CENTER

    CENTER --> SHOWMSG
    SHOWMSG --> END

rules.rule_name: Display Delete Success Informational Message
rules.rule_description: When a transaction type record has just been successfully deleted, the system must display a delete success informational message to confirm the completed action to the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Delete just Succeeded?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has confirmed a delete action by pressing PF10, and the transaction type record has been successfully deleted from the TRANSACTION_TYPE table and committed
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates which informational message to display on the screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the informational message to the Delete Success message (WS-INFORM-DELETE-SUCCESS), which is then centered and displayed on the screen in neutral color to confirm the deletion was completed successfully

rules.rule_name: Display Update Success Informational Message
rules.rule_description: When a transaction type description has just been successfully updated, the system must display an update success informational message to confirm the completed action to the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Update just Completed?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has confirmed an update action by pressing PF10, and the transaction type description has been successfully updated in the TRANSACTION_TYPE table and committed
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates which informational message to display on the screen, and the delete success condition is not met
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the informational message to the Update Success message (WS-INFORM-UPDATE-SUCCESS), which is then centered and displayed on the screen in neutral color to confirm the update was completed successfully

rules.rule_name: Suppress Informational Message When Filter Validation Errors Exist
rules.rule_description: When filter validation errors are present (invalid type code filter or invalid description filter), no additional informational message is displayed because the error message already communicates the issue to the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Filter Validation Errors Present?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has entered filter criteria on the screen, and either the type code filter is marked as invalid (FLG-TYPEFILTER-NOT-OK) or the description filter is marked as invalid (FLG-DESCFILTER-NOT-OK)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates which informational message to display, and neither the delete success nor update success conditions are met
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system skips setting any informational message (CONTINUE with no action), because the filter error message is already displayed separately to the user, and no informational guidance message is shown

rules.rule_name: Display Delete Confirmation Prompt When Single Delete Action Pending
rules.rule_description: When the user presses ENTER with exactly one delete action selected and no filter changes have occurred, the system displays a confirmation prompt instructing the user to press PF10 to confirm the delete.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Enter pressed + Delete pending + Only 1 valid action?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type maintenance screen with one or more rows displayed, and the user has entered the Delete action code (D) in exactly one row's selection field, and no other action codes are selected on any other row, and no filter criteria (type code or description) have been changed since the last screen submission
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses ENTER to submit the screen, and the system evaluates the informational message to display, and no delete success, update success, or filter error conditions are active, and the total actions requested equals exactly one (WS-ONLY-1-ACTION) and the total valid actions equals exactly one (WS-ONLY-1-VALID-ACTION) and the number of delete actions requested is greater than zero (WS-DELETES-REQUESTED > 0)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the informational message to the Delete Confirmation prompt (WS-INFORM-DELETE), instructing the user to press PF10 to confirm the delete action; this message is then centered and displayed on the screen in neutral color

rules.rule_name: Suppress Delete Confirmation Prompt When Filter Criteria Changed
rules.rule_description: When the user presses ENTER with a delete action selected but has also changed the filter criteria, the delete confirmation prompt is suppressed because the filter change resets the context.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Filter criteria changed?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has entered the Delete action code (D) in exactly one row's selection field with exactly one valid action selected, and the user has also changed either the type code filter (FLG-TYPEFILTER-CHANGED-YES) or the description filter (FLG-DESCFILTER-CHANGED-YES) since the last screen submission
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses ENTER and the system evaluates the informational message to display
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system does NOT display the delete confirmation prompt; instead, processing continues to evaluate subsequent message conditions (update pending, PF7/PF8 conditions, or default instructions)

rules.rule_name: Display Update Confirmation Prompt When Single Update Action Pending
rules.rule_description: When the user presses ENTER with exactly one update action selected and no filter changes have occurred, the system displays a confirmation prompt instructing the user to press PF10 to confirm the update.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Enter pressed + Update pending + Only 1 valid action?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type maintenance screen with one or more rows displayed, and the user has entered the Update action code (U) in exactly one row's selection field, and no other action codes are selected on any other row, and no filter criteria (type code or description) have been changed since the last screen submission
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses ENTER to submit the screen, and the system evaluates the informational message to display, and no delete success, update success, filter error, or delete pending conditions are active, and the total actions requested equals exactly one (WS-ONLY-1-ACTION) and the total valid actions equals exactly one (WS-ONLY-1-VALID-ACTION) and the number of update actions requested is greater than zero (WS-UPDATES-REQUESTED > 0)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the informational message to the Update Confirmation prompt (WS-INFORM-UPDATE), instructing the user to press PF10 to confirm the update action; this message is then centered and displayed on the screen in neutral color

rules.rule_name: Suppress Update Confirmation Prompt When Filter Criteria Changed
rules.rule_description: When the user presses ENTER with an update action selected but has also changed the filter criteria, the update confirmation prompt is suppressed because the filter change resets the context.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Filter criteria changed?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has entered the Update action code (U) in exactly one row's selection field with exactly one valid action selected, and the user has also changed either the type code filter (FLG-TYPEFILTER-CHANGED-YES) or the description filter (FLG-DESCFILTER-CHANGED-YES) since the last screen submission
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses ENTER and the system evaluates the informational message to display
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system does NOT display the update confirmation prompt; instead, processing continues to evaluate subsequent message conditions (PF7/PF8 conditions or default instructions)

rules.rule_name: Display No Previous Pages Message When PF7 Pressed on First Page
rules.rule_description: When the user attempts to scroll backward (PF7) while already viewing the first page of transaction types, the system informs the user that no previous pages are available.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: PF7 pressed and already on First Page?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is viewing the Transaction Type maintenance screen and the current page is the first page (CA-FIRST-PAGE is true), meaning there are no records before the currently displayed set
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses PF7 (scroll backward) and the system evaluates the informational message to display
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the return message to 'No previous pages to display', which is then centered and displayed on the screen to inform the user they are already on the first page

rules.rule_name: Display No More Pages Message When PF8 Pressed and Last Page Already Shown
rules.rule_description: When the user attempts to scroll forward (PF8) but there are no more pages and the last page has already been shown in a previous PF8 press, the system informs the user that no more pages are available.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: PF8 pressed + No next page + Last page already shown?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is viewing the Transaction Type maintenance screen, and there is no next page of records (CA-NEXT-PAGE-NOT-EXISTS is true), and the last page has already been shown to the user in a prior interaction (CA-LAST-PAGE-SHOWN is true)
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses PF8 (scroll forward) and the system evaluates the informational message to display
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the return message to 'No more pages to display', which is then centered and displayed on the screen to inform the user they have reached the end of the available records

rules.rule_name: Display Action Instructions and Mark Last Page Shown When PF8 Reaches Last Page for First Time
rules.rule_description: When the user scrolls forward (PF8) and reaches the last page of records for the first time, the system displays instructions for available record actions and marks the last page as having been shown.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: PF8 pressed + No next page + Last page not yet shown?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is viewing the Transaction Type maintenance screen, and there is no next page of records (CA-NEXT-PAGE-NOT-EXISTS is true), and the last page has NOT yet been shown to the user (CA-LAST-PAGE-NOT-SHOWN is true)
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses PF8 (scroll forward) and the system evaluates the informational message to display, and no higher-priority message conditions (delete success, update success, filter errors, action pending) are active
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the informational message to the Record Actions instructions (WS-INFORM-REC-ACTIONS), instructing the user to type U or D to select actions on the displayed records; AND the system marks the last page as having been shown (CA-LAST-PAGE-SHOWN is set to TRUE) so that subsequent PF8 presses show the 'No more pages' message instead; the message is centered and displayed in neutral color

rules.rule_name: Display Default Action Instructions When No Specific Message Condition Met
rules.rule_description: When no specific message condition applies (no delete/update success, no filter errors, no pending actions, no PF7/PF8 boundary conditions), the system displays default instructions guiding the user to type U or D to select actions on displayed records.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display: Instructions to type U or D to select actions

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is viewing the Transaction Type maintenance screen with records displayed, and none of the specific message conditions are met: no delete just succeeded, no update just completed, no filter validation errors, no single pending delete or update action, not pressing PF7 on first page, not pressing PF8 on last page; AND either no informational message has been set yet (WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE is true) OR a next page of records exists (CA-NEXT-PAGE-EXISTS is true)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates which informational message to display
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the informational message to the Record Actions instructions (WS-INFORM-REC-ACTIONS), instructing the user to type U or D in the selection field of a row to perform an update or delete action; the message is then centered and displayed on the screen in neutral color

rules.rule_name: Center Informational Message on Screen
rules.rule_description: Before displaying any informational message, the system calculates the message length and midpoint offset to center the message within the available screen display area.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
40: Center the message
Calculate message length
Compute midpoint offset
Position message on screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: An informational message (WS-INFO-MSG) has been determined and is ready to be displayed on the Transaction Type maintenance screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the message for display
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system calculates the trimmed length of the message (WS-STRING-LEN = length of trimmed WS-INFO-MSG), then computes the starting position to center it (WS-STRING-MID = (total field length of WS-INFO-MSG minus WS-STRING-LEN) divided by 2, plus 1), then places the trimmed message text into the output string buffer (WS-STRING-OUT) at the calculated midpoint position, resulting in a centered message ready for screen display

rules.rule_name: Display Final Centered Informational Message in Neutral Color
rules.rule_description: The final centered informational message is displayed on the screen in neutral color, but only when a meaningful informational message exists and the 'no records found' condition is not active.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display final centered informational message on screen in neutral color

acceptance_criteria.Given: The informational message has been determined, centered, and placed into the output string buffer (WS-STRING-OUT), and the system is preparing to send the screen to the user
acceptance_criteria.When: The system applies the final message to the screen output area
acceptance_criteria.Then: If an informational message is active (NOT WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE) AND the 'no records found' condition is not set (NOT WS-MESG-NO-RECORDS-FOUND), the system moves the centered message text (WS-STRING-OUT) to the screen informational message output field (INFOMSGO of CTRTLIAO) and sets the display color to neutral (DFHNEUTR) for the informational message color attribute (INFOMSGC of CTRTLIAO); if either condition is not met, no informational message is displayed on screen

key_functionalities.title: Error Message Display
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    START([Start: Error Message Display])

    ROWVAL{Invalid Action Code\nentered in row\nselection field?}
    ROWVAL_ERR[Mark row in RED\nSet error flag:\nInvalid Action Code]

    MULTIACT{More than one row\nselected for action?}
    MULTI_ERR[Set error flag:\nOnly one action\nallowed at a time]

    DBCHECK[(Check CARDDEMO.\nTRANSACTION_TYPE\nfor matching records)]

    START --> ROWVAL
    ROWVAL -->|Yes - Invalid Code| ROWVAL_ERR
    ROWVAL -->|No| MULTIACT
    ROWVAL_ERR --> MULTIACT
    MULTIACT -->|Yes - More than 1| MULTI_ERR
    MULTIACT -->|No| DESCBLANK
    MULTI_ERR --> DESCBLANK
    DESCBLANK -->|Yes - Blank| DESCBLANK_ERR
    DESCBLANK -->|No| DESCALPHA
    DESCBLANK_ERR --> DESCALPHA
    DESCALPHA -->|Yes - Invalid chars| DESCALPHA_ERR
    DESCALPHA -->|No| TYPEFILTER
    DESCALPHA_ERR --> TYPEFILTER
    TYPEFILTER -->|Yes - Not numeric| TYPEFILTER_ERR
    TYPEFILTER -->|No| CROSSVAL
    TYPEFILTER_ERR --> CROSSVAL
    CROSSVAL -->|Yes - Filter supplied| DBCHECK
    CROSSVAL -->|No - No filters| ANYERROR
    DBCHECK -.->|COUNT matching records| NORECFOUND

    NORECFOUND -->|Records exist| ANYERROR
    NOREC_ERR --> ANYERROR
    ANYERROR -->|Yes - Errors exist| DISPLAYERR
    ANYERROR -->|No errors| SENDSCREEN
    DISPLAYERR --> PROTECTROWS
    PROTECTROWS --> SENDSCREEN
    SENDSCREEN([End: Screen sent\nwith error messages])

rules.rule_name: Validate Row Selection Action Code
rules.rule_description: When a user enters a value in a row's selection field that is not a valid action code (not Delete 'D' or Update 'U'), the system must reject the input, highlight the row selection field in RED, and set an error flag indicating an invalid action code was entered.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Invalid Action Code entered in row selection field?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A Transaction Type list screen is displayed with one or more rows of transaction type data, and the user has entered a value in a row's selection field
acceptance_criteria.When: The entered value in the row selection field is not blank, not a valid Delete action code ('D'), and not a valid Update action code ('U')
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must: (1) set the overall input status to ERROR, (2) mark that specific row's selection field error indicator to '1' (highlighted in RED), (3) set the error flag 'FLG-BAD-ACTIONS-SELECTED-YES' to indicate bad actions were selected, and (4) set the message flag 'WS-MESG-INVALID-ACTION-CODE' to TRUE to indicate an invalid action code was entered

rules.rule_name: Restrict to Single Row Action Selection
rules.rule_description: The system enforces that only one row can have an action (Delete or Update) selected at a time. If the user selects actions on more than one row simultaneously, the system must reject the input and display an appropriate error message.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: More than one row selected for action?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A Transaction Type list screen is displayed and the user has entered action codes in the row selection fields of multiple rows
acceptance_criteria.When: The count of rows with valid action codes (Delete or Update) plus any invalid selections results in more than one row having an action selected (WS-ACTIONS-REQUESTED > 1), and a second valid selection is detected while iterating through rows
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must: (1) mark the additional selected row's selection field error indicator to '1' (highlighted in RED), (2) set the error flag 'FLG-BAD-ACTIONS-SELECTED-YES', (3) set the overall input status to ERROR, and (4) set the message flag 'WS-MESG-MORE-THAN-1-ACTION' to TRUE indicating only one action is allowed at a time

rules.rule_name: Require Non-Blank Description for Update Action
rules.rule_description: When a user selects the Update action on a transaction type row, the description field for that row is mandatory and must not be left blank. If the description is blank or contains only spaces, the system must reject the update request with an appropriate error message.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Update requested but description is blank?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A Transaction Type list screen is displayed, the user has entered 'U' (Update) in a row's selection field, and the description field for that row is being validated
acceptance_criteria.When: The description field value for the selected update row is blank, contains only spaces, contains only low-values, or has a trimmed length of zero
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must: (1) set the overall input status to ERROR, (2) set the description field flag to 'FLG-ALPHNANUM-BLANK', (3) if no prior error message has been set (WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF), construct and store the error message 'Transaction Desc must be supplied.' in WS-RETURN-MSG, and (4) set the row description validation flag to 'FLG-ROW-DESCRIPTION-NOT-OK'

rules.rule_name: Restrict Description to Alphanumeric Characters Only
rules.rule_description: When a user selects the Update action on a transaction type row and provides a description, the description must contain only letters and numbers. Special characters or symbols are not permitted in the transaction type description.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Update requested but description contains non-alphanumeric characters?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A Transaction Type list screen is displayed, the user has entered 'U' (Update) in a row's selection field, the description field is not blank, and the description is being validated for character content
acceptance_criteria.When: After converting all valid alphanumeric characters to spaces, the remaining trimmed content of the description field (up to 50 characters) is not empty — meaning non-alphanumeric characters are present
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must: (1) set the overall input status to ERROR, (2) set the description field flag to 'FLG-ALPHNANUM-NOT-OK', (3) if no prior error message has been set (WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF), construct and store the error message 'Transaction Desc can have numbers or alphabets only.' in WS-RETURN-MSG, and (4) set the row description validation flag to 'FLG-ROW-DESCRIPTION-NOT-OK'

rules.rule_name: Validate Type Code Filter as Numeric
rules.rule_description: The Transaction Type Code filter field, when supplied by the user, must be a numeric value. Non-numeric entries are invalid and must be rejected. The field is optional — if left blank, no type code filtering is applied.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Type Code Filter entered but not a 2-digit number?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A Transaction Type list screen is displayed and the user has entered a value in the Type Code filter field (the value is not blank, not spaces, not zeros, and not low-values)
acceptance_criteria.When: The entered Type Code filter value fails a numeric check (IS NOT NUMERIC)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must: (1) set the overall input status to ERROR, (2) set the type filter flag to 'FLG-TYPEFILTER-NOT-OK', (3) set the flag 'FLG-PROTECT-SELECT-ROWS-YES' to lock all row selection fields preventing further row selections, and (4) store the error message 'TYPE CODE FILTER,IF SUPPLIED MUST BE A 2 DIGIT NUMBER' in WS-RETURN-MSG

rules.rule_name: Verify Filter Criteria Returns Matching Records
rules.rule_description: When the user supplies one or more filter values (Type Code filter and/or Description filter), the system must verify that at least one matching transaction type record exists in the database before proceeding. This cross-validation prevents the user from navigating to an empty result set.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Any filter supplied? Type Code or Description?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A Transaction Type list screen is displayed and the user has supplied at least one filter value — either a valid Type Code filter ('FLG-TYPEFILTER-ISVALID') or a valid Description filter ('FLG-DESCFILTER-ISVALID') or both
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes a COUNT query against the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table applying the active filter conditions: if Type Code filter is active (WS-EDIT-TYPE-FLAG = '1'), filter by exact match on TR_TYPE = WS-TYPE-CD-FILTER; if Description filter is active (WS-EDIT-DESC-FLAG = '1'), filter by TR_DESCRIPTION LIKE TRIM(WS-TYPE-DESC-FILTER) using wildcard matching
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system stores the count of matching records in WS-RECORDS-COUNT and proceeds to evaluate whether any records were found

rules.rule_name: Reject Filter Criteria with No Matching Records
rules.rule_description: If the filter criteria entered by the user (Type Code and/or Description) do not match any transaction type records in the database, the system must reject the filter values and inform the user that no records were found for the specified conditions.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Any matching records found?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has executed a count query against CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE using the supplied filter criteria and the result count (WS-RECORDS-COUNT) has been evaluated
acceptance_criteria.When: The count of matching records (WS-RECORDS-COUNT) equals zero — no transaction type records match the supplied filter conditions
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must: (1) set the overall input status to ERROR, (2) if the Type Code filter was active and valid, set its flag to 'FLG-TYPEFILTER-NOT-OK', (3) if the Description filter was active and valid, set its flag to 'FLG-DESCFILTER-NOT-OK', (4) set the flag 'FLG-PROTECT-SELECT-ROWS-YES' to lock all row selection fields, and (5) store the error message 'No Records found for these filter conditions' in WS-RETURN-MSG

rules.rule_name: Display Error Messages and Protect Row Selections on Validation Failure
rules.rule_description: When any input validation errors are detected during screen processing, the system must display the accumulated error message to the user, protect all row selection fields to prevent further invalid input, and re-send the screen with all error highlights and messages visible.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Any errors detected?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has completed all input validation checks (row action codes, multiple selections, description content, type code filter, and filter cross-validation) and one or more validation errors have been detected (INPUT-ERROR flag is set to TRUE)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the overall input error status and determines that errors exist
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must: (1) move the error message stored in WS-RETURN-MSG to the screen error message area (CCARD-ERROR-MSG / ERRMSGO), (2) set the next program, mapset, and map to the current program's values to stay on the same screen, (3) if filter validation failed (FLG-TYPEFILTER-NOT-OK), highlight the Type Code filter field in RED and position the cursor on it, (4) if description filter validation failed (FLG-DESCFILTER-NOT-OK), highlight the Description filter field in RED and position the cursor on it, (5) if row protection is required (FLG-PROTECT-SELECT-ROWS-YES), set all row selection fields to protected (DFHBMPRO) preventing user input, and (6) send the screen back to the user with all error highlights, RED field indicators, and error messages displayed

key_functionalities.title: Next Page Existence Check
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Start: Page of Records Has Been Read])
    B{Was the maximum\nnumber of rows per page\nreached?}
    C[Save the last transaction\ntype code of current page]
    D[Perform one extra fetch\nfrom the database beyond\nthe current page]
    E{Was an additional\nrecord found?}
    F[Set indicator:\nNext Page EXISTS\nSave the extra record's key\nas the starting point\nfor the next page]
    G[Set indicator:\nNext Page DOES NOT EXIST\nUser has reached the\nlast available page]
    H{Was this the\nfirst page and\nno records at all?}
    I[Set indicator:\nNo Records Found\nfor current search conditions]
    J([End: Next Page Indicator Set])

    A --> B
    B -->|Yes - Page is Full| C
    C --> D
    D --> E
    E -->|Yes - More Records Exist| F
    E -->|No - No More Records| G
    F --> J
    G --> J
    B -->|No - Page Not Full| H
    H -->|Yes - Zero Records on Page 1| I
    H -->|No - Partial Page Returned| G
    I --> J

rules.rule_name: Determine If Current Page Is Full
rules.rule_description: After reading transaction type records from the database, the system checks whether the number of records retrieved equals the maximum allowed rows per page to decide if a next-page existence check is needed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Was the maximum number of rows per page reached?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has been reading transaction type records forward from the database and is accumulating rows for the current page display
acceptance_criteria.When: The count of records read equals the maximum number of screen lines (rows per page)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system recognizes the current page is full, stops the read loop, saves the current transaction type code as the last record key of the current page, and proceeds to perform an extra fetch to check for additional records beyond this page

rules.rule_name: Save Last Transaction Type Code of Current Page
rules.rule_description: When the current page is determined to be full, the system saves the transaction type code of the last record on the page so it can be used as the boundary key for next-page detection and future navigation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Save the last transaction type code of current page

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has read the maximum number of records allowed per page from the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table
acceptance_criteria.When: The row count reaches the maximum screen lines limit
acceptance_criteria.Then: The transaction type code (TR_TYPE) of the last fetched record is saved as the last transaction type code for the current page (WS-CA-LAST-TR-CODE), which will serve as the starting reference point for determining if a next page exists

rules.rule_name: Perform Extra Fetch to Check for Next Page
rules.rule_description: After filling the current page to its maximum capacity, the system performs one additional database read beyond the last displayed record to determine whether more transaction type records exist, without displaying that extra record to the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Perform one extra fetch from the database beyond the current page

acceptance_criteria.Given: The current page of transaction type records is full (maximum rows per page have been read) and the last record's transaction type code has been saved
acceptance_criteria.When: The system performs one additional fetch from the forward-reading database cursor (C-TR-TYPE-FORWARD) using the same active filter conditions (type code filter and/or description filter if applicable)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The result of this extra fetch is evaluated to determine whether additional records exist beyond the current page, and the next-page indicator is set accordingly — this extra record is never displayed to the user

rules.rule_name: Set Next Page Exists and Save Next Page Starting Key
rules.rule_description: When the extra fetch beyond the current page successfully retrieves a record, the system confirms that a next page of transaction types is available and saves the retrieved record's transaction type code as the starting key for the next page navigation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set indicator: Next Page EXISTS
Save the extra record's key as the starting point for the next page

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has performed an extra fetch beyond the last displayed record on the current page
acceptance_criteria.When: The extra fetch returns a valid transaction type record (fetch is successful with no end-of-data condition)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the next-page indicator to 'Next Page EXISTS' (CA-NEXT-PAGE-EXISTS) and saves the transaction type code (TR_TYPE) of the extra fetched record as the last transaction type code (WS-CA-LAST-TR-CODE), which will be used as the starting key when the user navigates to the next page

rules.rule_name: Set Next Page Does Not Exist When Extra Fetch Returns No Record
rules.rule_description: When the extra fetch beyond the current full page returns no record, the system confirms the user is viewing the last available page of transaction types and sets the indicator accordingly. If the user was scrolling forward (PF8), an informational message is also set.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set indicator: Next Page DOES NOT EXIST
User has reached the last available page

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has performed an extra fetch beyond the last displayed record on a full page of transaction type records
acceptance_criteria.When: The extra fetch returns no record (end-of-data condition is reached)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the next-page indicator to 'Next Page DOES NOT EXIST' (CA-NEXT-PAGE-NOT-EXISTS); additionally, if the user pressed PF8 (scroll forward) to reach this page, the system sets the 'No More Records' message to inform the user that no further pages are available

rules.rule_name: Set Next Page Does Not Exist When Page Is Not Full
rules.rule_description: When the database returns fewer records than the maximum page size (a partial page), the system recognizes this as the last page of results and sets the next-page indicator to indicate no further pages exist.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set indicator: Next Page DOES NOT EXIST
User has reached the last available page

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is reading transaction type records forward from the database and the read loop ends before reaching the maximum rows per page
acceptance_criteria.When: The database cursor returns an end-of-data condition (no more records to fetch) before the page is full
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the next-page indicator to 'Next Page DOES NOT EXIST' (CA-NEXT-PAGE-NOT-EXISTS); if the user pressed PF8 (scroll forward) to navigate here, the system also sets the 'No More Records' message to inform the user that no further pages are available

rules.rule_name: Detect Zero Records on First Page
rules.rule_description: When the database returns no records at all during a forward read on the first page, the system must distinguish this condition from a partial page result in order to display an appropriate 'no records found' message to the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Was this the first page and no records at all?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has attempted to read transaction type records forward from the database and the read loop has ended with an end-of-data condition before retrieving any records
acceptance_criteria.When: The current page number is 1 (first page) AND the number of records read is zero
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system identifies this as a 'no records found' condition and proceeds to set the appropriate indicator to inform the user that no transaction type records exist for the current search or filter conditions

rules.rule_name: Set No Records Found Indicator on Empty First Page
rules.rule_description: When the first page of a transaction type search returns zero records, the system sets a 'No Records Found' indicator so the screen can display an appropriate message informing the user that no transaction types match the current filter conditions.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set indicator: No Records Found for current search conditions

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has determined that the current page is the first page (page number equals 1) and no transaction type records were retrieved from the database (row count is zero)
acceptance_criteria.When: Both conditions are confirmed — page number is 1 AND records read count is zero
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the 'No Records Found' message indicator (WS-MESG-NO-RECORDS-FOUND) so that the screen display will inform the user that no transaction type records exist for the applied search or filter conditions

key_functionalities.title: No Records Found Notification
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Start Forward Read])
    B[Open Forward Cursor\nand Begin Reading Records\nfrom Database]
    C{Records Returned\nfrom Database?}
    D[Load records onto screen\nup to 7 rows]
    E([Continue Normal Processing])
    F{Is this the\nFirst Page?\nPage Number = 1}
    G{Were Zero Rows\nReturned?}
    H[Set No Records Found Flag\nMark next page as not existing]
    I[Display Screen with\nNo Records Found Notification\nInforming user no records match\ncurrent search conditions]
    J([End - Await\nUser Action])

    A --> B
    B --> C
    C -->|Records Found| D
    D --> E
    C -->|No Records - Database\nreturned empty result| F
    F -->|Yes - First Page| G
    F -->|No - Not First Page| E
    G -->|Yes - Zero Rows Returned| H
    G -->|No - Some Rows Exist| E
    H --> I
    I --> J

rules.rule_name: No Records Found on First Page - Flag Setting
rules.rule_description: When the database returns no records during a forward read and the user is on the first page, the system must set the No Records Found flag and mark that no next page exists, so the screen can notify the user that no transaction types match the current search conditions.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set No Records Found Flag
Mark next page as not existing

acceptance_criteria.Given: A forward read of the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table has been executed using the current start key and any active filters (type code filter and/or description filter), AND the database returns no records (empty result set, SQL code indicates end of data), AND the current page number is 1 (first page), AND the number of rows loaded onto the screen is zero
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the result of the forward cursor fetch and detects that no records were returned
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must: (1) Set the No Records Found flag (WS-MESG-NO-RECORDS-FOUND) to TRUE to signal that no transaction types exist for the current search conditions, AND (2) Mark that no next page exists (CA-NEXT-PAGE-NOT-EXISTS) to indicate there are no further records beyond the current empty result

rules.rule_name: First Page Check Before No Records Found Notification
rules.rule_description: The No Records Found notification is only triggered when the user is on the first page of results. If the user is not on the first page, the absence of records is handled differently (e.g., as end of data), and no No Records Found message is shown.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Is this the
First Page?
Page Number = 1

acceptance_criteria.Given: A forward read of the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table has been executed, AND the database returns no records (empty result set)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system checks whether the current screen/page number equals 1 (first page)
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the page number IS 1 (first page): the system proceeds to check whether zero rows were returned before setting the No Records Found flag. If the page number is NOT 1 (not the first page): the system does NOT set the No Records Found flag and continues normal processing without a no-records notification

rules.rule_name: Zero Rows Returned Check Before No Records Found Notification
rules.rule_description: Even when on the first page and the database returns an end-of-data signal, the No Records Found flag is only set if the row counter is exactly zero, confirming that absolutely no records were loaded onto the screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Were Zero Rows
Returned?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has confirmed the current page is the first page (page number = 1), AND the database has returned an end-of-data result (no more records to fetch)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system checks whether the number of rows loaded onto the screen (WS-ROW-NUMBER) equals zero
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the row count IS zero: the system sets the No Records Found flag (WS-MESG-NO-RECORDS-FOUND) to TRUE. If the row count is NOT zero (some rows were already loaded before end-of-data was reached): the system does NOT set the No Records Found flag and continues normal processing

rules.rule_name: No Records Found Notification Display on Screen
rules.rule_description: When the No Records Found flag has been set, the screen must be sent to the user displaying a notification that no transaction type records match the current search conditions, and the user must await further action.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Display Screen with
No Records Found Notification
Informing user no records match
current search conditions

acceptance_criteria.Given: The No Records Found flag (WS-MESG-NO-RECORDS-FOUND) has been set to TRUE following a forward read that returned zero records on the first page, AND the screen setup process (2000-SEND-MAP) has been invoked including message setup (2500-SETUP-MESSAGE) and screen send (2600-SEND-SCREEN)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares and sends the screen to the user
acceptance_criteria.Then: The screen is displayed to the user with: (1) The No Records Found notification message populated in the error/message area of the screen (ERRMSGO), informing the user that no transaction type records match the current search conditions, AND (2) No data rows populated in the screen array (all row areas remain empty), AND (3) The next page indicator set to not existing, so no forward paging is available, AND (4) The screen awaits the user's next action (e.g., modify filters or navigate away)

rules.rule_name: Mark No Next Page When No Records Returned
rules.rule_description: When the database returns no records during a forward read (end-of-data condition), the system must always mark that no next page exists, regardless of whether it is the first page or not, to prevent the user from attempting to scroll forward.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set No Records Found Flag
Mark next page as not existing

acceptance_criteria.Given: A forward read of the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table has been executed using the current start key and any active filters
acceptance_criteria.When: The database returns an end-of-data result (SQL code indicates no more records), meaning no records were fetched in this read cycle
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must set the next page status to 'not exists' (CA-NEXT-PAGE-NOT-EXISTS), indicating to the screen that there are no further pages of transaction type records available for forward scrolling, regardless of which page the user is currently on

key_functionalities.title: Last Page Tracking
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([User Presses PF8
Page Forward]) --> B[Read Next Page
of Transaction Type Records]
    B --> C{More Records
Returned?}
    C -->|Yes - Records Found| D[Display Records
Set Next Page Exists flag]
    C -->|No - No More Records| E{Has Last Page
Already Been Shown
to User?}
    E -->|Yes - Already Shown| F[Display Message:
'No more pages to display']
    E -->|No - First Time
Reaching Last Page| G[Display Current Page
with Action Instructions]
    G --> H[Mark Last Page
as Already Shown]
    D --> I([Screen Displayed
to User])
    F --> I
    H --> I
    I --> J{User Navigates
Away from PF8?}
    J -->|Yes - Any Key
Other Than PF8| K[Reset Last Page
Tracking Flag
Back to Not Shown]
    J -->|No - Presses PF8
Again| A
    K --> L([Ready for
Next Interaction])

rules.rule_name: Reset Last Page Tracking When User Navigates Away from PF8
rules.rule_description: When the user presses any key other than PF8, the system resets the last-page-already-shown tracking flag so that if the user returns to the last page again, the appropriate first-time message and action instructions are displayed rather than the 'no more pages' message.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Reset Last Page Tracking Flag Back to Not Shown

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type list screen and the last page tracking flag may be in any state (shown or not shown)
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses any key other than PF8 (e.g., ENTER, PF7, PF3, PF10)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The last-page tracking flag is reset to 'Not Shown', so that the next time the user reaches the last page via PF8, the system will display the page with action instructions and mark it as shown for the first time again

rules.rule_name: Detect No More Records When Reading Forward
rules.rule_description: When reading transaction type records in the forward direction and no more records are found (end of data), the system marks that no next page exists. If the user pressed PF8 to trigger this read, a 'no more records' indicator is also set to drive the appropriate message display.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: No - No More Records

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is reading transaction type records in forward order using the active type code and/or description filters, and the current page has been filled with the maximum number of displayable rows
acceptance_criteria.When: An attempt to fetch one additional record beyond the page maximum returns no data (end of result set)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system marks that no next page exists, and if the read was triggered by the user pressing PF8, a 'no more records' indicator is set to drive the appropriate end-of-data message on the screen

rules.rule_name: Detect No More Records on Direct Fetch During Forward Read
rules.rule_description: When reading transaction type records in the forward direction and the very first fetch within the page loop returns no data, the system marks that no next page exists. If PF8 triggered the read, the no-more-records indicator is set. Additionally, if this occurs on the very first page (page 1) with zero rows returned, a 'no records found' indicator is set.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: No - No More Records

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is reading transaction type records in forward order using the active type code and/or description filters
acceptance_criteria.When: A fetch from the forward cursor returns no data (end of result set) before filling any row on the current page
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system marks that no next page exists; if the read was triggered by PF8, the no-more-records indicator is set; if this is page 1 and zero rows were returned, the 'no records found' indicator is set to inform the user that no transaction types match the current criteria

rules.rule_name: Display No More Pages Message When Last Page Already Shown
rules.rule_description: When the user presses PF8 to scroll forward but the last page has already been displayed in a previous PF8 action, the system informs the user that there are no further pages available.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Message: 'No more pages to display'

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is viewing the Transaction Type list screen, no next page of records exists beyond the current display, and the last page has already been shown to the user in a prior PF8 navigation
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses PF8 again to attempt to scroll forward
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system displays the message 'No more pages to display' on the screen, and no new data is loaded

rules.rule_name: Display Action Instructions and Mark Last Page as Shown on First Reach
rules.rule_description: When the user presses PF8 and reaches the last page of transaction type records for the first time (last page has not yet been shown), the system displays the current page along with available record action instructions, and marks the last page as having been shown so that subsequent PF8 presses trigger the 'no more pages' message instead.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Current Page with Action Instructions / Mark Last Page as Already Shown

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is viewing the Transaction Type list screen, no next page of records exists beyond the current display, and the last page has NOT yet been shown to the user
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses PF8 to scroll forward and reaches the last available page for the first time
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system displays the current page of transaction type records along with available record action instructions (informing the user of actions they can take on the displayed records), and the last-page tracking flag is set to 'Already Shown' so that any further PF8 press will display the 'No more pages to display' message

rules.rule_name: Navigate to Next Page When More Records Exist
rules.rule_description: When the user presses PF8 and more transaction type records exist beyond the current page, the system advances to the next page by using the last transaction type code of the current page as the starting point, increments the page number, clears all row selections, and displays the next set of records.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Yes - Records Found / Display Records / Set Next Page Exists flag

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is viewing the Transaction Type list screen and a next page of records exists (the system previously detected at least one record beyond the current page's maximum display rows)
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses PF8 to scroll forward
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system uses the last transaction type code displayed on the current page as the starting key for the next read, increments the page number by 1, reads the next page of transaction type records in ascending transaction type code order applying any active filters, clears all row selection flags, and displays the new page of records with the next-page-exists flag set appropriately

rules.rule_name: Display Record Action Instructions When Records Are Available
rules.rule_description: When transaction type records are displayed and either no informational message has been set yet or a next page of records exists, the system displays available record action instructions to guide the user on what actions they can perform on the displayed records.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Records / Set Next Page Exists flag

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is viewing the Transaction Type list screen with one or more transaction type records displayed
acceptance_criteria.When: No other overriding informational message has been set (such as delete/update confirmation or filter error) and either no message is currently set or a next page of records exists
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system displays the standard record action instructions message on the screen, informing the user of the available actions (such as selecting a row for update or delete) that can be performed on the displayed transaction type records

key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:

rules.rule_name: Save Current Transaction ID to Session State
rules.rule_description: Before returning control to the user, the system records the current transaction identifier into the communication area so that the next user interaction can identify which transaction was last active.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Save Current Transaction ID
to Communication Area

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has completed processing a user interaction and is preparing to return control to the user
acceptance_criteria.When: The session state is being saved before returning to CICS
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current Transaction ID (LIT-THISTRANID) must be saved into the 'From Transaction ID' field (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID) of the communication area

rules.rule_name: Save Current Program Name to Session State
rules.rule_description: Before returning control to the user, the system records the current program name into the communication area so that the next user interaction can identify which program was last executing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Save Current Program Name
to Communication Area

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has completed processing a user interaction and is preparing to return control to the user
acceptance_criteria.When: The session state is being saved before returning to CICS
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current Program Name (LIT-THISPGM) must be saved into the 'From Program' field (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM) of the communication area

rules.rule_name: Save Current Map Name to Session State
rules.rule_description: Before returning control to the user, the system records the name of the currently active screen map into the communication area so that the correct screen can be restored on the next user interaction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Save Current Map Name
to Communication Area

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has completed processing a user interaction and is preparing to return control to the user
acceptance_criteria.When: The session state is being saved before returning to CICS
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current Map Name (LIT-THISMAP) must be saved into the 'Last Map' field (CDEMO-LAST-MAP) of the communication area

rules.rule_name: Save Current Mapset Name to Session State
rules.rule_description: Before returning control to the user, the system records the name of the currently active screen mapset into the communication area so that the correct screen set can be restored on the next user interaction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Save Current Mapset Name
to Communication Area

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has completed processing a user interaction and is preparing to return control to the user
acceptance_criteria.When: The session state is being saved before returning to CICS
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current Mapset Name (LIT-THISMAPSET) must be saved into the 'Last Mapset' field (CDEMO-LAST-MAPSET) of the communication area

rules.rule_name: Save Paging Keys - First and Last Transaction Type Code of Current Page
rules.rule_description: The system preserves the Transaction Type Codes of the first and last records displayed on the current page so that forward and backward navigation can correctly retrieve the adjacent pages on the next user interaction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Paging Keys:
First and Last Transaction Type Code
of Current Page

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has read and displayed a page of Transaction Type records and is preparing to return control to the user
acceptance_criteria.When: The program-specific session state (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) is being saved into the combined communication area
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction Type Code of the first record on the current page (WS-CA-FIRST-TR-CODE) and the Transaction Type Code of the last record on the current page (WS-CA-LAST-TR-CODE) must both be preserved in the program-specific communication area so they are available for paging on the next interaction

rules.rule_name: Save Current Page Number to Session State
rules.rule_description: The system preserves the current page number so that the correct page number can be displayed and used for navigation on the next user interaction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Current Page Number

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has displayed a page of Transaction Type records and is preparing to return control to the user
acceptance_criteria.When: The program-specific session state (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) is being saved into the combined communication area
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current screen/page number (WS-CA-SCREEN-NUM) must be preserved in the program-specific communication area

rules.rule_name: Save Screen Row Data - Transaction Codes and Descriptions Displayed on Screen
rules.rule_description: The system preserves all Transaction Type Codes and Descriptions currently displayed on the screen so that on the next user interaction the program can compare user-entered values against the original displayed values, detect changes, and correctly process update or delete actions.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Screen Row Data:
Transaction Codes and Descriptions
Displayed on Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has populated the screen rows with Transaction Type records and is preparing to return control to the user
acceptance_criteria.When: The program-specific session state (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) is being saved into the combined communication area
acceptance_criteria.Then: For each screen row, both the Transaction Type Code (WS-CA-ROW-TR-CODE-OUT) and the Transaction Type Description (WS-CA-ROW-TR-DESC-OUT) that were displayed must be preserved in the program-specific communication area

rules.rule_name: Save Selected Row Number for Pending Action
rules.rule_description: The system preserves the row number that the user selected for a pending delete or update action so that on the next interaction (e.g., PF10 confirmation) the program can verify the same row is still selected and process the correct record.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Selected Row Number
for Pending Action

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has selected a row for a delete or update action and the program is preparing to return control to the user
acceptance_criteria.When: The program-specific session state (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) is being saved into the combined communication area
acceptance_criteria.Then: The selected row number (WS-CA-ROW-SELECTED) must be preserved in the program-specific communication area so it can be validated against the user's selection on the next interaction

rules.rule_name: Save Delete and Update Pending Flags to Session State
rules.rule_description: The system preserves the flags indicating whether a delete or update action is currently pending confirmation so that on the next user interaction (PF10) the program knows which action to execute.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Delete / Update
Pending Flags

acceptance_criteria.Given: A delete or update action has been initiated by the user but not yet confirmed, and the program is preparing to return control to the user
acceptance_criteria.When: The program-specific session state (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) is being saved into the combined communication area
acceptance_criteria.Then: The delete-requested flag (CA-DELETE-REQUESTED) and the update-requested flag (CA-UPDATE-REQUESTED) must both be preserved in the program-specific communication area so the correct confirmation action can be taken on the next interaction

rules.rule_name: Save Type Code Filter Value to Session State
rules.rule_description: The system preserves the Transaction Type Code filter value entered by the user so that on the next interaction the program can detect whether the filter has changed and apply the same filter when re-reading data.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Type Code Filter Value
Entered by User

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has entered a Transaction Type Code filter value and the program is preparing to return control to the user
acceptance_criteria.When: The program-specific session state (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) is being saved into the combined communication area
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction Type Code filter value (WS-CA-TYPE-CD) must be preserved in the program-specific communication area

rules.rule_name: Save Description Filter Value to Session State
rules.rule_description: The system preserves the Transaction Type Description filter value entered by the user so that on the next interaction the program can detect whether the filter has changed and apply the same filter when re-reading data.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Description Filter Value
Entered by User

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has entered a Transaction Type Description filter value and the program is preparing to return control to the user
acceptance_criteria.When: The program-specific session state (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) is being saved into the combined communication area
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction Type Description filter value (WS-CA-TYPE-DESC) must be preserved in the program-specific communication area

rules.rule_name: Save Next Page Exists and Last Page Shown Indicators to Session State
rules.rule_description: The system preserves the indicators for whether a next page of records exists beyond the current display and whether the last page has already been shown to the user, so that paging messages and navigation behavior are correct on the next user interaction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Next Page Exists Indicator
Last Page Shown Indicator

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has determined the paging status of the current display and is preparing to return control to the user
acceptance_criteria.When: The program-specific session state (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) is being saved into the combined communication area
acceptance_criteria.Then: The 'Next Page Exists' indicator (CA-NEXT-PAGE-EXISTS / CA-NEXT-PAGE-NOT-EXISTS) and the 'Last Page Shown' indicator (CA-LAST-PAGE-SHOWN / CA-LAST-PAGE-NOT-SHOWN) must both be preserved in the program-specific communication area

rules.rule_name: Combine General Session Data and Program-Specific State into Single Communication Area
rules.rule_description: The system merges the general session data (transaction ID, program name, map, mapset) and the program-specific state (paging keys, page number, row data, selected row, action flags, filter values, paging indicators) into a single combined communication area before passing it back to CICS.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Combine General Session Data
and Program-Specific State
into Single Communication Area

acceptance_criteria.Given: Both the general communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) and the program-specific state (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) have been updated with current session values
acceptance_criteria.When: The program is preparing to return control to CICS
acceptance_criteria.Then: The general communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) must be copied into the first portion of the combined work communication area (WS-COMMAREA), and the program-specific state (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) must be copied into the immediately following portion of WS-COMMAREA starting at the offset equal to the length of CARDDEMO-COMMAREA plus one, so that both sections are contiguous in a single communication area

rules.rule_name: Pass Combined Communication Area Back to CICS with Current Transaction ID
rules.rule_description: The system returns control to CICS, passing the fully combined communication area and specifying the current transaction ID so that the next user interaction resumes the same transaction with all preserved session state intact.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Pass Combined Communication Area
back to CICS with Current
Transaction ID

acceptance_criteria.Given: The combined communication area (WS-COMMAREA) has been fully populated with all current session state
acceptance_criteria.When: The program issues a CICS RETURN command
acceptance_criteria.Then: The CICS RETURN must specify the current Transaction ID (LIT-THISTRANID) as the next transaction to invoke, pass the combined communication area (WS-COMMAREA) with its full length, so that the next user interaction restores the complete session state

rules.rule_name: Map ENTER Key to Submit Screen Action
rules.rule_description: When a user presses the ENTER key, the system recognizes it as a screen submission action, triggering input validation and processing of any selected row actions or filter changes.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set Action: Enter
Submit Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is displayed and the user is ready to submit their input
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses the ENTER key
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the active key action to ENTER (CCARD-AID-ENTER = TRUE), which triggers screen input collection, validation of filters and row selections, and processing of any pending delete or update confirmations

rules.rule_name: Map PF2 Key to Add New Transaction Type Action
rules.rule_description: When a user presses PF2, the system recognizes it as a request to navigate to the Add New Transaction Type screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set Action: PF2
Add New Record

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is displayed
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses the PF2 key
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the active key action to PF2 (CCARD-AID-PFK02 = TRUE), which will trigger navigation to the Add New Transaction Type program

rules.rule_name: Map PF3 Key to Exit to Menu Action
rules.rule_description: When a user presses PF3, the system recognizes it as a request to exit the current screen and return to the calling menu or Admin menu.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set Action: PF3
Exit to Menu

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is displayed
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses the PF3 key
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the active key action to PF3 (CCARD-AID-PFK03 = TRUE), which will trigger navigation back to the calling program or Admin menu

rules.rule_name: Map PF7 Key to Page Backward Action
rules.rule_description: When a user presses PF7, the system recognizes it as a request to scroll backward to the previous page of transaction type records.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set Action: PF7
Page Backward

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is displaying a list of transaction types
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses the PF7 key
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the active key action to PF7 (CCARD-AID-PFK07 = TRUE), which will trigger reading the previous page of transaction type records in descending order

rules.rule_name: Map PF8 Key to Page Forward Action
rules.rule_description: When a user presses PF8, the system recognizes it as a request to scroll forward to the next page of transaction type records.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set Action: PF8
Page Forward

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is displaying a list of transaction types
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses the PF8 key
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the active key action to PF8 (CCARD-AID-PFK08 = TRUE), which will trigger reading the next page of transaction type records in ascending order

rules.rule_name: Map PF10 Key to Confirm Delete or Update Action
rules.rule_description: When a user presses PF10, the system recognizes it as a confirmation to execute a previously selected delete or update action on a transaction type record.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set Action: PF10
Confirm Delete or Update

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is displayed and the user has previously selected a delete or update action on a row and pressed ENTER to preview the action
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses the PF10 key
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the active key action to PF10 (CCARD-AID-PFK10 = TRUE), which will trigger execution of the confirmed delete or update operation, subject to additional validation that filters and row selection have not changed

rules.rule_name: Alias PF13 to PF1 Action
rules.rule_description: PF13 is treated as an alias for PF1, allowing users on terminals where upper-row function keys (PF13-PF24) are the primary keys to perform the same PF1 action.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: ALIAS13[PF13 → Same as PF1]

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is displayed and the user's terminal uses upper-row function keys
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses the PF13 key
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the active key action to PF1 (CCARD-AID-PFK01 = TRUE), identical to the result of pressing PF1, and the screen processes the action as if PF1 was pressed

rules.rule_name: Alias PF14 to PF2 Add New Record Action
