Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program entry state is set to indicate a fresh program entry (not a re-entry), the key action is set to ENTER (as if the user pressed Enter for the first time), and the current map and mapset are recorded as this program's own map and mapset

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Screen Navigation State to Fresh Entry on Return from Add/Update Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: After clearing saved session data, the system must set the navigation state flags so that the Transaction Type List screen behaves exactly as if the user is entering it for the first time. This ensures the screen initializes correctly and does not attempt to process any prior user input or pending actions.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen navigation state has been set to fresh entry following a PF3 return from the Add/Update Transaction Type screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The page position is being reset
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current page position is set to the first page, meaning the Transaction Type List will be displayed starting from the beginning of the transaction type records (ordered by transaction type code ascending)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reset Page Position to First Page on Return from Add/Update Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: When returning from the Add/Update Transaction Type screen, the list display position must be reset to the very first page of transaction types, regardless of which page the user was viewing before navigating to the Add/Update screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The page position has been reset to the first page following a PF3 return from the Add/Update Transaction Type screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The last-page tracking indicator is being reset
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The last-page-shown indicator is set to 'not yet shown', meaning the system will not display 'No more pages to display' prematurely and will correctly evaluate whether the end of the transaction type list has been reached as the user pages forward through the refreshed results

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark Last Page as Not Yet Shown on Return from Add/Update Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: When returning from the Add/Update Transaction Type screen and resetting to the first page, the system must also reset the indicator that tracks whether the last page of results has been displayed to the user. This ensures that end-of-list messaging and paging behavior are correct for the fresh display.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has submitted the Transaction Type List screen by pressing a key (Enter, PF key, etc.)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system receives the screen input from the Transaction Type List screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All user-entered data from the Transaction Type List screen is captured into working storage, including the type code filter field, description filter field, all row selection flags, all row transaction type codes, and all row descriptions, making them available for subsequent input validation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Receive Transaction Type List Screen Input
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user submits the Transaction Type List screen, the system must receive and capture all data entered by the user from the screen into working storage for subsequent validation and processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type List screen has been received successfully
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the Type Code filter field from the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The value entered by the user in the Type Code filter field (TRTYPEI) is stored in the working storage variable WS-IN-TYPE-CD, preserving exactly what the user typed including blanks or zeros if the field was left empty

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Type Code Filter Value from Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: After receiving the screen, the system captures the value entered by the user in the Type Code filter field and stores it in working storage for subsequent validation and filtering of transaction type records.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type List screen has been received successfully
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the Description filter field from the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The value entered by the user in the Description filter field (TRDESCI) is stored in the working storage variable WS-IN-TYPE-DESC, preserving exactly what the user typed including blanks if the field was left empty

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Description Filter Value from Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: After receiving the screen, the system captures the value entered by the user in the Description filter field and stores it in working storage for subsequent validation and partial-match filtering of transaction type records.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type List screen has been received and the type code and description filter values have been captured
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system begins processing row-level input
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system iterates through every row from row 1 to the maximum number of display rows (WS-MAX-SCREEN-LINES, which is 7), processing each row's selection flag, transaction type code, and description in sequence before moving to the next row

all_rules.Rule_Name: Iterate Through All Display Rows to Capture Row-Level Input
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system must process every row displayed on the Transaction Type List screen to capture any user-entered selections or description changes. All rows are processed regardless of whether they contain data, ensuring no user input is missed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is processing a specific row during the row iteration loop
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system reads the selection field for the current row
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The value from the row's selection field on screen (TRTSELI for the current row index I) is stored in the working storage array WS-EDIT-SELECT at position I, capturing whatever the user entered — U for update, D for delete, or blank for no action

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Row Action Selection Flag
all_rules.Rule_Description: For each displayed row, the system captures the action code entered by the user in the row's selection field. This action code indicates the user's intended operation for that row — Update (U), Delete (D), or no action (blank).

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is processing a specific row during the row iteration loop and has captured the row's selection flag
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system reads the transaction type code field for the current row
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The transaction type code value from the screen field TRTTYPI at position I is stored in the working storage array WS-ROW-TR-CODE-IN at position I, identifying the transaction type record associated with this row

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Transaction Type Code for Each Row
all_rules.Rule_Description: For each displayed row, the system captures the transaction type code shown on that row. This code is read-only on the screen and identifies which transaction type record the user is acting upon.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is processing a specific row during the row iteration loop and has captured the row's selection flag and transaction type code
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to evaluate the row description field
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The working storage array WS-ROW-TR-DESC-IN at position I is set to LOW-VALUES (empty) before any conditional check on the description field content, ensuring a clean default state regardless of what the description field contains

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initialize Row Description to Empty Before Conditional Capture
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before evaluating whether a user has entered a description for a row, the system pre-initializes the row description storage to empty. This ensures that if the description is subsequently skipped, the stored value is clean and does not carry over stale data from a previous execution.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is processing the description field for a specific row during the row iteration loop
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The row description field (TRTYPDI at position I) contains either an asterisk character (LIT-ASTERISK) or spaces
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system skips capturing the description for this row — the working storage array WS-ROW-TR-DESC-IN at position I retains the LOW-VALUES (empty) value that was set during initialization, and no description value is stored for this row

all_rules.Rule_Name: Skip Row Description When Field Contains Asterisk or Is Blank
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the description field for a row contains an asterisk (*) or is blank/spaces, the system treats the description as not entered by the user and retains the empty value. An asterisk is used as a system placeholder to indicate a blank or unchanged description, and spaces indicate the user left the field empty.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is processing the description field for a specific row during the row iteration loop
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The row description field (TRTYPDI at position I) contains a value that is neither an asterisk (LIT-ASTERISK) nor spaces
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system applies the TRIM function to remove leading and trailing spaces from the description value in TRTYPDI at position I, and stores the trimmed result in the working storage array WS-ROW-TR-DESC-IN at position I, making the cleaned description available for update validation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture and Trim Row Description When User Has Entered a Value
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the user has entered an actual description value in a row's description field (not an asterisk and not blank), the system captures it by trimming leading and trailing spaces before storing it. This ensures clean description data is available for subsequent update validation and comparison against the existing stored description.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type maintenance screen and has previously made row action selections (Delete or Update flags on rows)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user changes the Transaction Type Code filter value OR changes the Description filter value from their previous submitted values
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All row selection flags across all screen rows are cleared (reset to empty/spaces), no row-level action validation is performed, and the program proceeds directly to the end of row validation with zero counts for all action types

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Row Selections When Filter Changes
all_rules.Rule_Description: When either the Transaction Type Code filter or the Description filter has been changed by the user, all previously entered row action selections must be cleared and row-level validation must be skipped entirely to prevent stale selections from being processed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The filter values have not changed from the previous submission and row validation is about to begin
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Row selection validation is initiated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The following counters are all set to zero: Total Actions Requested, No-Action rows count, Deletes Requested count, Updates Requested count, and Valid Actions Selected count

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initialize Row Action Counters Before Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before scanning and validating row action selections, all action counters must be reset to zero to ensure accurate counting of the current screen submission's requested actions.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All row action counters have been initialized to zero and the filter has not changed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system scans all row selection fields across the entire screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system counts: (1) the number of rows with no action (blank or empty), (2) the number of rows with a Delete action flag, (3) the number of rows with an Update action flag; then calculates Total Actions Requested as (Maximum Screen Lines minus No-Action rows count), and Valid Actions Selected as (Deletes Requested plus Updates Requested)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Count Delete and Update Selections Across All Rows
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system scans all row selection fields simultaneously to tally the number of blank/empty rows, Delete requests, and Update requests, then calculates the total number of actions requested and the total number of valid actions selected.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is iterating through each screen row from the last row to the first row
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the action selection field value for the current row
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The row is classified into one of three categories: (1) Valid action — the selection contains a recognized Delete or Update action code; (2) Blank/Empty — the selection field is blank or empty, meaning no action is requested for this row; (3) Invalid — the selection contains any value other than a valid Delete or Update code or blank

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate Each Row Action Selection Code
all_rules.Rule_Description: Each row on the screen is examined individually (from the last row to the first row) to determine whether the action selection field contains a valid action code (Delete or Update), is blank (no action), or contains an invalid value.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is iterating through screen rows and has found a row with a valid Delete or Update action code
Acceptance_Criteria.When: A valid action code is identified on a row
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The row number (position on screen) is saved as the selected row number (I-SELECTED) for use in subsequent delete or update operations

all_rules.Rule_Name: Record the Row Number of the Selected Action
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a valid action (Delete or Update) is found on a row, the row number is recorded as the currently selected row for subsequent processing of the action.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has already found and recorded a valid action on a previous row during the current loop iteration
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Another row is found with a valid Delete or Update action code
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current row's selection field is flagged with an error indicator (highlighted in red), and the overall multiple-actions error flag is set to indicate that more than one action has been selected

all_rules.Rule_Name: Enforce Single Action Selection Rule - Flag Multiple Selections
all_rules.Rule_Description: Only one row action (Delete or Update) is permitted per screen submission. If a valid action is found on a row but another valid action has already been found on a previous row during the same loop iteration, the current row is flagged as an error.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A row has a valid Update action code selected and it is the only valid action found so far (no multiple-action error condition)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system identifies the action on the row as an Update request
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system proceeds to validate the description content for that row (description validation sub-process is invoked), checking that the description is not blank and contains only alphanumeric characters

all_rules.Rule_Name: Trigger Description Validation for Update Action
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a row has a valid Update action selected and it is the first (only) valid action found so far, the description field for that row must be validated to ensure the new description value is acceptable before the update can proceed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is evaluating a row's action selection field during the row validation loop
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The row's action selection field is blank or empty (no action code entered)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The row is skipped with no error flagging, no counter increments for this row, and processing continues to the next row

all_rules.Rule_Name: Skip Validation for Blank Row Selections
all_rules.Rule_Description: Rows where the action selection field is blank or empty represent no user intent and require no validation or processing; they are simply skipped.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is evaluating a row's action selection field during the row validation loop
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The row's action selection field contains any value other than a valid Delete code, a valid Update code, or blank/empty
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The following error conditions are set: (1) the row's selection field is flagged with an error indicator (to be displayed in red on screen), (2) the overall bad-actions-selected flag is set to Yes, (3) the overall input error flag is set, and (4) the error message is set to indicate an invalid action code was entered

all_rules.Rule_Name: Flag Invalid Action Code Entry
all_rules.Rule_Description: If a user enters any value in a row's selection field that is not a recognized action code (not Delete, not Update, and not blank), the entry is invalid and must be flagged as an error with appropriate messaging.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The row validation loop has completed and a selected row number has been identified (or remains at zero if no row was selected)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the current selected row number against the previously stored selected row number from the communication area
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the selected row number is the same as the previously stored value, the row-selection-changed flag is set to No (unchanged); if the selected row number is different from the previously stored value, the row-selection-changed flag is set to Yes (changed) and the new selected row number is saved to the communication area for use in subsequent PF10 confirmation validation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Change in Selected Row Between Submissions
all_rules.Rule_Description: After completing the row loop, the system compares the currently selected row number with the row number that was selected in the previous screen submission to detect whether the user has changed their row selection.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All screen rows have been evaluated and the total actions requested count has been determined
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The total number of action selections (Delete plus Update) across all rows is greater than one
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The overall input error flag is set to indicate an error condition, and the error message is set to communicate that only one action is allowed at a time per screen submission

all_rules.Rule_Name: Enforce Single Action Rule - Set Final Error for Multiple Actions
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all rows have been evaluated, if the total count of actions requested across all rows exceeds one, a final overall input error is set with a message instructing the user that only one action is permitted at a time.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has submitted the Transaction Type maintenance screen with one or more rows potentially having action codes entered in the selection fields
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system begins processing the submitted screen input and prepares to validate row selections
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) Count the number of rows with no action (blank or low-values) as 'no actions selected'; (2) Count the number of rows with a Delete action flag as 'deletes requested'; (3) Count the number of rows with an Update action flag as 'updates requested'; (4) Compute total actions requested as: Maximum Screen Lines minus No-Action rows; (5) Compute valid actions selected as: Deletes Requested plus Updates Requested. All counts are reset to zero before tallying begins.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Count All Row Actions Before Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before validating individual row selections, the system tallies all action flags entered across all screen rows to determine the total number of delete requests, update requests, and blank (no-action) rows. Valid actions are computed as the sum of deletes and updates.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has submitted the Transaction Type maintenance screen with changes to the Type Code filter field or the Description filter field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system begins processing row selections
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must immediately clear all row selection flags (reset all selection indicators to blank/empty) and skip all row-level action validation, proceeding directly to filter validation instead. No row action counts are computed and no row errors are flagged.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Skip Row Validation When Filters Have Changed
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the user has changed either the Type Code filter or the Description filter on the same screen submission, all previously entered row selections are automatically cleared and row-level validation is bypassed entirely, since the filter change will reload new data.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is processing submitted screen rows and filters have not changed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system examines each row from the last row to the first row
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: For each row where a valid action code (Delete or Update) is found, the system records that row's position number as the currently selected row. The loop continues examining all rows regardless of whether a selection has already been found, to detect multiple selections.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Identify and Track the Selected Row
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system iterates through all screen rows from the last row to the first row to identify which row has an action selected. The row number of the selected row is tracked so it can be used for subsequent update or delete operations.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has entered a value in a row's selection field on the Transaction Type maintenance screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the value in the selection field and it is not a valid Delete flag, not a valid Update flag, and not blank
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) Set an overall input error condition; (2) Flag that specific row with a selection error indicator (value '1'); (3) Set the bad-actions-selected flag to YES; (4) Set the error message to indicate an invalid action code was entered. The row is marked for red highlighting on the screen.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reject Invalid Action Codes in Row Selection Field
all_rules.Rule_Description: Each row's selection field must contain only a recognized action code (Delete or Update flag) or be blank. Any other value entered in the selection field is treated as an invalid action code, triggering an error condition on that specific row.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is iterating through screen rows and has already identified at least one row with a valid action selected
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system encounters another row that also has a valid action code (Delete or Update) entered
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) Flag the additional selected row with a selection error indicator (value '1'); (2) Set the bad-actions-selected flag to YES. The first selected row is not flagged as an error — only the additional rows beyond the first are marked as errors.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Prevent Multiple Simultaneous Row Actions
all_rules.Rule_Description: Only one transaction type record can be actioned (updated or deleted) at a time. If the system detects that a second row has been selected for action while a first row is already selected, the second (and any subsequent) row is flagged as an error.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is examining a row that has a valid action code entered and it is the first selected row encountered
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The action code on that row is an Update request
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must invoke the description validation routine (1211-EDIT-ARRAY-DESC) for that row to verify the new description value is acceptable before proceeding to the next row. If the action is a Delete request (not Update), description validation is skipped and the system proceeds directly to the next row.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Trigger Description Validation for Update Action
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a row is selected with an Update action and it is the first (only) selection found so far, the system must immediately validate the description field entered for that row before continuing to examine remaining rows.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has finished examining all screen rows for action selections
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The total number of actions requested across all rows is more than one (WS-MORETHAN1ACTION condition is true)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) Set the overall input error condition to ERROR; (2) Set the error message indicator to 'More Than 1 Action' message. No delete or update operation will be executed. The screen will be redisplayed with error indicators.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Final Error Condition When Multiple Actions Detected
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all rows have been examined, if the total count of actions requested exceeds one, the system sets a final error condition preventing any action from being processed and prepares the appropriate error message for display.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is preparing the screen display after processing row selections and one or more rows have been flagged with a selection error indicator (value '1')
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets up screen field attributes for each row
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: For every row where the selection error indicator equals '1': (1) The selection field color must be set to RED; (2) The cursor must be positioned to that selection field (length set to -1). Rows without a selection error indicator are not highlighted in red.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Highlight Invalid Row Selections in Red on Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: Any row that has been flagged with a selection error — either because it was an additional selection beyond the first, or because it contained an invalid action code — must be visually highlighted in red on the screen so the user can clearly identify which rows have problems.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has set the input error condition and the 'More Than 1 Action' message indicator after detecting multiple row selections
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the message area of the screen for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The 'More Than 1 Action' error message must be displayed in the error message area of the screen. The informational message area remains blank (no informational message is shown when there is an error condition). The screen is sent to the user showing the error.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Error Message for Multiple Action Selection
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the system has determined that more than one row action was selected simultaneously, the appropriate error message must be set and displayed to the user on the screen, clearly communicating that only one action is permitted at a time.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has finished examining all screen rows and exactly one row has a valid action code (Delete or Update) entered, with no other rows having any action selected
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The multiple-action check determines that WS-MORETHAN1ACTION is false (only one action exists)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) Not set any multiple-action error condition; (2) Retain the recorded selected row number (I-SELECTED) for use in subsequent delete or update processing; (3) Allow the flow to continue to the appropriate action handler (delete confirmation or update confirmation) based on the action type selected. If the single action is an Update, the description validation result from the earlier step is also carried forward.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Proceed with Single Valid Action
all_rules.Rule_Description: When exactly one row has a valid action selected (either Delete or Update), no error conditions are set for multiple selections, and the system proceeds to process the intended action for that single selected row.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has completed examining all rows and has identified the currently selected row number (I-SELECTED)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the current selected row number with the previously stored selected row number from the communication area (WS-CA-ROW-SELECTED)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the current selected row number equals the previously stored row number, the system sets the row-selection-changed flag to NO (unchanged). If the current selected row number differs from the previously stored row number, the system sets the row-selection-changed flag to YES (changed) and updates the stored row number to the new selection. This flag is later used to invalidate PF10 confirmation if the selection changed.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Change in Row Selection Between Screen Submissions
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system compares the currently selected row number with the row number that was selected in the previous screen submission. If the selection has changed, this is recorded so that PF10 confirmation actions can be invalidated when the user changes their selection.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A row on the Transaction Type maintenance screen has an Update action (U) selected by the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system begins the description change detection process for that row
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the initial change detection state to 'No Changes Found' before performing any comparison, ensuring a clean baseline for the comparison logic

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initialize Description Change Detection State
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before comparing the entered transaction description against the stored description for an update-requested row, the system initializes the change detection state to 'No Changes Found' as the default assumption.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A row on the Transaction Type maintenance screen has an Update action (U) selected, and the user has entered a value in the Transaction Description field for that row
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the entered description (from the screen input field WS-ROW-TR-DESC-IN for the selected row) against the stored description (from the communication area WS-CA-ROW-TR-DESC-OUT for the same row)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The comparison must satisfy ALL of the following conditions simultaneously to be considered a match: (1) the trimmed, uppercased content of the entered description equals the trimmed, uppercased content of the stored description, AND (2) the trimmed length of the entered description equals the trimmed length of the stored description; if both conditions are true the descriptions are considered identical, otherwise they are considered different

all_rules.Rule_Name: Compare Entered Description Against Stored Description
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an update is requested on a Transaction Type row, the system performs a precise comparison between the newly entered description and the original stored description. The comparison is case-insensitive, ignores leading and trailing spaces, and validates both the content and the trimmed length of both values to determine if a genuine change has been made.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A row on the Transaction Type maintenance screen has an Update action (U) selected, and the system has performed the case-insensitive trimmed comparison of the entered description against the stored description
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The trimmed uppercased content of the entered description matches the trimmed uppercased content of the stored description AND the trimmed length of the entered description equals the trimmed length of the stored description
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the 'No Changes Detected' message flag (WS-MESG-NO-CHANGES-DETECTED) to inform the user that no changes were made to the description, and immediately exits the description validation process without performing any further validation on the description field

all_rules.Rule_Name: No Changes Detected in Transaction Description
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the entered transaction description is determined to be identical to the stored description (after case-insensitive, trimmed comparison of both content and length), the system flags the situation as 'No Changes Detected' and informs the user that no modifications were made, bypassing further description validation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A row on the Transaction Type maintenance screen has an Update action (U) selected, and the system has performed the case-insensitive trimmed comparison of the entered description against the stored description
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The trimmed uppercased content of the entered description does NOT match the trimmed uppercased content of the stored description, OR the trimmed length of the entered description does NOT equal the trimmed length of the stored description (i.e., at least one of the two comparison conditions fails)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the 'Changes Have Occurred' flag and continues processing to validate the new description value — specifically checking that the Transaction Description field is not blank and contains only alphanumeric characters, with a maximum length of 50 characters

all_rules.Rule_Name: Changes Detected in Transaction Description
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the entered transaction description differs from the stored description (based on case-insensitive, trimmed comparison of content or length), the system flags that changes have occurred and proceeds to validate the new description value for correctness before allowing the update to proceed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has selected the Update action on a transaction type row, and the screen contains the entered description value alongside the previously stored description value for that row
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The entered description, after trimming leading and trailing spaces, matches the stored description (case-insensitive comparison) AND the trimmed length of the entered description equals the trimmed length of the stored description
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the message 'No Changes Detected', skips all further description validation for that row, and proceeds to the next validation step without marking any error

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect No Change in Transaction Description Before Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user selects an Update action on a transaction type row, the system compares the newly entered description against the previously stored description. If no change is detected, validation is skipped and a 'No Changes Detected' message is set.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has selected the Update action on a transaction type row, and the screen contains the entered description value alongside the previously stored description value for that row
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The entered description (trimmed, case-insensitive) does NOT match the stored description, OR the trimmed length of the entered description does NOT equal the trimmed length of the stored description
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks that a change has occurred and proceeds to validate the new description value for blank/empty check and alphanumeric character check

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Change in Transaction Description to Trigger Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user selects an Update action on a transaction type row, if the entered description differs from the stored description, the system marks that a change has occurred and proceeds to validate the new description value.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A change has been detected in the transaction description for a row where the Update action is selected, and the system is performing description validation for the field named 'Transaction Desc' with a maximum length of 50 characters
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The entered description value (up to 50 characters) is entirely blank spaces, low-values (empty binary), OR the trimmed length of the entered description equals zero
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the overall input as invalid, sets the description field status to blank-error, and sets the error message to 'Transaction Desc must be supplied.' The description field is highlighted in red on the screen, and no further alphanumeric validation is performed for this field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reject Blank or Empty Transaction Description on Update
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a change has been detected in the transaction description during an update action, the system validates that the new description is not blank or empty. A description is mandatory and must contain at least one non-space character.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A change has been detected in the transaction description for a row where the Update action is selected, the entered description is not blank or empty, and the system is performing alphanumeric validation for the field named 'Transaction Desc' with a maximum length of 50 characters
Acceptance_Criteria.When: After converting all valid alphanumeric characters (letters and numbers) to spaces within the entered description, the remaining trimmed content is NOT empty — meaning non-alphanumeric characters are present in the description
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the overall input as invalid, sets the description field status to not-ok, and sets the error message to 'Transaction Desc can have numbers or alphabets only.' The description field is highlighted in red on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reject Non-Alphanumeric Characters in Transaction Description on Update
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the entered transaction description is not blank, the system validates that it contains only letters (A-Z, a-z) and numbers (0-9). Special characters, punctuation, and symbols are not permitted in the transaction description.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A change has been detected in the transaction description for a row where the Update action is selected, the entered description is not blank or empty, and the system has performed alphanumeric validation for the field named 'Transaction Desc' with a maximum length of 50 characters
Acceptance_Criteria.When: After converting all valid alphanumeric characters (letters and numbers) to spaces within the entered description, the remaining trimmed content IS empty — meaning the description contains only letters and numbers with no invalid characters
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the description field status as valid (alphanumeric-is-valid), no error message is set, and the description field is not highlighted in red. The validation result is stored back into the row's description validation flags, and processing continues to the next step

all_rules.Rule_Name: Accept Valid Alphanumeric Transaction Description on Update
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the entered transaction description passes both the blank check and the alphanumeric character check, the system marks the description as valid and allows the update process to continue.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type maintenance screen and the Type Code Filter field is available for input
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user submits the screen with the Type Code Filter field left blank, containing only spaces, zeros, or empty (low-values)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the Type Code Filter as blank (no filter active), clears the stored type code filter value to zeros, and proceeds without applying any type code restriction to the transaction type list

all_rules.Rule_Name: Treat Blank or Empty Type Code Filter as No Filter
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user does not enter a Type Code Filter value (leaves it blank, enters zeros, or the field is empty), the system should treat it as if no filter was requested and clear any previously stored type code filter value.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type maintenance screen and has entered a value in the Type Code Filter field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The entered Type Code Filter value is not a numeric value
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the input as invalid, marks the Type Code Filter as invalid (not OK), sets the error message to 'TYPE CODE FILTER, IF SUPPLIED MUST BE A 2 DIGIT NUMBER', protects all row selection fields so no row action can be selected, and stops further processing of the type code filter

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reject Non-Numeric Type Code Filter Value
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user enters a Type Code Filter value that is not numeric, the system must reject it, display a specific error message, and prevent the user from selecting any rows until the filter is corrected.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type maintenance screen and has entered a value in the Type Code Filter field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The entered Type Code Filter value is numeric
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system stores the entered value as the active Type Code Filter and marks the Type Code Filter status as valid

all_rules.Rule_Name: Accept Valid Numeric Type Code Filter Value
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user enters a numeric value in the Type Code Filter field, the system accepts it as a valid filter and stores it for use in filtering the transaction type list.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type maintenance screen and a Type Code Filter value (blank or valid numeric) has been processed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The current Type Code Filter value is different from the previously stored Type Code Filter value — specifically, the new value does not equal the previously saved value, OR the filter is now blank but the previously saved value was not blank, zeros, or empty
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system resets all paging variables to their initial state (so display starts from the first page), saves the new Type Code Filter value as the current filter, and marks the Type Code Filter as changed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reset Paging When Type Code Filter Changes
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user changes the Type Code Filter value from what was previously used, the system must reset the paging position to the beginning of the results and save the new filter value, ensuring the user sees results from the first page with the new filter applied.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type maintenance screen and a Type Code Filter value (blank or valid numeric) has been processed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The current Type Code Filter value is the same as the previously stored value — specifically, the new value equals the previously saved value, OR both the new filter is blank AND the previously saved filter was also blank, zeros, or empty
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the Type Code Filter as not changed and retains the existing paging position without any reset, so the user continues viewing the same page of transaction types

all_rules.Rule_Name: Preserve Paging Position When Type Code Filter Is Unchanged
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user submits the screen without changing the Type Code Filter value from the previously used value, the system preserves the current paging position so the user remains on the same page of results.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type list screen and the new Type Code filter input field is blank (empty, low-values, or zeros), AND the previously stored Type Code filter value in the session is also blank (zeros, low-values, or spaces)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates whether the Type Code filter has changed after the user submits the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the Type Code filter status as UNCHANGED, and no paging variables are reset, allowing the current page position to be preserved

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect No Change When Both New and Previously Stored Type Code Filters Are Blank
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user leaves the Type Code filter field empty and no Type Code filter was previously stored in the session, the system recognises that no filter change has occurred and does not reset paging.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type list screen and has entered a Type Code filter value, AND the previously stored Type Code filter value in the session is not blank
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the newly entered Type Code filter value against the previously stored Type Code filter value in the session
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the new value is identical to the stored value, the system marks the Type Code filter status as UNCHANGED and no paging variables are reset, preserving the current page position

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect No Change When New Type Code Filter Value Is Identical to Previously Stored Filter Value
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user enters a Type Code filter value that is exactly the same as the one already stored in the session from the previous screen interaction, the system recognises no filter change has occurred and preserves the current page position.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type list screen and either both the new and previously stored Type Code filter values are blank, OR the new Type Code filter value is identical to the previously stored value
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system completes the Type Code filter change detection logic
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the Type Code filter change flag to UNCHANGED (FLG-TYPEFILTER-CHANGED-NO), and the current page number and paging position variables remain unaffected

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark Type Code Filter as Unchanged When No New Filter Is Applied
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Type Code filter has not changed (either both are blank or the values are identical), the system explicitly marks the filter status as unchanged so that downstream processing knows not to reset paging or re-query data.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type list screen and has entered a Type Code filter value that is different from the previously stored Type Code filter value in the session
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system detects that the Type Code filter value has changed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system resets all paging variables (WS-CA-PAGING-VARIABLES) to their initial state, so that the next data retrieval will start from the first page of results matching the new filter

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reset Paging Variables When a New Type Code Filter Is Applied
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user applies a different Type Code filter value than what was previously stored, the system resets all paging variables so that the result list restarts from the first page, ensuring the user sees results relevant to the new filter from the beginning.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type list screen and has entered a Type Code filter value that is different from the previously stored Type Code filter value
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system detects the Type Code filter has changed and resets paging variables
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system saves the newly entered Type Code filter value (WS-IN-TYPE-CD) into the session storage field (WS-CA-TYPE-CD) so that it becomes the reference value for future change detection on subsequent screen submissions

all_rules.Rule_Name: Save New Type Code Filter Value to Session Storage
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a new and different Type Code filter value is detected, the system saves the new filter value into the session communication area so it can be compared against future screen submissions to detect further changes.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type list screen and has entered a Type Code filter value that differs from the previously stored value, AND the paging variables have been reset and the new filter value has been saved to session storage
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system completes the Type Code filter change detection logic
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the Type Code filter change flag to CHANGED (FLG-TYPEFILTER-CHANGED-YES), which signals to subsequent processing steps that row selections should be cleared and data should be re-queried from the beginning using the new filter value

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark Type Code Filter as Changed When a New Filter Value Is Applied
all_rules.Rule_Description: After detecting that the Type Code filter value has changed, resetting paging, and saving the new value, the system explicitly marks the filter status as CHANGED so that downstream processing (such as clearing row selections and re-querying data) is triggered appropriately.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type maintenance screen and the Description Filter input field (WS-IN-TYPE-DESC) is either empty, contains only spaces, or contains low-values (no value entered)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system validates the Description Filter input
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Description Filter is marked as Blank (FLG-DESCFILTER-BLANK = TRUE), no description filter is applied to the data query, and all transaction type records are eligible to be displayed without any description-based restriction

all_rules.Rule_Name: Description Filter Treated as Blank When Not Supplied
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user does not enter a description filter value (leaves it empty or blank), the system treats the description filter as not active, meaning no filtering by description will be applied and all transaction type records will be eligible for display.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type maintenance screen and the Description Filter input field (WS-IN-TYPE-DESC) contains a non-blank, non-empty value
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system validates the Description Filter input
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Description Filter is marked as Valid (FLG-DESCFILTER-ISVALID = TRUE), indicating that a description-based filter should be applied when retrieving transaction type records

all_rules.Rule_Name: Description Filter Marked as Valid When Value Is Supplied
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user enters a description filter value, the system recognizes it as a valid filter input and marks it accordingly so that subsequent processing can apply the filter to the transaction type search.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has entered a description filter value and the Description Filter has been marked as Valid (FLG-DESCFILTER-ISVALID = TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the description filter for use in the data query
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system constructs the filter value by concatenating a '%' wildcard character, followed by the trimmed user-entered description text, followed by another '%' wildcard character (format: %entered-value%), and stores this formatted value in WS-TYPE-DESC-FILTER for use in the LIKE search against the TR_DESCRIPTION column of the Transaction Type table

all_rules.Rule_Name: Description Filter Wrapped with Wildcard Characters for Partial Match Search
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a valid description filter value has been entered by the user, the system automatically wraps the entered value with wildcard characters (%) at both the beginning and end, enabling a partial/contains match search so that any transaction type whose description contains the entered text will be returned.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Description Filter validation has completed and the system has a previously stored description filter value (WS-CA-TYPE-DESC) from the prior screen interaction
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the current description filter input (WS-IN-TYPE-DESC) with the previously stored value (WS-CA-TYPE-DESC)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the current input equals the previously stored value, OR if the current filter is blank AND the previously stored value was also blank (empty, spaces, or low-values), then the Description Filter is marked as NOT changed (FLG-DESCFILTER-CHANGED-NO = TRUE) and paging state is preserved; otherwise the Description Filter is marked as CHANGED (FLG-DESCFILTER-CHANGED-YES = TRUE)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Description Filter Change Detection Against Previous Value
all_rules.Rule_Description: After validating the description filter, the system compares the newly entered filter value against the previously stored filter value to determine whether the user has changed the filter. This is used to decide whether paging state needs to be reset and whether row selections should be cleared.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has detected that the current description filter input (WS-IN-TYPE-DESC) is different from the previously stored description filter value (WS-CA-TYPE-DESC), meaning the user has modified the description filter
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the description filter change
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system resets all paging variables (WS-CA-PAGING-VARIABLES is initialized to starting values), saves the new description filter value (WS-IN-TYPE-DESC is moved to WS-CA-TYPE-DESC), and marks the Description Filter as Changed (FLG-DESCFILTER-CHANGED-YES = TRUE) so that the display will restart from the first page with the new filter applied

all_rules.Rule_Name: Paging State Reset When Description Filter Changes
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user changes the description filter value from what was previously used, the system resets the paging position back to the beginning and saves the new filter value, ensuring that the results displayed reflect the new filter criteria starting from the first page.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has previously applied a description filter value stored in the session (WS-CA-TYPE-DESC), and the screen currently displays a page of transaction type results at a specific page position
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user submits the screen with a description filter value (WS-IN-TYPE-DESC) that is exactly equal to the previously stored description filter value (WS-CA-TYPE-DESC)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The description filter is marked as NOT CHANGED (FLG-DESCFILTER-CHANGED-NO is set to TRUE), the existing paging position is preserved, and the system proceeds to filter cross-validation without resetting to the first page

all_rules.Rule_Name: Description Filter Unchanged When Values Match
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user submits a description filter value that is identical to the previously stored description filter, the system recognizes no change has occurred and retains the current paging position without resetting to the first page.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has not previously applied any description filter (the stored description filter value WS-CA-TYPE-DESC is either empty/blank spaces or uninitialized/low-values), and the screen currently displays a page of transaction type results at a specific page position
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user submits the screen with a blank description filter (FLG-DESCFILTER-BLANK is TRUE, meaning WS-IN-TYPE-DESC contains only spaces or low-values) AND the previously stored description filter (WS-CA-TYPE-DESC) is also blank (equal to LOW-VALUES or SPACES)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The description filter is marked as NOT CHANGED (FLG-DESCFILTER-CHANGED-NO is set to TRUE), the existing paging position is preserved, and the system proceeds to filter cross-validation without resetting to the first page

all_rules.Rule_Name: Description Filter Unchanged When Both Current and Previous Filters Are Blank
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user submits a blank description filter and the previously stored description filter was also blank (empty or unset), the system treats this as no change and retains the current paging position.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has previously applied a description filter value stored in the session (WS-CA-TYPE-DESC), and the screen currently displays a page of transaction type results at a specific page position
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user submits the screen with a description filter value (WS-IN-TYPE-DESC) that is neither equal to the previously stored filter value (WS-CA-TYPE-DESC) nor a blank-to-blank transition (i.e., the new and old values are genuinely different)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The description filter is marked as CHANGED (FLG-DESCFILTER-CHANGED-YES is set to TRUE), all paging variables (WS-CA-PAGING-VARIABLES) are reset so the display returns to the first page of results, and the new description filter value (WS-IN-TYPE-DESC) is saved to session storage (WS-CA-TYPE-DESC) for future comparison, after which the system proceeds to filter cross-validation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Description Filter Changed - Reset Paging and Save New Filter Value
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user submits a description filter value that is genuinely different from the previously stored filter (not a blank-to-blank transition and not an identical value), the system marks the filter as changed, resets all paging variables to return to the first page of results, and saves the new filter value for future comparison.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Transaction Type maintenance screen and has not entered any value in the Type Code filter field and has not entered any value in the Description filter field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates whether cross-validation of filters is required
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system skips the filter cross-validation step entirely and proceeds without querying the Transaction Type table for a record count

all_rules.Rule_Name: Skip Filter Cross-Validation When No Filters Are Supplied
all_rules.Rule_Description: Filter cross-validation against the Transaction Type table is only triggered when at least one filter (Type Code or Description) has been supplied and validated as a valid input. If neither filter is active, the cross-validation step is bypassed entirely.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has supplied at least one valid filter — either a Type Code filter or a Description filter — on the Transaction Type maintenance screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system performs cross-validation of the supplied filter conditions
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system executes a COUNT query against the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table applying the following conditions: if the Type Code filter is active (type flag = '1'), only records where TR_TYPE exactly equals the supplied type code are counted; if the Description filter is active (description flag = '1'), only records where TR_DESCRIPTION matches the supplied description text using a partial (LIKE) search are counted; both conditions are applied simultaneously when both filters are active; the resulting count is stored for subsequent validation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Query Transaction Type Table to Count Records Matching Active Filters
all_rules.Rule_Description: When at least one filter is active and valid, the system queries the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table to count how many records satisfy the supplied filter conditions. The Type Code filter applies an exact match on TR_TYPE, and the Description filter applies a partial (LIKE) match on TR_DESCRIPTION. Each filter is only applied when its corresponding flag indicates it is active.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has supplied a Type Code filter value that passed individual field validation, and the system has queried the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table using the active filter conditions
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The count of matching records returned by the query is zero AND the Type Code filter was supplied and marked as valid
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the Type Code filter field as invalid (FLG-TYPEFILTER-NOT-OK) and sets the overall input status to error, indicating that the Type Code filter value produced no matching transaction type records

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark Type Code Filter as Invalid When No Matching Records Found
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the count query returns zero matching records and the Type Code filter was supplied and valid, the Type Code filter field is marked as invalid to indicate to the user that the entered type code produced no results.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has supplied a Description filter value that passed individual field validation, and the system has queried the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table using the active filter conditions
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The count of matching records returned by the query is zero AND the Description filter was supplied and marked as valid
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the Description filter field as invalid (FLG-DESCFILTER-NOT-OK) and sets the overall input status to error, indicating that the Description filter value produced no matching transaction type records

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark Description Filter as Invalid When No Matching Records Found
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the count query returns zero matching records and the Description filter was supplied and valid, the Description filter field is marked as invalid to indicate to the user that the entered description text produced no results.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has determined that no records in the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table match the supplied filter conditions
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The count of matching records is zero
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the row protection flag (FLG-PROTECT-SELECT-ROWS-YES) to true, which causes all row selection fields on the screen to be rendered as protected and non-enterable, preventing the user from performing any row-level actions such as update or delete

all_rules.Rule_Name: Protect All Row Selection Fields When Filter Conditions Return No Records
all_rules.Rule_Description: When no records are found matching the supplied filter conditions, all row selection fields on the screen are locked (protected) to prevent the user from attempting to select, update, or delete any rows while the filter is in an error state.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has evaluated the supplied filter conditions against the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table and found zero matching records
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The count of matching records is zero after querying with the active Type Code filter and/or Description filter
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error message to 'No Records found for these filter conditions' and displays it on the screen, and the overall input validation status is set to error so that no further processing of row actions is performed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Error Message When No Records Found for Filter Conditions
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the filter cross-validation determines that no records exist in the Transaction Type table matching the supplied filter criteria, a specific error message is set to inform the user that their filter conditions produced no results.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has supplied at least one valid filter — either a Type Code filter or a Description filter — on the Transaction Type maintenance screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The count of records in CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE matching the supplied filter conditions is greater than zero
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system considers the filter cross-validation as passed, does not set any filter error flags, does not protect row selection fields, and proceeds to retrieve and display the matching transaction type records on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Proceed with Filtered Results When Matching Records Exist
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the count query confirms that at least one record exists in the Transaction Type table matching the supplied filter conditions, the cross-validation passes and the system proceeds to display the filtered transaction type records.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has pressed any key on the Transaction Type Maintenance screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program begins processing the key press
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The key is immediately marked as INVALID before any further validation is performed, ensuring no key is permitted by default

all_rules.Rule_Name: Default All Key Presses to Invalid Before Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before any key validation logic is applied, every key press is initially marked as invalid. This ensures that only explicitly permitted keys are allowed to proceed, and no key is assumed valid by default.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Transaction Type Maintenance screen and presses a key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program reads the key press from the terminal interface
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program records the logical key as one of: ENTER, PF2, PF3, PF4, PF5, PF6, PF7, PF8, PF9, PF10, PF11, PF12 — where PF13 through PF24 are treated as equivalent to PF1 through PF12 respectively — and sets the corresponding key indicator flag to TRUE

all_rules.Rule_Name: Recognize and Record the Function Key Pressed by the User
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program identifies which physical key the user pressed and records it as a logical key indicator. Keys PF13–PF24 are treated as equivalents to PF1–PF12 respectively, so the same logical action is triggered regardless of which shift-key variant is used.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Transaction Type Maintenance screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses the ENTER key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The key is marked as VALID and processing proceeds with the ENTER action

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark ENTER Key as a Valid and Permitted Action
all_rules.Rule_Description: The ENTER key is always a permitted key on the Transaction Type Maintenance screen and is unconditionally marked as valid when pressed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Transaction Type Maintenance screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses PF2
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The key is marked as VALID and processing proceeds to navigate to the Add New Transaction Type screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark PF2 as Valid to Navigate to Add Transaction Type Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: PF2 is always a permitted key on the Transaction Type Maintenance screen. When pressed, it is marked as valid and the program proceeds to navigate the user to the Add New Transaction Type screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Transaction Type Maintenance screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses PF3
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The key is marked as VALID and processing proceeds to exit to the calling program or Admin menu

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark PF3 as Valid to Exit to Main Menu
all_rules.Rule_Description: PF3 is always a permitted key on the Transaction Type Maintenance screen. When pressed, it is marked as valid and the program proceeds to navigate the user back to the calling program or Admin menu.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Transaction Type Maintenance screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses PF7
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The key is marked as VALID and processing proceeds to display the previous page of transaction type records

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark PF7 as Valid to Navigate to Previous Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: PF7 is always a permitted key on the Transaction Type Maintenance screen. When pressed, it is marked as valid and the program proceeds to scroll backward to the previous page of transaction types.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Transaction Type Maintenance screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses PF8
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The key is marked as VALID and processing proceeds to display the next page of transaction type records

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark PF8 as Valid to Navigate to Next Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: PF8 is always a permitted key on the Transaction Type Maintenance screen. When pressed, it is marked as valid and the program proceeds to scroll forward to the next page of transaction types.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Transaction Type Maintenance screen and has previously selected the Delete action (D) on a transaction type row and pressed ENTER to initiate the confirmation step
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses PF10
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The key is marked as VALID because a delete action is pending, and processing proceeds to execute the deletion of the selected transaction type

all_rules.Rule_Name: Allow PF10 Only When a Delete Action is Pending Confirmation
all_rules.Rule_Description: PF10 is a conditional key. It is only permitted when the user has previously selected a Delete action on a transaction type row and is now confirming that deletion. If a delete is pending, PF10 is marked as valid.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Transaction Type Maintenance screen and has previously selected the Update action (U) on a transaction type row and pressed ENTER to initiate the confirmation step
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses PF10
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The key is marked as VALID because an update action is pending, and processing proceeds to execute the update of the selected transaction type's description

all_rules.Rule_Name: Allow PF10 Only When an Update Action is Pending Confirmation
all_rules.Rule_Description: PF10 is a conditional key. It is only permitted when the user has previously selected an Update action on a transaction type row and is now confirming that update. If an update is pending, PF10 is marked as valid.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Transaction Type Maintenance screen and no delete or update action has been previously selected and initiated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses PF10
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: PF10 is treated as an invalid key in the current context, the key indicator is overridden to ENTER, and the screen is refreshed as if the user pressed ENTER with no action pending

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reject PF10 When No Delete or Update Action is Pending
all_rules.Rule_Description: PF10 is not permitted when neither a delete nor an update action is currently pending. In this context, pressing PF10 has no special meaning and is treated as if the user pressed ENTER, preventing accidental confirmations.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Transaction Type Maintenance screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses any key other than ENTER, PF2, PF3, PF7, PF8, or PF10 (with a pending delete or update) — for example PF1, PF4, PF5, PF6, PF9, PF11, PF12, PA1, PA2, or CLEAR
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The key is marked as INVALID, the key indicator is overridden and set to ENTER, and the screen is refreshed as if the user pressed ENTER

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reject Any Unrecognized Key and Treat as ENTER
all_rules.Rule_Description: Any key press that is not one of the explicitly permitted keys (ENTER, PF2, PF3, PF7, PF8, or PF10 with a pending action) is not a valid action on this screen. Such key presses are silently treated as ENTER to prevent unexpected behavior.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has pressed a key on the Transaction Type Maintenance screen and the key has passed all validation checks and is marked as VALID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Key validation is complete
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program proceeds to execute the business action associated with the validated key: ENTER submits the screen, PF2 navigates to Add Transaction Type, PF3 exits to the menu, PF7 scrolls to the previous page, PF8 scrolls to the next page, and PF10 confirms the pending delete or update action

all_rules.Rule_Name: Proceed with Processing After Key Validation is Complete
all_rules.Rule_Description: Once a key has been determined to be valid — either because it is an unconditionally permitted key or because the conditional requirements for PF10 are met — the program proceeds to execute the corresponding business action for that key.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type Maintenance screen and presses PF3 to exit
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The originating transaction ID is empty, blank, or is the same as the current Transaction Type Maintenance transaction ID
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The destination transaction is set to the Administration Menu transaction ID; otherwise, the destination transaction is set to the originating transaction ID that launched this screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Determine Destination Transaction When PF3 is Pressed
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF3 to exit, the system determines which transaction to return to. If the session was started directly, started from the same transaction, or no originating transaction is recorded, the system defaults to the Administration Menu transaction. Otherwise, it returns to the originating transaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type Maintenance screen and presses PF3 to exit, and the destination transaction has already been determined
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The originating program name is empty, blank, or is the same as the current Transaction Type Maintenance program name
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The destination program is set to the Administration Menu program; otherwise, the destination program is set to the originating program that launched this screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Determine Destination Program When PF3 is Pressed
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF3 to exit, the system determines which program to transfer control to. If the session was started directly, started from the same program, or no originating program is recorded, the system defaults to the Administration Menu program. Otherwise, it returns to the originating program.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF3 and the destination transaction and program have been determined
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system is preparing to transfer control to the destination program
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The communication area is updated with: the current Transaction Type Maintenance transaction ID as the originating transaction, the current Transaction Type Maintenance program name as the originating program, user type set to Admin, program state set to Entering, and the current map name and mapset name recorded

all_rules.Rule_Name: Update Communication Area Context Before Exiting via PF3
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before transferring control to the destination program, the communication area must be updated to record the current program as the originator, set the user type to Admin, mark the program state as entering, and record the current map and mapset names so the destination program has accurate context about where the user came from.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF3, the destination has been determined, and the communication area has been updated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system is about to transfer control to the destination program
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: A synchronization point (commit) is issued to permanently save any pending database changes before the program transfer occurs

all_rules.Rule_Name: Commit Pending Changes Before Exiting via PF3
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before transferring control to the destination program when PF3 is pressed, all pending database changes must be committed to ensure data consistency. This commit occurs prior to the program transfer so that no uncommitted work is carried over to the next program.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF3, the destination program has been determined, the communication area has been updated with current context, and pending changes have been committed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the program transfer
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Control is transferred to the destination program with the updated communication area passed along, and the Administration Menu screen (or originating program screen) is displayed to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transfer Control to Destination Program When PF3 is Pressed
all_rules.Rule_Description: After committing pending changes and updating the communication area, the system transfers control to the determined destination program (either the Administration Menu program or the originating program), passing the updated communication area so the destination program has full context of the user session.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user presses PF3 to exit the Transaction Type Maintenance screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The originating transaction ID is empty, contains only spaces, or matches the current Transaction Type Maintenance transaction ID, AND the originating program name is empty, contains only spaces, or matches the current Transaction Type Maintenance program name
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The destination transaction is set to the Administration Menu transaction ID and the destination program is set to the Administration Menu program name

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Destination to Administration Menu When No Valid Originator Exists
all_rules.Rule_Description: When PF3 is pressed and the session has no valid originating transaction or program (i.e., the user started the session directly or from the same transaction/program), the system defaults both the destination transaction and destination program to the Administration Menu, ensuring the user always has a valid return destination.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user presses PF3 to exit the Transaction Type Maintenance screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The originating transaction ID is not empty, not blank, and does not match the current Transaction Type Maintenance transaction ID, AND the originating program name is not empty, not blank, and does not match the current Transaction Type Maintenance program name
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The destination transaction is set to the originating transaction ID and the destination program is set to the originating program name that originally launched the Transaction Type Maintenance screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Use Originating Transaction and Program as Return Destination
all_rules.Rule_Description: When PF3 is pressed and the session was launched from another transaction and program, the system uses the recorded originating transaction ID and program name as the return destination, ensuring the user is returned to exactly where they came from.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is interacting with the Transaction Type maintenance application and presses the PF2 key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates whether the currently active program is the Transaction Type List program (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM equals LIT-THISPGM)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the current program IS the Transaction Type List program, the system proceeds with navigation to the Add Transaction Type screen. If the current program is NOT the Transaction Type List program, no navigation action is taken and the current screen remains unchanged.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Restrict PF2 Navigation to Add Screen Only When on Transaction Type List
all_rules.Rule_Description: PF2 key to navigate to the Add Transaction Type screen is only honored when the user is currently active on the Transaction Type List program. If PF2 is pressed from any other context, no navigation action is taken.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF2 and the system has confirmed the current active program is the Transaction Type List program
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to navigate to the Add Transaction Type screen
