Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system records the current Transaction Type List transaction ID (LIT-THISTRANID) as the originating transaction ID (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID), records the current Transaction Type List program name (LIT-THISPGM) as the originating program (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM), records the current mapset (LIT-THISMAPSET) as the last used mapset (CDEMO-LAST-MAPSET), and records the current map (LIT-THISMAP) as the last used map (CDEMO-LAST-MAP) in the communication area.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Record Current Program and Transaction Context Before Navigating Away
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before transferring control to the Add Transaction Type screen, the system records the current transaction ID, program name, mapset, and map in the communication area so that the destination program knows where to return upon completion.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF2 and the system has confirmed the current active program is the Transaction Type List program
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the session context for transfer to the Add Transaction Type screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the user type to regular user (CDEMO-USRTYP-USER = TRUE) and sets the program mode to initial entry (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER = TRUE) in the communication area.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set User Type to Regular User When Navigating to Add Transaction Type Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: When navigating to the Add Transaction Type screen via PF2, the user context is set to regular user type (not admin), and the program entry mode is set to initial entry.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF2, the current program is confirmed as the Transaction Type List program, and the return navigation context has been recorded
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets up the destination for the screen transfer
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the destination program to the Add Transaction Type program (LIT-ADDTPGM stored in CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM), sets the next mapset to the Add Transaction Type mapset (LIT-ADDTMAPSET stored in CCARD-NEXT-MAPSET), and sets the next map to the Add Transaction Type map (LIT-ADDTMAP stored in CCARD-NEXT-MAP).

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Destination Program and Map Details for Add Transaction Type Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system designates the Add/Update Transaction Type program as the navigation destination, along with its associated map and mapset identifiers, so the correct screen is displayed upon transfer.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The destination program has been set to the Add Transaction Type program, the return navigation context has been recorded, and the user type has been set to regular user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the transfer of control
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the exit message indicator (WS-EXIT-MESSAGE = TRUE), sets program entry mode to initial entry (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER = TRUE), and transfers control to the Add Transaction Type program (LIT-ADDTPGM) passing the full communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) so the destination program receives all session context. Control does not return to the Transaction Type List program.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transfer Control to Add Transaction Type Screen with Session Context
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system transfers full control to the Add Transaction Type program, passing the complete session communication area so that the destination program has all necessary context including user identity, return navigation details, and program state.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is viewing a page of transaction type records and a next page exists beyond the current display
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses PF8 to scroll forward to the next page
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the start key for the next database read to the last transaction type code that was displayed on the current page, ensuring the next page begins immediately after the current page's last record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Start Key to Last Transaction Code of Current Page for Forward Navigation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF8 to navigate to the next page, the system uses the last transaction type code displayed on the current page as the starting point for reading the next set of records.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on a page of transaction type records and presses PF8 to go to the next page
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The forward paging operation is triggered
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The page number counter is increased by exactly 1, and the updated page number is displayed on the screen to inform the user of their current position in the result set

all_rules.Rule_Name: Increment Page Number When Navigating Forward
all_rules.Rule_Description: Each time the user navigates forward to the next page, the current page number is incremented by 1 to reflect the new page position in the result set.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen currently displays transaction type records from the previous page
Acceptance_Criteria.When: A forward page read operation is initiated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All existing row data (transaction type codes and descriptions) stored for screen display are cleared to empty/low values before any new records are fetched from the database

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear All Screen Row Data Before Loading New Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before reading and displaying a new page of transaction type records, all previously displayed row data on the screen must be cleared to prevent stale data from appearing alongside new records.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user may have had row selections (delete or update flags) set on the current page
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses PF8 and the system moves to the next page
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All row selection flags are reset to blank/empty, ensuring no prior page selections are retained on the new page

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Row Selection Flags When Moving to Next Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user navigates to the next page, any previously selected row actions (delete or update selections) from the prior page are cleared so that no unintended actions carry over to the new page.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A start key has been set to the last transaction type code of the current page, and optional filters for type code and/or description may be active
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The forward reading cursor is opened against the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system retrieves records where the transaction type code is greater than or equal to the start key, AND if the type code filter is active, only records with an exact match on the type code are included, AND if the description filter is active, only records whose description contains the filter text (partial match) are included, with results ordered ascending by transaction type code

all_rules.Rule_Name: Read Transaction Type Records Forward from Start Key with Active Filters
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system reads transaction type records from the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table in ascending order by transaction type code, starting from the specified start key, and applies any active type code or description filters.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The forward reading cursor has been opened and records are being fetched
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The first record is successfully fetched from the database (row counter equals 1)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The transaction type code of that first record is stored as the first transaction type code for the current page, and if the page number is currently zero it is set to 1

all_rules.Rule_Name: Store First Transaction Type Code of New Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: The transaction type code of the very first record fetched for a new page is stored as the first key of that page, enabling backward navigation to return to this page later.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The forward reading cursor is open and records are being fetched from CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE
Acceptance_Criteria.When: A record is successfully fetched (transaction type code and description are returned)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The row counter is incremented by 1, the transaction type code is stored in the corresponding screen row position, and the transaction type description text is stored in the corresponding screen row position, continuing until either no more records exist or 7 rows have been filled

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Screen Rows with Fetched Transaction Type Records Up to Maximum of 7
all_rules.Rule_Description: Each successfully fetched transaction type record is added to the screen display, storing both the transaction type code and its description, until the maximum number of displayable rows (7) is reached.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Records are being fetched from the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table and added to screen rows
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The row counter reaches the maximum screen lines value of 7
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The fetch loop is flagged to exit, the transaction type code of the 7th record is stored as the last transaction type code of the current page, and the system proceeds to perform an extra fetch to determine if additional pages exist

all_rules.Rule_Name: Stop Reading After Maximum 7 Rows Are Filled
all_rules.Rule_Description: The screen can display a maximum of 7 transaction type records per page. Once 7 rows have been populated, the system stops the main fetch loop regardless of how many more records may exist in the database.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen has been filled with the maximum 7 transaction type records
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The 7th record is added to the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The transaction type code of the 7th (last) record is stored as the last transaction type code for the current page, to be used as the starting point if the user presses PF8 again

all_rules.Rule_Name: Store Last Transaction Type Code of Current Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the maximum number of rows for a page is reached, the transaction type code of the last displayed record is stored as the last key of the current page, which will serve as the start key for the next forward page navigation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All 7 screen rows have been filled with transaction type records
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system performs one additional fetch from the forward reading cursor
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If an additional record is found, the system marks that more pages exist and updates the last transaction type code to this extra record's type code; if no additional record is found (end of data), the system marks that no more pages exist

all_rules.Rule_Name: Perform Extra Fetch to Determine if Additional Pages Exist
all_rules.Rule_Description: After filling all 7 screen rows, the system performs one additional database fetch beyond the displayed records to determine whether more transaction type records exist, enabling the system to correctly indicate whether further forward paging is possible.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All 7 screen rows have been filled and an extra fetch has been performed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The extra fetch returns a valid record (more data exists in the database beyond the current page)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the next-page-exists indicator to TRUE and stores the extra fetched record's transaction type code as the new last transaction type code for the current page, so that the next PF8 press will start from the correct position

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark Next Page as Available When More Records Exist Beyond Current Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the extra fetch after filling 7 rows returns a record, the system marks that a next page is available, allowing the user to continue pressing PF8 to see more transaction type records.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All 7 screen rows have been filled and an extra fetch has been performed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The extra fetch returns no record (end of data reached, SQL code +100)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the next-page-does-not-exist indicator to TRUE, and if the user pressed PF8 to get here, a message is set to inform the user that no more records are available

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark No More Pages When End of Data Reached After Full Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the extra fetch after filling 7 rows returns no record, the system marks that the current page is the last page and no further forward navigation is possible.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The forward reading cursor is open and records are being fetched to fill screen rows
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The database returns end-of-data (no more records) before 7 rows are filled
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the next-page-does-not-exist indicator to TRUE, stores the last fetched transaction type code as the last key, and if the user pressed PF8 to trigger this read, a message is set indicating no more records are available

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark No More Pages When End of Data Reached During Page Fill
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the database returns no more records before all 7 screen rows are filled, the system marks that no further pages exist and the current page is the last page.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The forward reading cursor has been opened and a fetch is attempted on page 1
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The database returns no records at all (end-of-data on the very first fetch, row counter is zero, and screen number is 1)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the no-records-found message indicator so that the screen displays a message informing the user that no transaction type records exist for the current filter conditions

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display No Records Found Message When Zero Records Returned on First Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the database returns no records at all when reading the first page (page number equals 1 and row count is zero), the system displays a message informing the user that no transaction type records were found matching the current search conditions.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The forward read operation has completed and screen rows have been populated with transaction type records
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The send map operation is executed to display the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen is displayed to the user showing up to 7 rows of transaction type data, each row containing the transaction type code and its description, along with the current page number, date, time, and any applicable informational messages

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Up to 7 Transaction Type Records on List Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: After reading records from the database, the system sends the screen to the user displaying up to 7 transaction type records, each showing the transaction type code and its description.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is viewing a page of Transaction Type records and presses PF7 to navigate to the previous page
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The backward paging process is initiated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All currently displayed row data (Transaction Type Codes and Descriptions for all rows) in the display area are cleared before any new records are loaded

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Display Area Before Loading Previous Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before reading and displaying the previous page of transaction type records, all currently displayed row data must be cleared to ensure no stale data remains on screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The backward paging process has been initiated and the display area has been cleared
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to fetch records from the database in descending order
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The row position counter is set to the maximum number of screen rows (7), so that the first record fetched is placed in the last row position and subsequent records fill upward toward row 1

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initialize Row Counter to Maximum for Bottom-Up Fill
all_rules.Rule_Description: When reading records in reverse order (descending by Type Code), the row counter must be initialized to the maximum number of displayable rows (7) so that records are placed from the bottom of the screen upward, resulting in correct top-to-bottom ascending order when displayed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is preparing to display the previous page of Transaction Type records, and the current page's first Transaction Type Code (start key) is known, and optional Type Code filter and/or Description filter may be active
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The backward database cursor is opened against the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The cursor retrieves records where the Transaction Type Code is strictly LESS THAN the current page's first Transaction Type Code, AND if the Type Code filter is active, only records with an exact match on Transaction Type Code are included, AND if the Description filter is active, only records whose Description contains the filter text (partial match) are included, AND all qualifying records are ordered by Transaction Type Code in DESCENDING order

all_rules.Rule_Name: Open Backward Database Cursor with Filter Conditions
all_rules.Rule_Description: The backward cursor must be opened to retrieve Transaction Type records that come before the current page's first record, applying any active Type Code or Description filters, and ordering results in descending Type Code order to enable bottom-up screen filling.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The backward database cursor has been successfully opened and the row counter is positioned at the current fill position
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system fetches the next record from the backward cursor
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Type Code (TR_TYPE) and Transaction Type Description (TR_DESCRIPTION) are retrieved from the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table for the current record in the result set

all_rules.Rule_Name: Fetch Each Record from Backward Cursor
all_rules.Rule_Description: Each record is fetched one at a time from the backward cursor, retrieving the Transaction Type Code and Description for placement into the display rows.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A record has been successfully fetched from the backward cursor (fetch returned a valid record)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The fetched record data is placed into the display area
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The fetched Transaction Type Code is stored in the current row position's Type Code output field, AND the fetched Transaction Type Description text is stored in the current row position's Description output field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Fill Current Row Position with Fetched Record Data
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a record is successfully fetched from the backward cursor, its Transaction Type Code and Description are stored into the current row position of the display area.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A fetched record has been successfully placed into the current row position in the display area
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system advances to the next row position
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The row position counter is decremented by 1, moving the fill position one row upward toward row 1

all_rules.Rule_Name: Move Row Position Upward After Each Record Placed
all_rules.Rule_Description: After placing a fetched record into the current row position, the row counter is decremented by 1 to move the fill position one row upward, enabling the next fetched record to be placed in the row above.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A record has been placed into a row position and the row counter has been decremented
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates whether the page is full
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the row counter equals zero, the page is considered full and the fetch loop is exited; if the row counter is greater than zero, the system continues fetching the next record to fill the next row upward

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect When All Display Rows Are Filled
all_rules.Rule_Description: After each record is placed and the row counter is decremented, the system checks whether all available display rows have been filled (row counter reaches zero), which signals that the page is complete.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The row counter has reached zero, indicating all display rows have been filled with records fetched in descending order
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system records the page boundary key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Type Code of the record just placed into row position 1 (the last record fetched that caused the counter to reach zero) is saved as the new First Transaction Type Code for the current page

all_rules.Rule_Name: Save First Transaction Type Code of the New Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: When all 7 rows have been filled (row counter reaches zero), the Transaction Type Code of the last record placed (which is the topmost row on screen after display) is saved as the new first key of the page, enabling correct forward and backward navigation from this page.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF7 to navigate to the previous page AND the current page is NOT the first page
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The backward read operation is performed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current page number is decremented by 1 before the backward read is executed, so the displayed page number correctly reflects the previous page

all_rules.Rule_Name: Decrement Page Number When Navigating Backward
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user navigates to the previous page using PF7 and the current page is not the first page, the page number displayed on screen is decremented by 1 to reflect the correct page position.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The backward cursor has been opened and the system is fetching records to fill the display rows
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The backward cursor returns no more records (end of result set reached before all rows are filled)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The fetch loop is immediately exited, and the page is displayed with only the rows that were successfully populated; any remaining row positions stay empty

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle No More Records Available During Backward Read
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the backward cursor returns no more records before all display rows are filled, the fetch loop is exited and the page is displayed with however many rows were successfully populated.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The backward fetch loop has completed, either because all display rows were filled or because no more records were available in the cursor
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system finalizes the backward read operation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The backward database cursor (C-TR-TYPE-BACKWARD) is closed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Close Backward Cursor After Page Read Completes
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the backward fetch loop completes (either all rows filled or no more records), the backward database cursor must be closed to release database resources.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The backward read has completed and the previous page records have been loaded into the display area
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to display the previous page
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All row selection flags for every display row are cleared (reset to blank/no action) before the page is sent to the screen, ensuring no action selections from the previous page view are retained

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Row Selections When Navigating to Previous Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user navigates to the previous page, all previously entered row action selections (Delete or Update flags) are cleared so that no prior selections carry over to the newly displayed page.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Records have been fetched in descending Transaction Type Code order and placed into display rows from the bottom row upward (row 7 down to row 1)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The completed page is sent to the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The records appear on screen in ascending Transaction Type Code order from top (row 1) to bottom (row 7), because the bottom-up fill of descending records naturally produces ascending top-to-bottom display order

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Previous Page Records in Ascending Type Code Order
all_rules.Rule_Description: Although records are fetched from the database in descending order and placed into the display area from bottom to top, the final display presents the records in ascending Transaction Type Code order from top to bottom, providing a consistent and intuitive view to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user presses PF7 to navigate to the previous page and the current page's first Transaction Type Code is stored as the start key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets up the backward cursor query
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The backward cursor retrieves only records where the Transaction Type Code is strictly LESS THAN (not equal to) the current page's first Transaction Type Code, so the current page's records are excluded from the previous page results

all_rules.Rule_Name: Use Current Page First Key as Backward Read Boundary
all_rules.Rule_Description: The backward navigation uses the first Transaction Type Code currently displayed on screen as the exclusive upper boundary for the backward read, ensuring the previous page contains only records that precede the current page.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is viewing the Transaction Type List screen and the current page is the first page of results (CA-FIRST-PAGE is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses PF7 (backward scroll key) to navigate to a previous page
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system identifies that the current page is the first page and no backward navigation is possible; the same first record key (WS-CA-FIRST-TR-CODE) is retained as the starting point for re-display, and no page number decrement occurs

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Backward Navigation Attempt on First Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user requests to scroll backward (PF7) while already viewing the first page of Transaction Types, the system must detect this boundary condition and prevent any further backward navigation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the first page of the Transaction Type List and has pressed PF7, and the system has determined that no previous page exists
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to re-read the Transaction Type records for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the query start key (WS-START-KEY) to the first transaction type code stored for the current page (WS-CA-FIRST-TR-CODE), so that the same set of records will be retrieved from the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retain First Record Key as Starting Point on First Page Boundary
all_rules.Rule_Description: When backward navigation is blocked because the user is already on the first page, the system must use the stored first transaction type code of the current page as the starting key for re-reading, ensuring the same page content is displayed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The start key (WS-START-KEY) has been set to the first transaction type code of the current page (WS-CA-FIRST-TR-CODE), and the user is on the first page after pressing PF7
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes a forward read of the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table using cursor C-TR-TYPE-FORWARD, selecting TR_TYPE and TR_DESCRIPTION where TR_TYPE is greater than or equal to the start key, applying any active type code filter (exact match) and/or description filter (partial contains match), ordered by TR_TYPE ascending, up to the maximum number of screen lines
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system populates the screen rows with the retrieved transaction type records (TR_TYPE and TR_DESCRIPTION), sets the first and last transaction type codes for the page, and determines whether a next page exists by attempting to fetch one additional record beyond the page limit

all_rules.Rule_Name: Re-Read Transaction Type Records from Same Starting Position
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the first page boundary is reached on a PF7 request, the system re-reads the Transaction Type records from the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table starting from the same first record key, applying any active filters, to refresh and re-display the current page content.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF7 and the system has determined that the current page is the first page (CA-FIRST-PAGE is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the informational message for the screen during the message setup phase (2500-SETUP-MESSAGE)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the return message (WS-RETURN-MSG) to exactly 'No previous pages to display', which is then moved to the error message output field (ERRMSGO) on the Transaction Type List screen for the user to see

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Informational Message When No Previous Pages Exist
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user attempts to scroll backward while already on the first page, the system must inform the user that there are no previous pages available by setting a specific boundary message for display on the screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has re-read the same page of Transaction Type records from CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE, set the message 'No previous pages to display' in the error message field (ERRMSGO), initialized screen header fields (current date, current time, page number, program name, transaction ID), and set up all screen field attributes and row data
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sends the Transaction Type List screen (CTRTLIAO) to the user via CICS SEND MAP with ERASE and cursor positioning
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The user sees the same Transaction Type List screen with the identical set of transaction type records (TR_TYPE and TR_DESCRIPTION) that were displayed before the PF7 key was pressed, along with the message 'No previous pages to display' in the message area, and the program returns control awaiting the next user interaction with the same transaction ID

all_rules.Rule_Name: Re-Display Transaction Type List Screen with Same Page Content
all_rules.Rule_Description: After detecting the first page boundary on a PF7 request, re-reading the same records, and setting the boundary message, the system must send the fully prepared screen back to the user showing the same transaction type records along with the informational message.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is viewing the Transaction Type list screen and has previously submitted the screen from the same program
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses the Enter key and at least one row has a Delete action flag (D) entered in its selection field
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system routes processing into the delete confirmation workflow, reading the current page of Transaction Type records starting from the first transaction code of the current page, and proceeds to re-display the screen with the selected row highlighted

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Delete Action on Enter Key Press
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Enter key is pressed, the system checks whether at least one row on the current screen has a delete action selected. This determines whether the delete confirmation workflow should be initiated.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type list screen and has entered action codes in the row selection fields
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses Enter and more than one row has an action code (D or U) entered in the selection fields
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets an input error condition, sets the message flag to 'More Than 1 Action', marks each row that has a selection with an error indicator, highlights those selection fields in RED, and re-displays the screen with the error message — no delete confirmation prompt is shown

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reject Multiple Simultaneous Row Actions
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system enforces that only one action (delete or update) can be selected across all displayed rows at the same time. If more than one row has an action selected, the submission is rejected with an error.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type list screen and has entered a value in a row selection field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The value entered in a row selection field is not blank, not a Delete flag (D), and not an Update flag (U)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets an input error condition, marks that specific row's selection field with an error indicator, highlights the selection field in RED with cursor positioned on it, sets the message to 'Invalid Action Code', sets the bad-actions flag to YES, and re-displays the screen with the error — no delete confirmation prompt is shown

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reject Invalid Row Action Code
all_rules.Rule_Description: Each row selection field only accepts valid action codes (D for Delete, U for Update). Any other value entered is treated as an invalid action and triggers an error.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Enter key was pressed, exactly one delete action is selected, and no input errors exist on filters
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to display the delete confirmation screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the database read start key to the first transaction code of the current page (WS-CA-FIRST-TR-CODE), then reads forward through the TRANSACTION_TYPE table only if both the type code filter and the description filter are in a valid state (not flagged as invalid), populating the screen rows with current data

all_rules.Rule_Name: Re-Read Current Page Before Delete Confirmation Display
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before displaying the delete confirmation screen, the system re-reads the current page of Transaction Type records from the database to ensure the displayed data is current. The read uses the first transaction code of the current page as the starting key.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen is being prepared for delete confirmation display and exactly one valid delete action is selected with no bad action selections
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets up screen attributes for the row that has the delete action selected
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The transaction type code field color for that row is set to neutral (DFHNEUTR), the transaction description field color for that row is set to neutral (DFHNEUTR), and the cursor length for the selection field of that row is set to highlight it — making the pending-delete row visually distinct from other rows

all_rules.Rule_Name: Highlight Selected Row for Delete Confirmation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a single valid delete action is selected on a row, the system visually highlights that row by changing the transaction type code and description fields to a neutral color, drawing the user's attention to the record pending deletion.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen is being populated with row data for delete confirmation and exactly one valid delete action is selected with no bad action selections
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the row that has the delete action selected and the deletion has not yet been completed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The session state flag CA-DELETE-REQUESTED is set to TRUE for that row, preserving the pending delete intent so that when the user subsequently presses PF10, the system knows a delete confirmation is expected for that transaction type

all_rules.Rule_Name: Preserve Delete Pending State in Session
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a single valid delete action is selected and the delete has not yet been confirmed, the system preserves the delete-requested state in the session so that a subsequent PF10 key press can execute the actual deletion.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Enter key was pressed, exactly one delete action is selected, exactly one total action is selected across all rows, and the screen is being prepared for display
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Both the type code filter value and the description filter value are unchanged from the previous screen submission (FLG-TYPEFILTER-CHANGED-NO is TRUE and FLG-DESCFILTER-CHANGED-NO is TRUE) and no informational message has already been set
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the informational message flag to WS-INFORM-DELETE, which triggers the display of the delete confirmation prompt message (e.g., 'Press PF10 to Confirm Deletion') centered on the screen — prompting the user to press PF10 to proceed with the deletion

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Delete Confirmation Prompt When Filters Are Unchanged
all_rules.Rule_Description: The delete confirmation prompt message is only displayed when the filter criteria (type code filter and description filter) have not changed since the last screen display. This ensures the user is confirming deletion of the correct record in the correct filter context.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Enter key was pressed and a delete action is selected on a row
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Either the type code filter value has changed from the previous submission (FLG-TYPEFILTER-CHANGED-YES is TRUE) or the description filter value has changed from the previous submission (FLG-DESCFILTER-CHANGED-YES is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system does NOT set the delete confirmation prompt message (WS-INFORM-DELETE is not set), all row selections are cleared (WS-EDIT-SELECT-FLAGS is initialized), and the screen is re-displayed showing the updated filter results without any delete confirmation prompt

all_rules.Rule_Name: Suppress Delete Confirmation Prompt When Filters Have Changed
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the user has changed either the type code filter or the description filter at the same time as selecting a delete action, the delete confirmation prompt is suppressed. The screen is re-displayed with the new filter results but without a confirmation prompt.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All screen initialization, row attribute setup, row data population, screen field attributes, and message setup have been completed for the delete confirmation scenario
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the send-map sequence (2000-SEND-MAP) which includes screen initialization, array attribute setup, screen array data population, screen field attribute setup, and message setup
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sends the composed screen map to the user terminal with: the current date and time displayed, the current page number displayed, all transaction type rows populated with their codes and descriptions, the selected delete-pending row highlighted in neutral color, the confirmation prompt message centered on the screen (if filters are unchanged), and the keyboard unlocked awaiting the user's next input (PF10 to confirm or another key to cancel)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Send Updated Screen with Highlighted Row and Confirmation Prompt
all_rules.Rule_Description: After preparing all screen attributes, row data, and messages, the system sends the fully composed screen to the user. The screen includes the current page of transaction type records, the highlighted pending-delete row, and (when applicable) the delete confirmation prompt.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF10 to confirm deletion and a valid row with a Transaction Type Code has been selected on the screen (identified by the selected row index I-SELECTED)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to execute the delete operation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Type Code (TR_TYPE) from the selected screen row is retrieved and set as the key value to be used in the DELETE statement targeting the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Type Code of Selected Row Before Deletion
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before executing a delete operation, the system must identify and retrieve the Transaction Type Code of the row the user has selected for deletion, so that the correct record is targeted in the database.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Code of the selected row has been retrieved and the system is ready to perform the deletion
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The DELETE statement is executed against the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table with the condition WHERE TR_TYPE equals the selected Transaction Type Code
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The matching transaction type record is deleted from the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table and the outcome (success, child record constraint violation, or other failure) is captured for subsequent processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Execute Delete of Transaction Type Record from Database
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system executes a DELETE operation against the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table using the Transaction Type Code of the selected row as the exact match key, permanently removing that transaction type record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The DELETE statement executed against CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE completed without any errors (SQL return code equals zero)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the outcome of the DELETE operation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The database transaction is committed immediately (SYNCPOINT) to permanently save the deletion, the Delete Succeeded flag is set to TRUE, and a delete success informational message is queued for display to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Commit Transaction and Confirm Successful Deletion
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the DELETE operation completes successfully, the system must immediately commit the database change to make it permanent and record that the deletion succeeded so that downstream processing can display a success message and reset the screen state.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The DELETE statement was executed against CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE for the selected Transaction Type Code
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The deletion fails because one or more child records in the database are associated with (reference) this Transaction Type Code, resulting in a referential integrity constraint violation (equivalent to SQL error -532)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The deletion is not performed, the Delete Requested state is preserved (kept as pending, not succeeded), and the user is presented with the error message: 'Please delete associated child records first' — the user must delete all associated child records before this Transaction Type can be deleted

all_rules.Rule_Name: Prevent Deletion When Associated Child Records Exist
all_rules.Rule_Description: A Transaction Type record cannot be deleted if other records in the system reference it as a foreign key (child records). The system must detect this constraint violation and inform the user that they must first remove all associated child records before the transaction type can be deleted.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The DELETE statement was executed against CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE for the selected Transaction Type Code
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The deletion fails for any reason other than a child record constraint violation (i.e., any error condition that is not a referential integrity violation)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The deletion is not performed, the error details are captured and formatted into a message beginning with 'Delete failed with message:' followed by the specific error information, the error message is displayed to the user, and the delete-pending state is preserved so the user is aware the deletion did not complete

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle General Deletion Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the DELETE operation fails for any reason other than a child record constraint violation, the system must inform the user of the failure and preserve the delete-pending state so the user can retry or take corrective action.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The DELETE operation completed successfully, the transaction was committed, and the Delete Succeeded flag is set to TRUE
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the post-deletion screen update
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: A delete success message is displayed on the screen; then all session state is fully reset — including the communication area, program communication area, and miscellaneous storage — the program is set to Enter mode, the display is repositioned to the first page, and the last-page-shown indicator is reset to 'not shown', effectively returning the user to a fresh first-page view of the remaining transaction type records

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Success Message and Reset Session to First Page After Deletion
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a transaction type record is successfully deleted, the system must display a confirmation message to the user, reset all session state (filters, selections, page position), and return the user to the first page of the transaction type list so they see a refreshed, accurate view of remaining records.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A delete operation has been executed against the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table for the selected Transaction Type Code (TR_TYPE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The delete operation completes and the system evaluates the result
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the deletion completed without error, the system marks the deletion as succeeded and proceeds to success handling; if the deletion failed (due to child records existing or any other failure), the system routes to failure handling without marking success

all_rules.Rule_Name: Determine Delete Operation Outcome
all_rules.Rule_Description: After executing a delete operation on a Transaction Type record, the system evaluates whether the deletion was completed successfully and routes to the appropriate success or failure handling path.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A delete operation has been executed on the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table for the selected Transaction Type Code (TR_TYPE) and the deletion completed without any errors
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system confirms the deletion was successful (no database errors returned)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system immediately commits the deletion to the database (making it permanent and visible to all users), sets the deletion status to 'succeeded', and sets an informational flag to display a delete success message to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark Deletion as Successful and Commit Transaction
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a Transaction Type record is successfully deleted from the database, the system commits the change permanently and sets the internal state to reflect that the deletion succeeded.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A Transaction Type record has been successfully deleted and the screen is being prepared for display
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the row that had the delete action selected and the deletion flag is marked as successful
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The selection field for that specific row is blanked out (cleared), removing the delete action indicator from the display so the row no longer shows a pending delete selection

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Action Selection for Deleted Row on Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a successful deletion, the selection field of the row that was deleted is cleared on the screen so that the deleted record no longer appears as having a pending action.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A Transaction Type record has been successfully deleted and the screen message area is being prepared
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the deletion outcome flag and finds the deletion was successful (FLG-DELETED-YES is true)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the informational message to the delete success message and displays it on the screen in the message area, confirming to the user that the deletion was completed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Delete Success Message to User
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a successful deletion of a Transaction Type record, the system sets and displays a success confirmation message to inform the user that the delete operation completed successfully.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen has been prepared with the delete success message and the deleted row's selection has been cleared
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system is ready to present the result of the delete operation to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sends the fully prepared screen map to the user's terminal, displaying the success message and the updated transaction type list with the deleted row's action selection removed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Send Updated Screen with Success Message After Deletion
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a successful deletion, the system sends the refreshed screen to the user displaying the success message and the updated list with the deleted row's selection cleared.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A Transaction Type record has been successfully deleted and the success screen has been sent to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the post-deletion cleanup after confirming the deletion flag is marked as successful
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system clears all session data by reinitializing: the main communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA), the program-specific communication area (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA), and all miscellaneous working storage (WS-MISC-STORAGE), effectively removing all filter values, row selections, paging keys, and any other session state accumulated during the current session

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reset All Session Data to Initial State After Successful Deletion
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a successful deletion and the success screen has been sent, the system resets all session-level data including filters, selections, paging state, and program communication areas back to their initial values to prepare for a fresh start.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All session data has been reset following a successful deletion of a Transaction Type record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets the navigation state for the next program entry
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the program entry mode to 'entering' (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER) and sets the page position indicator to 'first page' (CA-FIRST-PAGE), ensuring the next display will begin from the first record in the Transaction Type list

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reset Page Position to First Page After Successful Deletion
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a successful deletion and session reset, the system sets the page navigation state so that the next screen display will start from the very first page of the Transaction Type list.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The page position has been reset to the first page following a successful deletion of a Transaction Type record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system completes the full post-deletion state reset
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the last-page indicator to 'not yet shown' (CA-LAST-PAGE-NOT-SHOWN), ensuring that end-of-list messages such as 'No more pages to display' will not appear prematurely when the user begins navigating the refreshed Transaction Type list

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark Last Page as Not Yet Shown After Deletion Reset
all_rules.Rule_Description: As part of the post-deletion reset, the system marks that the last page of the Transaction Type list has not yet been reached or shown, resetting the end-of-list tracking for the fresh navigation session.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has selected a transaction type row with action code 'D' (Delete) on the Transaction Type List screen, and the user has pressed PF10 to confirm the deletion
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes a DELETE operation against the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table targeting the record whose TR_TYPE matches the transaction type code of the selected row
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system evaluates the outcome of the delete operation to determine whether it succeeded, failed due to associated child records, or failed for another reason, and routes processing accordingly

all_rules.Rule_Name: Attempt to Delete Transaction Type Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user confirms deletion by pressing PF10, the system attempts to permanently remove the selected transaction type record from the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table using the transaction type code of the selected row.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has pressed PF10 to confirm deletion of a selected transaction type record, and the DELETE operation has been executed against the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The deletion fails because the transaction type code is still referenced by one or more associated child records in the database (referential integrity violation)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the delete action as still pending (CA-DELETE-REQUESTED remains active), indicating the deletion was not completed and the user must take further action before the record can be deleted

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Referential Integrity Violation on Delete - Child Records Exist
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a deletion attempt fails because the transaction type is still referenced by associated child records (referential integrity constraint), the system must detect this specific condition and prevent the deletion from proceeding.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The deletion of a transaction type has failed due to a referential integrity violation (child records are associated with the transaction type), and no prior error message has already been set for this transaction
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the referential integrity violation outcome
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error message context to 'Please delete associated child records first:' and formats a complete error message combining this context with the database error details, which is stored in the return message field for display to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Prepare Error Message for Child Records Constraint Violation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a transaction type cannot be deleted because associated child records exist, the system must prepare a specific, user-friendly error message instructing the user to remove the child records first before retrying the deletion.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A deletion attempt has failed because child records exist, and the delete action is still marked as pending (CA-DELETE-REQUESTED is active) for the selected row
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the Transaction Type List screen for redisplay by populating each row's display data
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The selected row retains its delete-requested state (the row is NOT cleared/blanked), the transaction type code and description for that row are displayed in neutral highlight color to indicate the pending delete action, and the selection field remains visible — so the user can clearly identify which record still requires child record removal

all_rules.Rule_Name: Preserve Selected Row Highlight After Delete Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a failed deletion due to child records, the selected transaction type row must remain visually highlighted on the screen with the delete action still indicated, so the user can clearly see which record still needs attention.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The deletion of a transaction type has failed due to associated child records, the delete action is still marked as pending, and the error message 'Please delete associated child records first:' has been prepared
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sends the Transaction Type List screen back to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen is redisplayed with: (1) the selected transaction type row still highlighted showing the pending delete action, (2) the error message 'Please delete associated child records first:' visible on the screen, (3) the delete outcome flag set to 'not deleted' (FLG-DELETED-NO), and (4) the screen reflects that the deletion did NOT succeed — the record remains in the database and the user must first delete all associated child records before the transaction type can be removed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Redisplay Transaction Type List Screen with Child Records Error Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a failed deletion due to child records, the system must redisplay the full Transaction Type List screen including the error message, so the user is informed of the reason for failure and can take corrective action.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A transaction type record exists in the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table and one or more other records in the database reference this transaction type (child records exist)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: A user attempts to delete the transaction type by selecting it with action code 'D' and confirming with PF10
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system blocks the deletion, does not remove the transaction type record from the database, keeps the delete action as pending on the screen, displays the message 'Please delete associated child records first:', and requires the user to first delete all associated child records before the transaction type deletion can be successfully retried

all_rules.Rule_Name: Block Transaction Type Deletion When Associated Child Records Exist
all_rules.Rule_Description: A transaction type record cannot be deleted from the system as long as other records in the database reference it. This is a data integrity policy that protects against orphaned child records.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type maintenance screen and has previously selected the Update action (U) on one or more rows
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses the Enter key and the screen was submitted from the Transaction Type maintenance program itself (same program re-entry) and at least one Update action is recorded as requested
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the start key to the first transaction code of the current page, re-reads the current page of transaction type records from the database applying existing filters, and re-displays the screen to prompt the user for confirmation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Trigger Update Confirmation Flow on Enter Key with Update Action
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses the Enter key and at least one Update action has been selected on the Transaction Type maintenance screen, the system initiates the update confirmation flow by re-reading the current page and re-displaying the screen for user confirmation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has entered action codes in the row selection fields on the Transaction Type maintenance screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the row selections after Enter is pressed with updates requested
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If exactly one action is selected (WS-ONLY-1-ACTION), exactly one valid action exists (WS-ONLY-1-VALID-ACTION), and no bad/invalid action codes are present (FLG-BAD-ACTIONS-SELECTED-NO), then the system proceeds to highlight the selected row and enable the description field for editing; otherwise the confirmation display steps are skipped and the screen is re-displayed without the update confirmation prompts

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate Single Update Action Before Confirmation Display
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system verifies that exactly one valid Update action is selected across all rows and that no invalid selection codes exist before proceeding to highlight the selected row and prompt for PF10 confirmation. If multiple actions or invalid selections exist, the confirmation display is bypassed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The update confirmation flow has been triggered by the user pressing Enter with an update action selected
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the validity of the current type code filter and description filter
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the type code filter is NOT in an invalid state (NOT FLG-TYPEFILTER-NOT-OK) AND the description filter is NOT in an invalid state (NOT FLG-DESCFILTER-NOT-OK), the system performs a forward database read (8000-READ-FORWARD) using the current start key and active filters; if either filter is invalid, the database read is skipped entirely and the screen is re-displayed with existing data

all_rules.Rule_Name: Conditionally Read Current Page Based on Filter Validity
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before re-displaying the screen for update confirmation, the system checks whether the current filter conditions (type code filter and description filter) are valid. If both filters are valid, the system reads the current page of transaction type records from the database. If either filter is invalid, the database read is skipped.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Both the type code filter and description filter are in a valid state
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system performs a forward read of Transaction Type records
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system opens the forward cursor (C-TR-TYPE-FORWARD) and fetches records from CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE where TR_TYPE is greater than or equal to the current start key (WS-START-KEY), applying the type code filter as an exact match on TR_TYPE if the type filter flag is active, and applying the description filter as a LIKE (contains) match on TR_DESCRIPTION if the description filter flag is active, ordering results by TR_TYPE ascending, filling up to the maximum number of screen rows, and storing the first and last transaction codes of the page for paging navigation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Read Current Page of Transaction Type Records for Update Confirmation
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system reads the current page of Transaction Type records from the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table using the existing start key and any active filter conditions, to populate the screen before re-displaying it for update confirmation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A row on the Transaction Type maintenance screen has the Update action (U) selected, exactly one valid action is selected, and no bad selections exist
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the screen array data for display during the update confirmation flow
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the update has NOT already been completed (NOT FLG-UPDATE-COMPLETED), the system sets the communication area flag to 'Update Requested' (CA-UPDATE-REQUESTED = TRUE) for the selected row, preserving the update intent for the next user interaction; if the update has already been completed, the selection field for that row is cleared (SELECT-BLANK)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark Selected Row as Update Requested for Screen Display
all_rules.Rule_Description: When exactly one valid Update action is selected and the update has not yet been completed, the system marks the communication area state as 'Update Requested' so the screen correctly reflects the pending update action on the selected row.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A row has the Update action selected, exactly one valid action is selected, and no bad selections exist
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets up the screen field attributes for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The transaction type code field (TRTTYPC) for the selected row is set to neutral color (DFHNEUTR), visually distinguishing the selected row from other rows on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Highlight Selected Row in Neutral Color for Update Confirmation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an Update action is selected on a row and the update is pending confirmation, the system highlights the transaction type code field of the selected row in neutral color to visually indicate that the row is the target of the pending update action.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A row has the Update action selected, exactly one valid action is selected, no bad selections exist, and the update has NOT yet been completed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets up the screen field attributes for the selected row
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The description field attribute (TRTYPDA) for the selected row is set to unprotected/editable (DFHBMFSE), the cursor length for the description field (TRTYPDL) is set to -1 to position the cursor there, allowing the user to modify the transaction description; if the description field has a validation error, it is additionally highlighted in RED (DFHRED)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Enable Description Field for Editing on Selected Update Row
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an Update action is pending confirmation (not yet confirmed with PF10), the system makes the description field of the selected row editable so the user can modify the transaction description before confirming the update.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A row has the Update action selected, exactly one valid action is selected, no bad selections exist, and the update has NOT yet been completed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the screen array data for the selected row
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the user has made changes to the description (CHANGES-HAVE-OCCURRED): if the new description is blank (FLG-ROW-DESCRIPTION-BLANK), display an asterisk (*) in the description field (TRTYPDO); otherwise display the newly entered description value (WS-ROW-TR-DESC-IN(I)); if no changes have been made (NO-CHANGES-FOUND), display the original stored description from the communication area (WS-CA-ROW-TR-DESC-OUT(I))

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Current Description Value in Editable Field
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system populates the editable description field of the selected update row with the appropriate description value — either the newly entered value, an asterisk placeholder if the new value is blank, or the original stored description if no changes have been made.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed Enter with exactly one Update action selected (WS-UPDATES-REQUESTED > 0), exactly one total action is selected (WS-ONLY-1-ACTION), exactly one valid action is selected (WS-ONLY-1-VALID-ACTION), no informational message is already set (WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE), the type code filter has not changed (FLG-TYPEFILTER-CHANGED-NO), and the description filter has not changed (FLG-DESCFILTER-CHANGED-NO)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the informational message for screen display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the update confirmation prompt flag (WS-INFORM-UPDATE = TRUE), which causes an informational message to be displayed on the screen instructing the user to press PF10 to confirm the update action

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Update Confirmation Prompt Message to User
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user has selected exactly one valid Update action and pressed Enter, and the filters have not changed, the system displays an informational prompt message instructing the user to press PF10 to confirm and save the update.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen is being prepared for display during the update confirmation flow
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets up the screen field attributes for each row in the display array
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: For each row where the row data is empty (WS-CA-EACH-ROW-OUT(I) equals LOW-VALUES) OR the row selection protection flag is active (FLG-PROTECT-SELECT-ROWS-YES), the selection field attribute (TRTSELA) is set to protected/read-only (DFHBMPRO), preventing the user from entering a selection code on those rows; rows with data and no protection flag have their selection fields set to unprotected/editable (DFHBMFSE)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Protect All Other Rows from Selection Changes During Update Confirmation
all_rules.Rule_Description: While an update action is pending confirmation, rows that have no data or are in a protected state have their selection fields locked so the user cannot select additional rows or change selections on other rows during the confirmation step.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen is being prepared for display and at least one row action has been requested (WS-ACTIONS-REQUESTED > 0)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets up the screen field attributes for the filter input fields
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The type code filter field (TRTYPEO) is populated with the current type code input value (WS-IN-TYPE-CD), its color attribute (TRTYPEC) is set to blue (DFHBLUE), and its field attribute (TRTYPEA) is set to auto-skip (DFHBMASF); similarly, the description filter field (TRDESCO) is populated with the current description input value (WS-IN-TYPE-DESC), its color attribute (TRDESCC) is set to blue (DFHBLUE), and its field attribute (TRDESCA) is set to auto-skip (DFHBMASF)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Filter Fields in Blue to Indicate Pending Action
all_rules.Rule_Description: When one or more row actions are requested (an update or delete is pending), the system displays the type code filter and description filter fields in blue color and sets them as auto-skip fields, visually communicating to the user that an action is in progress and the filters are not the current focus.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected a row with action 'U' (Update) and entered a new description value, and PF10 has been pressed to confirm the update
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the data for the update operation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system retrieves the Transaction Type Code (TR_TYPE) from the selected row's input field (WS-ROW-TR-CODE-IN for the selected row index), trims and stores the new Description text (up to 50 characters) entered by the user from WS-ROW-TR-DESC-IN for the selected row index, and computes the length of the new description to be stored alongside the description text

all_rules.Rule_Name: Prepare Update Data from Selected Row
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before executing the database update, the system retrieves the Transaction Type Code and the new Description value entered by the user from the selected row on the screen to prepare the update payload.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Code and new Description have been prepared from the selected row
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the update against the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE database table
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system updates the TR_DESCRIPTION column to the new description value for the record where TR_TYPE exactly matches the selected Transaction Type Code; no other fields or records are modified

all_rules.Rule_Name: Execute Description Update on Transaction Type Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system updates only the description field of the matching Transaction Type record in the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table using the Transaction Type Code as the unique identifier. The Transaction Type Code itself is never modified.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The update of TR_DESCRIPTION in CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE has been executed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The database confirms the update was successful (no errors returned)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system immediately commits the transaction to make the change permanent, marks the update status as 'succeeded' (CA-UPDATE-SUCCEEDED), sets the update-completed flag (FLG-UPDATE-COMPLETED) to TRUE so the screen reflects completion, and sets an informational success message (WS-INFORM-UPDATE-SUCCESS) if no other informational message is already set

all_rules.Rule_Name: Commit Transaction on Successful Update
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the database update completes successfully, the system commits the change permanently to the database and marks the update as completed so the screen can reflect the success state.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The update of TR_DESCRIPTION in CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE has been executed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The database returns a 'record not found' result (no rows were updated)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system keeps the update action in a pending/requested state (CA-UPDATE-REQUESTED remains active), displays the message 'Record not found. Deleted by others ?' to inform the user that the record may have been removed by another user, and does not commit any changes

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle Record Not Found During Update
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the Transaction Type record no longer exists at the time of the update attempt, the system informs the user that the record may have been deleted by another user and keeps the update in a pending state.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The update of TR_DESCRIPTION in CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE has been executed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The database returns a deadlock error (resource contention with another user's transaction)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the overall input as an error (INPUT-ERROR), keeps the update action in a pending/requested state (CA-UPDATE-REQUESTED remains active), and displays the message 'Deadlock. Someone else updating ?' to inform the user that another user may be updating the same record; no changes are committed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle Deadlock During Update
all_rules.Rule_Description: If a deadlock is detected during the update attempt, indicating another user may be simultaneously updating the same record, the system treats this as an input error, informs the user, and keeps the update in a pending state.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The update of TR_DESCRIPTION in CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE has been executed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The database returns any negative error code that is not a deadlock error (i.e., any database failure other than record-not-found or deadlock)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system keeps the update action in a pending/requested state (CA-UPDATE-REQUESTED remains active), displays the message 'Update failed with' along with the database error details to inform the user of the unexpected failure, and does not commit any changes

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle Unexpected Update Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the update fails due to any unexpected database error other than record-not-found or deadlock, the system informs the user of the failure and keeps the update in a pending state without committing any changes.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The update operation on CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE has completed with any result (success, not found, deadlock, or other failure)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system proceeds to refresh the screen after the update attempt
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system always re-reads the current page of Transaction Type records from the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table starting from the first Transaction Type Code of the current page (WS-CA-FIRST-TR-CODE used as the start key WS-START-KEY), applying any active filters, and populates the screen rows with the latest data from the database

all_rules.Rule_Name: Refresh Transaction Type List After Update Attempt
all_rules.Rule_Description: Regardless of whether the update succeeded or failed, the system always refreshes the displayed list of Transaction Types by re-reading the current page of records from the database, ensuring the screen reflects the latest data.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type list has been refreshed from the database after the update attempt
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares and sends the screen to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system displays the refreshed Transaction Type list on screen; if the update succeeded, a success message (WS-INFORM-UPDATE-SUCCESS) is shown and the selection field for the updated row is cleared; if the update failed (record not found, deadlock, or other error), the corresponding error message is displayed and the row remains in its update-pending state with the description field still editable; the screen is sent with cursor positioning and keyboard unlocked

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Updated Screen with Outcome Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: After refreshing the data, the system sends the updated screen to the user showing the current list of Transaction Types along with an appropriate success or error message reflecting the outcome of the update operation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has confirmed an update action (PF10) on a selected Transaction Type row, and the UPDATE statement against CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE executes without any database error (SQL code = 0)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The database successfully updates the TR_DESCRIPTION for the matching TR_TYPE record and commits the transaction
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the update operation as succeeded (CA-UPDATE-SUCCEEDED = TRUE), and subsequently sets the Update Completed Flag (FLG-UPDATE-COMPLETED = TRUE) in the main processing flow so that all subsequent screen-building steps treat the update as finished

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark Transaction Type Update as Successfully Completed
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the database update of a Transaction Type description completes without error, the system marks the update as succeeded and sets the update-completed flag so downstream screen-building steps can reflect the completed state.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The update of a Transaction Type description has been marked as succeeded and the Update Completed Flag is set to TRUE
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to redisplay the Transaction Type list
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the database read start key to the first Transaction Type code of the current page (WS-CA-FIRST-TR-CODE) and reads forward through CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE using the forward cursor (C-TR-TYPE-FORWARD), applying any active Type Code filter (exact match on TR_TYPE) and/or Description filter (LIKE match with wildcard characters), ordered ascending by TR_TYPE, to populate up to the maximum number of screen rows with refreshed data

all_rules.Rule_Name: Refresh Transaction Type List After Successful Update
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a successful update, the system re-reads the Transaction Type records from the database starting from the same page position the user was on, so the refreshed list reflects the newly saved description.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The forward read from CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE has completed and row data is available in the working storage output array (WS-CA-ALL-ROWS-OUT)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system builds the screen to be sent to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sequentially: (1) initializes screen header fields including current date, current time, page number, program name, and transaction ID; (2) sets display attributes for each row up to the maximum screen lines; (3) populates each row with TR_TYPE and TR_DESCRIPTION from the refreshed data; (4) configures filter field attributes; (5) prepares the appropriate informational or status message; and (6) sends the completed screen to the user's terminal, displaying up to the maximum number of Transaction Type records

all_rules.Rule_Name: Build Refreshed Screen with Up to Maximum Transaction Type Records
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system assembles the full screen output by initializing screen fields, setting row attributes, populating row data, configuring field attributes, preparing messages, and sending the screen — displaying up to the maximum number of Transaction Type records per page.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen row array is being populated and a specific row had an Update action (U) selected, exactly one valid action was selected across all rows, and the Update Completed Flag is TRUE
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets the display values for that row during screen construction
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The action selection field for that row is cleared to blank (SELECT-BLANK), removing the 'U' indicator so the row appears unselected on the refreshed screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Action Selection Field on the Updated Row After Successful Update
