Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A Transaction Type list screen is displayed, the user has entered 'U' (Update) in a row's selection field, and the description field for that row is being validated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The description field value for the selected update row is blank, contains only spaces, contains only low-values, or has a trimmed length of zero
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) set the overall input status to ERROR, (2) set the description field flag to 'FLG-ALPHNANUM-BLANK', (3) if no prior error message has been set (WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF), construct and store the error message 'Transaction Desc must be supplied.' in WS-RETURN-MSG, and (4) set the row description validation flag to 'FLG-ROW-DESCRIPTION-NOT-OK'

all_rules.Rule_Name: Require Non-Blank Description for Update Action
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user selects the Update action on a transaction type row, the description field for that row is mandatory and must not be left blank. If the description is blank or contains only spaces, the system must reject the update request with an appropriate error message.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A Transaction Type list screen is displayed, the user has entered 'U' (Update) in a row's selection field, the description field is not blank, and the description is being validated for character content
Acceptance_Criteria.When: After converting all valid alphanumeric characters to spaces, the remaining trimmed content of the description field (up to 50 characters) is not empty — meaning non-alphanumeric characters are present
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) set the overall input status to ERROR, (2) set the description field flag to 'FLG-ALPHNANUM-NOT-OK', (3) if no prior error message has been set (WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF), construct and store the error message 'Transaction Desc can have numbers or alphabets only.' in WS-RETURN-MSG, and (4) set the row description validation flag to 'FLG-ROW-DESCRIPTION-NOT-OK'

all_rules.Rule_Name: Restrict Description to Alphanumeric Characters Only
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user selects the Update action on a transaction type row and provides a description, the description must contain only letters and numbers. Special characters or symbols are not permitted in the transaction type description.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A Transaction Type list screen is displayed and the user has entered a value in the Type Code filter field (the value is not blank, not spaces, not zeros, and not low-values)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The entered Type Code filter value fails a numeric check (IS NOT NUMERIC)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) set the overall input status to ERROR, (2) set the type filter flag to 'FLG-TYPEFILTER-NOT-OK', (3) set the flag 'FLG-PROTECT-SELECT-ROWS-YES' to lock all row selection fields preventing further row selections, and (4) store the error message 'TYPE CODE FILTER,IF SUPPLIED MUST BE A 2 DIGIT NUMBER' in WS-RETURN-MSG

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate Type Code Filter as Numeric
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Transaction Type Code filter field, when supplied by the user, must be a numeric value. Non-numeric entries are invalid and must be rejected. The field is optional — if left blank, no type code filtering is applied.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A Transaction Type list screen is displayed and the user has supplied at least one filter value — either a valid Type Code filter ('FLG-TYPEFILTER-ISVALID') or a valid Description filter ('FLG-DESCFILTER-ISVALID') or both
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes a COUNT query against the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table applying the active filter conditions: if Type Code filter is active (WS-EDIT-TYPE-FLAG = '1'), filter by exact match on TR_TYPE = WS-TYPE-CD-FILTER; if Description filter is active (WS-EDIT-DESC-FLAG = '1'), filter by TR_DESCRIPTION LIKE TRIM(WS-TYPE-DESC-FILTER) using wildcard matching
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system stores the count of matching records in WS-RECORDS-COUNT and proceeds to evaluate whether any records were found

all_rules.Rule_Name: Verify Filter Criteria Returns Matching Records
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user supplies one or more filter values (Type Code filter and/or Description filter), the system must verify that at least one matching transaction type record exists in the database before proceeding. This cross-validation prevents the user from navigating to an empty result set.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has executed a count query against CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE using the supplied filter criteria and the result count (WS-RECORDS-COUNT) has been evaluated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The count of matching records (WS-RECORDS-COUNT) equals zero — no transaction type records match the supplied filter conditions
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) set the overall input status to ERROR, (2) if the Type Code filter was active and valid, set its flag to 'FLG-TYPEFILTER-NOT-OK', (3) if the Description filter was active and valid, set its flag to 'FLG-DESCFILTER-NOT-OK', (4) set the flag 'FLG-PROTECT-SELECT-ROWS-YES' to lock all row selection fields, and (5) store the error message 'No Records found for these filter conditions' in WS-RETURN-MSG

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reject Filter Criteria with No Matching Records
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the filter criteria entered by the user (Type Code and/or Description) do not match any transaction type records in the database, the system must reject the filter values and inform the user that no records were found for the specified conditions.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has completed all input validation checks (row action codes, multiple selections, description content, type code filter, and filter cross-validation) and one or more validation errors have been detected (INPUT-ERROR flag is set to TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the overall input error status and determines that errors exist
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) move the error message stored in WS-RETURN-MSG to the screen error message area (CCARD-ERROR-MSG / ERRMSGO), (2) set the next program, mapset, and map to the current program's values to stay on the same screen, (3) if filter validation failed (FLG-TYPEFILTER-NOT-OK), highlight the Type Code filter field in RED and position the cursor on it, (4) if description filter validation failed (FLG-DESCFILTER-NOT-OK), highlight the Description filter field in RED and position the cursor on it, (5) if row protection is required (FLG-PROTECT-SELECT-ROWS-YES), set all row selection fields to protected (DFHBMPRO) preventing user input, and (6) send the screen back to the user with all error highlights, RED field indicators, and error messages displayed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Error Messages and Protect Row Selections on Validation Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: When any input validation errors are detected during screen processing, the system must display the accumulated error message to the user, protect all row selection fields to prevent further invalid input, and re-send the screen with all error highlights and messages visible.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has been reading transaction type records forward from the database and is accumulating rows for the current page display
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The count of records read equals the maximum number of screen lines (rows per page)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system recognizes the current page is full, stops the read loop, saves the current transaction type code as the last record key of the current page, and proceeds to perform an extra fetch to check for additional records beyond this page

all_rules.Rule_Name: Determine If Current Page Is Full
all_rules.Rule_Description: After reading transaction type records from the database, the system checks whether the number of records retrieved equals the maximum allowed rows per page to decide if a next-page existence check is needed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has read the maximum number of records allowed per page from the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The row count reaches the maximum screen lines limit
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The transaction type code (TR_TYPE) of the last fetched record is saved as the last transaction type code for the current page (WS-CA-LAST-TR-CODE), which will serve as the starting reference point for determining if a next page exists

all_rules.Rule_Name: Save Last Transaction Type Code of Current Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the current page is determined to be full, the system saves the transaction type code of the last record on the page so it can be used as the boundary key for next-page detection and future navigation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current page of transaction type records is full (maximum rows per page have been read) and the last record's transaction type code has been saved
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system performs one additional fetch from the forward-reading database cursor (C-TR-TYPE-FORWARD) using the same active filter conditions (type code filter and/or description filter if applicable)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The result of this extra fetch is evaluated to determine whether additional records exist beyond the current page, and the next-page indicator is set accordingly — this extra record is never displayed to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Perform Extra Fetch to Check for Next Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: After filling the current page to its maximum capacity, the system performs one additional database read beyond the last displayed record to determine whether more transaction type records exist, without displaying that extra record to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has performed an extra fetch beyond the last displayed record on the current page
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The extra fetch returns a valid transaction type record (fetch is successful with no end-of-data condition)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the next-page indicator to 'Next Page EXISTS' (CA-NEXT-PAGE-EXISTS) and saves the transaction type code (TR_TYPE) of the extra fetched record as the last transaction type code (WS-CA-LAST-TR-CODE), which will be used as the starting key when the user navigates to the next page

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Next Page Exists and Save Next Page Starting Key
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the extra fetch beyond the current page successfully retrieves a record, the system confirms that a next page of transaction types is available and saves the retrieved record's transaction type code as the starting key for the next page navigation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has performed an extra fetch beyond the last displayed record on a full page of transaction type records
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The extra fetch returns no record (end-of-data condition is reached)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the next-page indicator to 'Next Page DOES NOT EXIST' (CA-NEXT-PAGE-NOT-EXISTS); additionally, if the user pressed PF8 (scroll forward) to reach this page, the system sets the 'No More Records' message to inform the user that no further pages are available

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Next Page Does Not Exist When Extra Fetch Returns No Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the extra fetch beyond the current full page returns no record, the system confirms the user is viewing the last available page of transaction types and sets the indicator accordingly. If the user was scrolling forward (PF8), an informational message is also set.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is reading transaction type records forward from the database and the read loop ends before reaching the maximum rows per page
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The database cursor returns an end-of-data condition (no more records to fetch) before the page is full
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the next-page indicator to 'Next Page DOES NOT EXIST' (CA-NEXT-PAGE-NOT-EXISTS); if the user pressed PF8 (scroll forward) to navigate here, the system also sets the 'No More Records' message to inform the user that no further pages are available

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Next Page Does Not Exist When Page Is Not Full
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the database returns fewer records than the maximum page size (a partial page), the system recognizes this as the last page of results and sets the next-page indicator to indicate no further pages exist.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to read transaction type records forward from the database and the read loop has ended with an end-of-data condition before retrieving any records
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The current page number is 1 (first page) AND the number of records read is zero
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system identifies this as a 'no records found' condition and proceeds to set the appropriate indicator to inform the user that no transaction type records exist for the current search or filter conditions

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Zero Records on First Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the database returns no records at all during a forward read on the first page, the system must distinguish this condition from a partial page result in order to display an appropriate 'no records found' message to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has determined that the current page is the first page (page number equals 1) and no transaction type records were retrieved from the database (row count is zero)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Both conditions are confirmed — page number is 1 AND records read count is zero
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the 'No Records Found' message indicator (WS-MESG-NO-RECORDS-FOUND) so that the screen display will inform the user that no transaction type records exist for the applied search or filter conditions

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set No Records Found Indicator on Empty First Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the first page of a transaction type search returns zero records, the system sets a 'No Records Found' indicator so the screen can display an appropriate message informing the user that no transaction types match the current filter conditions.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A forward read of the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table has been executed using the current start key and any active filters (type code filter and/or description filter), AND the database returns no records (empty result set, SQL code indicates end of data), AND the current page number is 1 (first page), AND the number of rows loaded onto the screen is zero
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the result of the forward cursor fetch and detects that no records were returned
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) Set the No Records Found flag (WS-MESG-NO-RECORDS-FOUND) to TRUE to signal that no transaction types exist for the current search conditions, AND (2) Mark that no next page exists (CA-NEXT-PAGE-NOT-EXISTS) to indicate there are no further records beyond the current empty result

all_rules.Rule_Name: No Records Found on First Page - Flag Setting
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the database returns no records during a forward read and the user is on the first page, the system must set the No Records Found flag and mark that no next page exists, so the screen can notify the user that no transaction types match the current search conditions.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A forward read of the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table has been executed, AND the database returns no records (empty result set)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system checks whether the current screen/page number equals 1 (first page)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the page number IS 1 (first page): the system proceeds to check whether zero rows were returned before setting the No Records Found flag. If the page number is NOT 1 (not the first page): the system does NOT set the No Records Found flag and continues normal processing without a no-records notification

all_rules.Rule_Name: First Page Check Before No Records Found Notification
all_rules.Rule_Description: The No Records Found notification is only triggered when the user is on the first page of results. If the user is not on the first page, the absence of records is handled differently (e.g., as end of data), and no No Records Found message is shown.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has confirmed the current page is the first page (page number = 1), AND the database has returned an end-of-data result (no more records to fetch)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system checks whether the number of rows loaded onto the screen (WS-ROW-NUMBER) equals zero
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the row count IS zero: the system sets the No Records Found flag (WS-MESG-NO-RECORDS-FOUND) to TRUE. If the row count is NOT zero (some rows were already loaded before end-of-data was reached): the system does NOT set the No Records Found flag and continues normal processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Zero Rows Returned Check Before No Records Found Notification
all_rules.Rule_Description: Even when on the first page and the database returns an end-of-data signal, the No Records Found flag is only set if the row counter is exactly zero, confirming that absolutely no records were loaded onto the screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The No Records Found flag (WS-MESG-NO-RECORDS-FOUND) has been set to TRUE following a forward read that returned zero records on the first page, AND the screen setup process (2000-SEND-MAP) has been invoked including message setup (2500-SETUP-MESSAGE) and screen send (2600-SEND-SCREEN)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares and sends the screen to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen is displayed to the user with: (1) The No Records Found notification message populated in the error/message area of the screen (ERRMSGO), informing the user that no transaction type records match the current search conditions, AND (2) No data rows populated in the screen array (all row areas remain empty), AND (3) The next page indicator set to not existing, so no forward paging is available, AND (4) The screen awaits the user's next action (e.g., modify filters or navigate away)

all_rules.Rule_Name: No Records Found Notification Display on Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the No Records Found flag has been set, the screen must be sent to the user displaying a notification that no transaction type records match the current search conditions, and the user must await further action.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A forward read of the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table has been executed using the current start key and any active filters
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The database returns an end-of-data result (SQL code indicates no more records), meaning no records were fetched in this read cycle
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must set the next page status to 'not exists' (CA-NEXT-PAGE-NOT-EXISTS), indicating to the screen that there are no further pages of transaction type records available for forward scrolling, regardless of which page the user is currently on

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark No Next Page When No Records Returned
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the database returns no records during a forward read (end-of-data condition), the system must always mark that no next page exists, regardless of whether it is the first page or not, to prevent the user from attempting to scroll forward.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type list screen and the last page tracking flag may be in any state (shown or not shown)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses any key other than PF8 (e.g., ENTER, PF7, PF3, PF10)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The last-page tracking flag is reset to 'Not Shown', so that the next time the user reaches the last page via PF8, the system will display the page with action instructions and mark it as shown for the first time again

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reset Last Page Tracking When User Navigates Away from PF8
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses any key other than PF8, the system resets the last-page-already-shown tracking flag so that if the user returns to the last page again, the appropriate first-time message and action instructions are displayed rather than the 'no more pages' message.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is reading transaction type records in forward order using the active type code and/or description filters, and the current page has been filled with the maximum number of displayable rows
Acceptance_Criteria.When: An attempt to fetch one additional record beyond the page maximum returns no data (end of result set)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks that no next page exists, and if the read was triggered by the user pressing PF8, a 'no more records' indicator is set to drive the appropriate end-of-data message on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect No More Records When Reading Forward
all_rules.Rule_Description: When reading transaction type records in the forward direction and no more records are found (end of data), the system marks that no next page exists. If the user pressed PF8 to trigger this read, a 'no more records' indicator is also set to drive the appropriate message display.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is reading transaction type records in forward order using the active type code and/or description filters
Acceptance_Criteria.When: A fetch from the forward cursor returns no data (end of result set) before filling any row on the current page
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks that no next page exists; if the read was triggered by PF8, the no-more-records indicator is set; if this is page 1 and zero rows were returned, the 'no records found' indicator is set to inform the user that no transaction types match the current criteria

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect No More Records on Direct Fetch During Forward Read
all_rules.Rule_Description: When reading transaction type records in the forward direction and the very first fetch within the page loop returns no data, the system marks that no next page exists. If PF8 triggered the read, the no-more-records indicator is set. Additionally, if this occurs on the very first page (page 1) with zero rows returned, a 'no records found' indicator is set.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is viewing the Transaction Type list screen, no next page of records exists beyond the current display, and the last page has already been shown to the user in a prior PF8 navigation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses PF8 again to attempt to scroll forward
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system displays the message 'No more pages to display' on the screen, and no new data is loaded

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display No More Pages Message When Last Page Already Shown
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF8 to scroll forward but the last page has already been displayed in a previous PF8 action, the system informs the user that there are no further pages available.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is viewing the Transaction Type list screen, no next page of records exists beyond the current display, and the last page has NOT yet been shown to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses PF8 to scroll forward and reaches the last available page for the first time
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system displays the current page of transaction type records along with available record action instructions (informing the user of actions they can take on the displayed records), and the last-page tracking flag is set to 'Already Shown' so that any further PF8 press will display the 'No more pages to display' message

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Action Instructions and Mark Last Page as Shown on First Reach
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF8 and reaches the last page of transaction type records for the first time (last page has not yet been shown), the system displays the current page along with available record action instructions, and marks the last page as having been shown so that subsequent PF8 presses trigger the 'no more pages' message instead.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is viewing the Transaction Type list screen and a next page of records exists (the system previously detected at least one record beyond the current page's maximum display rows)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses PF8 to scroll forward
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system uses the last transaction type code displayed on the current page as the starting key for the next read, increments the page number by 1, reads the next page of transaction type records in ascending transaction type code order applying any active filters, clears all row selection flags, and displays the new page of records with the next-page-exists flag set appropriately

all_rules.Rule_Name: Navigate to Next Page When More Records Exist
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF8 and more transaction type records exist beyond the current page, the system advances to the next page by using the last transaction type code of the current page as the starting point, increments the page number, clears all row selections, and displays the next set of records.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is viewing the Transaction Type list screen with one or more transaction type records displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: No other overriding informational message has been set (such as delete/update confirmation or filter error) and either no message is currently set or a next page of records exists
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system displays the standard record action instructions message on the screen, informing the user of the available actions (such as selecting a row for update or delete) that can be performed on the displayed transaction type records

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Record Action Instructions When Records Are Available
all_rules.Rule_Description: When transaction type records are displayed and either no informational message has been set yet or a next page of records exists, the system displays available record action instructions to guide the user on what actions they can perform on the displayed records.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has completed processing a user interaction and is preparing to return control to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The session state is being saved before returning to CICS
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current Transaction ID (LIT-THISTRANID) must be saved into the 'From Transaction ID' field (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID) of the communication area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Save Current Transaction ID to Session State
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before returning control to the user, the system records the current transaction identifier into the communication area so that the next user interaction can identify which transaction was last active.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has completed processing a user interaction and is preparing to return control to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The session state is being saved before returning to CICS
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current Program Name (LIT-THISPGM) must be saved into the 'From Program' field (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM) of the communication area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Save Current Program Name to Session State
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before returning control to the user, the system records the current program name into the communication area so that the next user interaction can identify which program was last executing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has completed processing a user interaction and is preparing to return control to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The session state is being saved before returning to CICS
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current Map Name (LIT-THISMAP) must be saved into the 'Last Map' field (CDEMO-LAST-MAP) of the communication area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Save Current Map Name to Session State
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before returning control to the user, the system records the name of the currently active screen map into the communication area so that the correct screen can be restored on the next user interaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has completed processing a user interaction and is preparing to return control to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The session state is being saved before returning to CICS
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current Mapset Name (LIT-THISMAPSET) must be saved into the 'Last Mapset' field (CDEMO-LAST-MAPSET) of the communication area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Save Current Mapset Name to Session State
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before returning control to the user, the system records the name of the currently active screen mapset into the communication area so that the correct screen set can be restored on the next user interaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has read and displayed a page of Transaction Type records and is preparing to return control to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program-specific session state (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) is being saved into the combined communication area
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Type Code of the first record on the current page (WS-CA-FIRST-TR-CODE) and the Transaction Type Code of the last record on the current page (WS-CA-LAST-TR-CODE) must both be preserved in the program-specific communication area so they are available for paging on the next interaction

all_rules.Rule_Name: Save Paging Keys - First and Last Transaction Type Code of Current Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system preserves the Transaction Type Codes of the first and last records displayed on the current page so that forward and backward navigation can correctly retrieve the adjacent pages on the next user interaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has displayed a page of Transaction Type records and is preparing to return control to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program-specific session state (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) is being saved into the combined communication area
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current screen/page number (WS-CA-SCREEN-NUM) must be preserved in the program-specific communication area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Save Current Page Number to Session State
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system preserves the current page number so that the correct page number can be displayed and used for navigation on the next user interaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has populated the screen rows with Transaction Type records and is preparing to return control to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program-specific session state (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) is being saved into the combined communication area
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: For each screen row, both the Transaction Type Code (WS-CA-ROW-TR-CODE-OUT) and the Transaction Type Description (WS-CA-ROW-TR-DESC-OUT) that were displayed must be preserved in the program-specific communication area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Save Screen Row Data - Transaction Codes and Descriptions Displayed on Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system preserves all Transaction Type Codes and Descriptions currently displayed on the screen so that on the next user interaction the program can compare user-entered values against the original displayed values, detect changes, and correctly process update or delete actions.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected a row for a delete or update action and the program is preparing to return control to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program-specific session state (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) is being saved into the combined communication area
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The selected row number (WS-CA-ROW-SELECTED) must be preserved in the program-specific communication area so it can be validated against the user's selection on the next interaction

all_rules.Rule_Name: Save Selected Row Number for Pending Action
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system preserves the row number that the user selected for a pending delete or update action so that on the next interaction (e.g., PF10 confirmation) the program can verify the same row is still selected and process the correct record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A delete or update action has been initiated by the user but not yet confirmed, and the program is preparing to return control to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program-specific session state (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) is being saved into the combined communication area
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The delete-requested flag (CA-DELETE-REQUESTED) and the update-requested flag (CA-UPDATE-REQUESTED) must both be preserved in the program-specific communication area so the correct confirmation action can be taken on the next interaction

all_rules.Rule_Name: Save Delete and Update Pending Flags to Session State
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system preserves the flags indicating whether a delete or update action is currently pending confirmation so that on the next user interaction (PF10) the program knows which action to execute.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has entered a Transaction Type Code filter value and the program is preparing to return control to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program-specific session state (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) is being saved into the combined communication area
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Type Code filter value (WS-CA-TYPE-CD) must be preserved in the program-specific communication area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Save Type Code Filter Value to Session State
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system preserves the Transaction Type Code filter value entered by the user so that on the next interaction the program can detect whether the filter has changed and apply the same filter when re-reading data.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has entered a Transaction Type Description filter value and the program is preparing to return control to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program-specific session state (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) is being saved into the combined communication area
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Type Description filter value (WS-CA-TYPE-DESC) must be preserved in the program-specific communication area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Save Description Filter Value to Session State
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system preserves the Transaction Type Description filter value entered by the user so that on the next interaction the program can detect whether the filter has changed and apply the same filter when re-reading data.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has determined the paging status of the current display and is preparing to return control to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program-specific session state (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) is being saved into the combined communication area
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The 'Next Page Exists' indicator (CA-NEXT-PAGE-EXISTS / CA-NEXT-PAGE-NOT-EXISTS) and the 'Last Page Shown' indicator (CA-LAST-PAGE-SHOWN / CA-LAST-PAGE-NOT-SHOWN) must both be preserved in the program-specific communication area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Save Next Page Exists and Last Page Shown Indicators to Session State
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system preserves the indicators for whether a next page of records exists beyond the current display and whether the last page has already been shown to the user, so that paging messages and navigation behavior are correct on the next user interaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Both the general communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) and the program-specific state (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) have been updated with current session values
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program is preparing to return control to CICS
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The general communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) must be copied into the first portion of the combined work communication area (WS-COMMAREA), and the program-specific state (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) must be copied into the immediately following portion of WS-COMMAREA starting at the offset equal to the length of CARDDEMO-COMMAREA plus one, so that both sections are contiguous in a single communication area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Combine General Session Data and Program-Specific State into Single Communication Area
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system merges the general session data (transaction ID, program name, map, mapset) and the program-specific state (paging keys, page number, row data, selected row, action flags, filter values, paging indicators) into a single combined communication area before passing it back to CICS.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The combined communication area (WS-COMMAREA) has been fully populated with all current session state
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program issues a CICS RETURN command
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The CICS RETURN must specify the current Transaction ID (LIT-THISTRANID) as the next transaction to invoke, pass the combined communication area (WS-COMMAREA) with its full length, so that the next user interaction restores the complete session state

all_rules.Rule_Name: Pass Combined Communication Area Back to CICS with Current Transaction ID
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system returns control to CICS, passing the fully combined communication area and specifying the current transaction ID so that the next user interaction resumes the same transaction with all preserved session state intact.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is displayed and the user is ready to submit their input
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses the ENTER key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the active key action to ENTER (CCARD-AID-ENTER = TRUE), which triggers screen input collection, validation of filters and row selections, and processing of any pending delete or update confirmations

all_rules.Rule_Name: Map ENTER Key to Submit Screen Action
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user presses the ENTER key, the system recognizes it as a screen submission action, triggering input validation and processing of any selected row actions or filter changes.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses the PF2 key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the active key action to PF2 (CCARD-AID-PFK02 = TRUE), which will trigger navigation to the Add New Transaction Type program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Map PF2 Key to Add New Transaction Type Action
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user presses PF2, the system recognizes it as a request to navigate to the Add New Transaction Type screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses the PF3 key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the active key action to PF3 (CCARD-AID-PFK03 = TRUE), which will trigger navigation back to the calling program or Admin menu

all_rules.Rule_Name: Map PF3 Key to Exit to Menu Action
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user presses PF3, the system recognizes it as a request to exit the current screen and return to the calling menu or Admin menu.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is displaying a list of transaction types
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses the PF7 key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the active key action to PF7 (CCARD-AID-PFK07 = TRUE), which will trigger reading the previous page of transaction type records in descending order

all_rules.Rule_Name: Map PF7 Key to Page Backward Action
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user presses PF7, the system recognizes it as a request to scroll backward to the previous page of transaction type records.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is displaying a list of transaction types
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses the PF8 key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the active key action to PF8 (CCARD-AID-PFK08 = TRUE), which will trigger reading the next page of transaction type records in ascending order

all_rules.Rule_Name: Map PF8 Key to Page Forward Action
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user presses PF8, the system recognizes it as a request to scroll forward to the next page of transaction type records.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is displayed and the user has previously selected a delete or update action on a row and pressed ENTER to preview the action
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses the PF10 key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the active key action to PF10 (CCARD-AID-PFK10 = TRUE), which will trigger execution of the confirmed delete or update operation, subject to additional validation that filters and row selection have not changed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Map PF10 Key to Confirm Delete or Update Action
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user presses PF10, the system recognizes it as a confirmation to execute a previously selected delete or update action on a transaction type record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is displayed and the user's terminal uses upper-row function keys
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses the PF13 key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the active key action to PF1 (CCARD-AID-PFK01 = TRUE), identical to the result of pressing PF1, and the screen processes the action as if PF1 was pressed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Alias PF13 to PF1 Action
all_rules.Rule_Description: PF13 is treated as an alias for PF1, allowing users on terminals where upper-row function keys (PF13-PF24) are the primary keys to perform the same PF1 action.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is displayed and the user's terminal uses upper-row function keys
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses the PF14 key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the active key action to PF2 (CCARD-AID-PFK02 = TRUE), identical to the result of pressing PF2, and the screen navigates to the Add New Transaction Type program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Alias PF14 to PF2 Add New Record Action
all_rules.Rule_Description: PF14 is treated as an alias for PF2, allowing users on terminals where upper-row function keys are the primary keys to navigate to the Add New Transaction Type screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is displayed and the user's terminal uses upper-row function keys
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses the PF15 key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the active key action to PF3 (CCARD-AID-PFK03 = TRUE), identical to the result of pressing PF3, and the screen navigates back to the calling program or Admin menu

all_rules.Rule_Name: Alias PF15 to PF3 Exit to Menu Action
all_rules.Rule_Description: PF15 is treated as an alias for PF3, allowing users on terminals where upper-row function keys are the primary keys to exit to the calling menu or Admin menu.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is displaying a list of transaction types and the user's terminal uses upper-row function keys
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses the PF19 key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the active key action to PF7 (CCARD-AID-PFK07 = TRUE), identical to the result of pressing PF7, and the screen reads and displays the previous page of transaction type records

all_rules.Rule_Name: Alias PF19 to PF7 Page Backward Action
all_rules.Rule_Description: PF19 is treated as an alias for PF7, allowing users on terminals where upper-row function keys are the primary keys to scroll backward to the previous page of transaction type records.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is displaying a list of transaction types and the user's terminal uses upper-row function keys
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses the PF20 key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the active key action to PF8 (CCARD-AID-PFK08 = TRUE), identical to the result of pressing PF8, and the screen reads and displays the next page of transaction type records

all_rules.Rule_Name: Alias PF20 to PF8 Page Forward Action
all_rules.Rule_Description: PF20 is treated as an alias for PF8, allowing users on terminals where upper-row function keys are the primary keys to scroll forward to the next page of transaction type records.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is displayed, the user has previously selected a delete or update action and pressed ENTER to preview it, and the user's terminal uses upper-row function keys
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses the PF22 key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the active key action to PF10 (CCARD-AID-PFK10 = TRUE), identical to the result of pressing PF10, and the screen executes the confirmed delete or update operation subject to validation that filters and row selection have not changed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Alias PF22 to PF10 Confirm Delete or Update Action
all_rules.Rule_Description: PF22 is treated as an alias for PF10, allowing users on terminals where upper-row function keys are the primary keys to confirm a previously selected delete or update action on a transaction type record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is displayed and the user presses any function key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The key pressed is any of the following pairs: PF1 or PF13, PF2 or PF14, PF3 or PF15, PF4 or PF16, PF5 or PF17, PF6 or PF18, PF7 or PF19, PF8 or PF20, PF9 or PF21, PF10 or PF22, PF11 or PF23, PF12 or PF24
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the same internal action flag for both keys in each pair (e.g., both PF2 and PF14 set CCARD-AID-PFK02 = TRUE), and all subsequent processing uses only the internal action flag, making the behavior completely identical regardless of which physical key in the pair was pressed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Unified Key Action Processing Regardless of Physical Key Pressed
all_rules.Rule_Description: Once a function key is mapped to its logical action (either directly or via alias), the system processes the action identically regardless of which physical key was pressed. PF1 and PF13 produce the same outcome; PF2 and PF14 produce the same outcome; PF3 and PF15 produce the same outcome; PF7 and PF19 produce the same outcome; PF8 and PF20 produce the same outcome; PF10 and PF22 produce the same outcome.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An informational message (WS-INFO-MSG) has been prepared for display on the Transaction Type maintenance screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to center the informational message on the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system calculates the trimmed length of WS-INFO-MSG by applying the TRIM function to remove trailing spaces, and stores the result as the Trimmed Message Length (WS-STRING-LEN), which represents the number of meaningful characters in the message

all_rules.Rule_Name: Calculate Trimmed Informational Message Length
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before centering an informational message on screen, the system calculates the actual content length of the message by trimming trailing spaces, so that only the meaningful text portion is used for positioning calculations.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Trimmed Message Length (WS-STRING-LEN) has been calculated and the total available display width of the informational message field is known as the full length of WS-INFO-MSG
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system computes the horizontal center position for the message
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system calculates the center starting position (WS-STRING-MID) using the formula: WS-STRING-MID = (Total Field Width of WS-INFO-MSG minus WS-STRING-LEN) divided by 2, plus 1; this position represents the column offset at which the trimmed message text should begin to appear centered within the field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Compute Center Starting Position for Informational Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: To visually center the informational message within the available display field, the system computes the starting position by subtracting the trimmed message length from the total field width, dividing the remainder by 2, and adding 1 to obtain the correct offset position.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Trimmed Message Length (WS-STRING-LEN) and the center starting position (WS-STRING-MID) have both been computed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system writes the informational message into the screen output buffer
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system copies the trimmed portion of WS-INFO-MSG (from position 1 for WS-STRING-LEN characters) into the output string buffer WS-STRING-OUT, starting at position WS-STRING-MID for a length of WS-STRING-LEN characters, effectively placing the message text at the centered position within the output field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Place Trimmed Message Text at Calculated Center Position
all_rules.Rule_Description: After computing the center starting position, the system places the trimmed informational message text into the output display buffer at the calculated offset, so that the message appears visually centered when rendered on screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The centered informational message text has been placed into the output buffer (WS-STRING-OUT)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates whether to display the informational message on the Transaction Type maintenance screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system displays the centered message ONLY IF both of the following conditions are true: (1) the informational message flag is NOT set to 'No Info Message' (WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE is FALSE), AND (2) the message is NOT a 'No Records Found' message (WS-MESG-NO-RECORDS-FOUND is FALSE); if either condition fails, no informational message is displayed on screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Determine Whether Informational Message Should Be Displayed
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before rendering the centered informational message on screen, the system evaluates two conditions: whether an informational message actually exists, and whether the current state is not a 'no records found' situation. Both conditions must be satisfied for the message to be displayed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The informational message exists (WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE is FALSE) AND the message is not a 'No Records Found' message (WS-MESG-NO-RECORDS-FOUND is FALSE), and the centered message text has been placed in WS-STRING-OUT
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sends the Transaction Type maintenance screen to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system moves WS-STRING-OUT to the informational message output field (INFOMSGO) of the screen map (CTRTLIAO), and sets the color attribute of the informational message field (INFOMSGC) to neutral color (DFHNEUTR), so the message appears centered and in neutral color on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Centered Informational Message in Neutral Color
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the conditions for displaying an informational message are met, the system renders the centered message text on the screen using a neutral color attribute, ensuring the message is visually distinguishable without being highlighted as an error.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has selected the Update action on a transaction type row and has entered a description in the description field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The entered description, after trimming leading and trailing spaces and converting to uppercase, is equal to the stored description after the same transformation, AND the trimmed length of the entered description equals the trimmed length of the stored description
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the status to 'No Changes Detected', does not mark the input as invalid, does not set any error message, and exits the description validation without proceeding to further content checks

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect No Changes in Transaction Description for Update
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user selects the Update action on a transaction type row, the system compares the entered description against the currently stored description using a case-insensitive, trimmed comparison. If both the content and length match exactly after trimming and uppercasing, the system determines no changes have been made and skips the update without raising an error.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has selected the Update action on a transaction type row and has entered a description in the description field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The entered description does NOT match the stored description after trimming and case-insensitive comparison, OR the trimmed lengths differ
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the 'Changes Have Occurred' flag to TRUE and proceeds to validate the entered description for blank content and alphanumeric character constraints

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark Description as Changed When Differences Are Detected
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the entered transaction description differs from the stored description (either in content or trimmed length after case-insensitive comparison), the system marks that changes have occurred and proceeds to validate the content of the new description.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has selected the Update action on a transaction type row, changes have been detected in the description field, and the system is validating the entered description content
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The entered description value (up to 50 characters) is equal to low-values, OR equal to spaces, OR the trimmed length of the entered description is zero
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the input as invalid (Input Error), sets the description blank error flag, and sets the error message to 'Transaction Desc must be supplied.' — no further alphanumeric validation is performed for this row

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reject Blank or Empty Transaction Description on Update
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user attempts to update a transaction type description and the entered description is blank, empty, or contains only spaces or low-values, the system rejects the input, marks it as invalid, and displays a mandatory field error message. The field label used in the message is 'Transaction Desc'.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has selected the Update action on a transaction type row, changes have been detected, the entered description is not blank, and the system is performing alphanumeric character validation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The entered description (up to 50 characters) contains one or more characters that are not letters (A-Z, a-z) or digits (0-9) — i.e., special characters, punctuation, or symbols are present — determined by converting all valid alphanumeric characters to spaces and checking if any non-space content remains
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the input as invalid (Input Error), sets the alphanumeric invalid character error flag, and sets the error message to 'Transaction Desc can have numbers or alphabets only.'

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reject Transaction Description Containing Non-Alphanumeric Characters
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user enters a non-blank transaction description for an update, the system validates that the description contains only letters and numbers. Special characters are not permitted. If any non-alphanumeric characters are found, the input is rejected with a specific error message. The field label used in the message is 'Transaction Desc'.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has selected the Update action on a transaction type row, changes have been detected in the description, the entered description is not blank, and the system has completed the alphanumeric character check
Acceptance_Criteria.When: All characters in the entered description (up to 50 characters) are letters or digits with no special characters present
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the description validation flag to 'Valid' (alphanumeric check passed), does not set any error message, and exits the validation — the description is ready for update confirmation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Accept Valid Alphanumeric Transaction Description for Update
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the entered transaction description is non-blank and contains only alphanumeric characters (letters and numbers), the system marks the description as valid and ready for update confirmation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has selected the Update action on a transaction type row and changes have been detected in the entered description compared to the stored description
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to validate the description content by setting the field label to 'Transaction Desc', copying the entered description into the validation work area, setting the maximum validation length to 50 characters, and calling the alphanumeric required field validation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The alphanumeric required field validation is executed against the entered description with a maximum length of 50 characters, and the resulting validation status flags (blank, invalid characters, or valid) are stored back against the specific row's description flags in the screen array

all_rules.Rule_Name: Prepare and Invoke Description Content Validation for Update Row
all_rules.Rule_Description: When changes are detected in the transaction description for an update action, the system prepares the validation context by setting the field name to 'Transaction Desc', loading the entered description, setting the maximum allowed length to 50 characters, and invoking the alphanumeric required field validation routine. After validation, the resulting validation flags are stored against the specific row being updated.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has selected a row with action 'U' (Update) on the Transaction Type maintenance screen, and the selected row index (I-SELECTED) identifies the specific row
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares data for the database update operation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Type Code (TR_TYPE) is taken from the selected row's type code input field (WS-ROW-TR-CODE-IN at position I-SELECTED); the new Transaction Description is taken from the selected row's description input field (WS-ROW-TR-DESC-IN at position I-SELECTED) with leading and trailing spaces trimmed; and the description length is computed as the full field length of the description input

all_rules.Rule_Name: Prepare Transaction Type Data for Update
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before executing the database update, the system retrieves the Transaction Type Code and the new Description entered by the user from the selected screen row, and calculates the length of the new description to pass to the database.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Code (DCL-TR-TYPE) and the new Description (DCL-TR-DESCRIPTION) have been prepared from the selected screen row
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the database update against the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The TR_DESCRIPTION column is updated to the new description value for the record where TR_TYPE exactly matches the selected Transaction Type Code; the Transaction Type Code (TR_TYPE) itself is never modified

all_rules.Rule_Name: Execute Database Update for Transaction Type Description
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system updates the TR_DESCRIPTION field in the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table for the specific Transaction Type Code selected by the user. Only the description is updated; the type code itself is never changed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The database update for the Transaction Type Description has been executed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The update completes successfully (database returns a success status with no errors)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system immediately commits the transaction to make the change permanent (SYNCPOINT); the update status is marked as 'Update Succeeded' (CA-UPDATE-SUCCEEDED); and if no other informational message is already set, an 'Update Success' informational message (WS-INFORM-UPDATE-SUCCESS) is prepared for display to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Commit and Confirm Successful Transaction Type Update
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the database update completes successfully, the system immediately commits the change to make it permanent, marks the update as succeeded, and prepares a success confirmation message for the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The database update for the Transaction Type Description has been executed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The database reports that no matching record was found (record not found condition, equivalent to SQLCODE +100)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The update status remains as 'Update Still Requested/Pending' (CA-UPDATE-REQUESTED is set, meaning the update did NOT succeed); an error message is prepared stating 'Record not found. Deleted by others?' along with the database status details; the screen is re-displayed with the error message so the user is informed the record no longer exists

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle Transaction Type Record Not Found During Update
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the Transaction Type record targeted for update cannot be found in the database at the time of the update attempt, the system treats the update as still pending (not completed) and informs the user that the record may have been deleted by another user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The database update for the Transaction Type Description has been executed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The database detects a deadlock condition (SQLCODE -911), indicating another user is concurrently updating the same Transaction Type record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The update status remains as 'Update Still Requested/Pending' (CA-UPDATE-REQUESTED is set, meaning the update did NOT succeed); the overall input is flagged as an error (INPUT-ERROR is set to TRUE); an error message is prepared stating 'Deadlock. Someone else updating?' along with the database status details; the screen is re-displayed with the error message so the user is aware of the concurrent conflict

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle Deadlock Conflict During Transaction Type Update
all_rules.Rule_Description: If a deadlock is detected during the update attempt — meaning another user is simultaneously trying to update the same Transaction Type record — the system marks the update as still pending, flags the input as an error, and informs the user of the concurrent access conflict.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The database update for the Transaction Type Description has been executed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The database returns any failure condition other than record-not-found or deadlock (any negative database error code other than -911)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The update status remains as 'Update Still Requested/Pending' (CA-UPDATE-REQUESTED is set, meaning the update did NOT succeed); an error message is prepared with the text 'Update failed with' followed by the database error details; the screen is re-displayed with the error message so the user is informed of the failure reason

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle General Update Failure for Transaction Type
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the database update fails for any reason other than record-not-found or deadlock (such as a constraint violation or other database error), the system marks the update as still pending and prepares a detailed failure message for the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is being prepared for display, and the user has previously entered a value in the Type Code filter field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: One or more row actions (delete or update) are pending — meaning the count of requested actions is greater than zero
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Type Code filter field must display the previously entered type code value, the field color must be set to BLUE to visually indicate it is locked, and the field must be set to PROTECTED so the user cannot modify the filter value while an action is in progress

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Type Code Filter Field in Blue and Protected When Row Actions Are Pending
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user has selected a delete or update action on any row in the transaction type list, the Type Code filter field must be displayed in blue and made read-only (protected) to prevent the user from changing the filter while an action is in progress.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is being prepared for display, no row actions (delete or update) are pending, and the user has entered a value in the Type Code filter field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Type Code filter is in a valid state (a valid numeric 2-digit code was entered) OR the Type Code filter is in an invalid state (a non-numeric or otherwise unacceptable value was entered)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Type Code filter field must display the entered type code value as-is, and the field must be set to MODIFIABLE so the user can edit or correct the filter value

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Type Code Filter Field as Modifiable When a Filter Value Has Been Entered
all_rules.Rule_Description: When no row actions are pending but the user has entered a type code filter value — whether that value passed validation or failed validation — the filter field must display the entered value and remain editable so the user can correct or change it.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is being prepared for display, no row actions (delete or update) are pending, and the Type Code filter is neither in a valid nor invalid state
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Type Code filter value is zero or empty (no filter has been entered by the user)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Type Code filter field must be cleared — no value is displayed to the user — indicating that no type code filter is currently active. No field attribute change is applied beyond clearing the displayed value.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Type Code Filter Field When Filter Value Is Zero or Empty
all_rules.Rule_Description: When no row actions are pending, no filter value has been entered or the filter value is zero, the Type Code filter field must be cleared so that no value is shown to the user, indicating no active filter is applied.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is being prepared for display, no row actions (delete or update) are pending, the Type Code filter is neither valid nor invalid, and the filter value is not zero or empty
Acceptance_Criteria.When: None of the specific type code filter conditions (actions pending, filter valid, filter invalid, value zero or empty) are met — a catch-all other condition applies
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Type Code filter field must be cleared so no value is displayed, and the field must be set to MODIFIABLE so the user can freely enter a new type code filter value

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Type Code Filter Field and Keep It Modifiable for All Other Conditions
all_rules.Rule_Description: When no row actions are pending, no recognized filter state applies, and the filter value is not zero or empty, the Type Code filter field must be cleared and kept editable so the user can freely enter a new filter value.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is displayed and the user has previously entered a description filter value, and at least one row on the screen has a pending action (delete or update) requested by the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen is being prepared for display and the system evaluates the display attributes for the description filter field
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must display the previously entered description filter value in the description filter field, set the field attribute to PROTECTED (skip-enabled, auto-skip) so the user cannot modify it, and set the field color to BLUE to visually indicate it is locked during the pending action

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Description Filter Field in Blue and Protected When Row Actions Are Pending
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user has selected a delete or update action on any row currently displayed on the Transaction Type maintenance screen, the description filter field must be displayed in blue color and set to protected (read-only), showing the previously entered description filter value. This prevents the user from changing filter criteria while an action is in progress.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is being prepared for display, no row-level actions (delete or update) are currently pending, and the description filter field either contains a valid filter value that was accepted by the system OR the description filter has been marked as invalid due to a validation error (no records found for the filter)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the display attributes for the description filter field
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must display the previously entered description filter value in the description filter field and set the field attribute to MODIFIABLE (field send enable) so the user can edit or clear the filter value

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Description Filter Field as Modifiable with Entered Value When Filter Is Active or Has Validation Error
all_rules.Rule_Description: When no row actions are pending and the description filter field either contains a valid filter value or has been flagged as invalid due to a validation error, the system must display the entered description value in the field and allow the user to edit it. This applies both when the filter successfully returned records and when the filter produced an error condition.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is being prepared for display, no row-level actions (delete or update) are currently pending, and the description filter field has not been supplied with any value (it is blank, low-values, or spaces — neither a valid filter nor an invalid filter condition exists)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the display attributes for the description filter field and none of the specific filter conditions (actions pending, filter valid, filter invalid) are met
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must set the description filter field attribute to MODIFIABLE (field send enable) so the user can freely enter a description filter value, and no prior value is displayed in the field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Description Filter Field as Empty and Modifiable When No Filter Has Been Supplied
all_rules.Rule_Description: When no row actions are pending and no description filter has been supplied by the user (the field is blank), the description filter field must be presented as an empty, editable field ready for user input. No value is pre-populated in the field.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is being prepared for display and the description filter field has been marked as invalid or in error — specifically because no records were found in the Transaction Type table matching the entered description filter criteria
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system applies the final display attribute overrides after the initial field display state has been determined
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must override the description filter field color to RED to visually signal the error condition to the user, and must position the screen cursor on the description filter field so the user's attention is immediately directed to correct the invalid filter value

all_rules.Rule_Name: Override Description Filter Field to Red with Cursor Positioning When Filter Validation Has Failed
all_rules.Rule_Description: Regardless of the initial display state set for the description filter field, if the description filter has been marked as invalid (e.g., no records were found matching the filter criteria), the system must override the field color to RED and position the cursor on the description filter field. This error highlight applies after all other display attribute decisions have been made and acts as a final override to draw the user's attention to the problematic filter.

description:
COTRTLIC is an online CICS program that provides a paginated list screen for viewing, updating, and deleting Transaction Type records from the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE DB2 table. It supports forward and backward paging using DB2 cursors, allows users to filter records by transaction type code or description, and enables single-record update or delete operations with confirmation via PF10. Based on the Linkage Section using DFHCOMMAREA and EXEC CICS calls with XCTL and RETURN, this is a Main/Driver program within the CardDemo application.
- **Execution Environment**: Online (CICS) - **Database Access**: DB2 - **MQ Calls**: No - **Module Type**: Main module
### Key Functionalities: 1: Program Initialization - Initialize working storage areas, communication areas, and set default values for a new session or carry forward existing session data from the communication area 2: Session Context Setup - Store the current transaction ID, program name, map name, and mapset name to maintain session context across screen interactions 3: First-Time Entry Detection - Detect if this is the first time the program is entered (no communication area) and initialize paging variables, setting the screen to the first page 4: Return-from-Add-Screen Detection - Detect if the user pressed PF3 from the Add/Update transaction type screen and reset the list screen to a fresh state starting from the first page 5: Screen Input Reception - Receive user input from the Transaction Type List screen, capturing the type code filter, description filter, row selection flags, transaction type codes, and descriptions entered by the user 6: Row Selection Validation - Validate each row's action selection field to ensure only valid action codes (U for Update, D for Delete) are entered, flagging invalid entries and counting deletes and updates requested 7: Multiple Action Prevention - Check if more than one row has been selected for action and set an error condition requiring the user to select only one action at a time 8: Row Description Change Detection - For rows where Update is requested, compare the entered description against the stored description to detect if any changes have been made by the user 9: Row Description Validation - Validate that the updated description field contains only alphanumeric characters and is not blank when an update action is requested 10: Type Code Filter Validation - Validate the transaction type code filter entered by the user, ensuring it is a 2-digit numeric value if supplied, or treating it as blank/no-filter if not supplied 11: Type Code Filter Change Detection - Detect if the type code filter has changed compared to the previously stored filter value, and reset paging variables if a new filter is applied 12: Description Filter Validation - Validate the description filter entered by the user, treating it as blank if not supplied, or wrapping it with wildcard characters for a LIKE search if supplied 13: Description Filter Change Detection - Detect if the description filter has changed compared to the previously stored filter value, and reset paging variables if a new filter is applied 14: Filter Cross-Validation - When either a type code or description filter is supplied, verify that at least one matching record exists in the Transaction Type table; set an error if no records are found for the given filter conditions 15: PF Key Validation - Determine which function key the user pressed and validate whether it is permissible in the current context (Enter, PF2, PF3, PF7, PF8, PF10 with delete or update pending) 16: Exit to Main Menu - When PF3 is pressed, transfer control back to the administration menu program, passing the communication area with updated context 17: Navigate to Add Transaction Type Screen - When PF2 is pressed, transfer control to the Add/Update Transaction Type program to allow adding a new transaction type 18: Forward Paging - Read the next page of transaction type records from the database starting from the last key of the current page, incrementing the page number and displaying up to 7 records 19: Backward Paging - Read the previous page of transaction type records from the database by reading backwards from the first key of the current page, decrementing the page number and filling up to 7 rows in reverse order 20: First Page Boundary Check - When PF7 is pressed and already on the first page, re-display the first page without navigating further back, informing the user there are no previous pages 21: Delete Confirmation Request - When Enter is pressed with a delete action selected, re-display the screen highlighting the selected row and prompting the user to press PF10 to confirm the deletion 22: Delete Record Execution - When PF10 is pressed to confirm deletion, delete the selected transaction type record from the database by its type code 23: Delete Success Handling - After a successful deletion, display a success message, reset the session state, and return to the first page of the list 24: Delete Failure - Child Records Exist - If deletion fails because child records are associated with the transaction type, inform the user to delete associated child records first before retrying 25: Update Confirmation Request - When Enter is pressed with an update action selected, re-display the screen highlighting the selected row and prompting the user to press PF10 to save the update 26: Update Record Execution - When PF10 is pressed to confirm update, update the description of the selected transaction type record in the database with the new value entered by the user 27: Update Success Handling - After a successful update, display a success message and refresh the list to show the updated data 28: No Change Detection for Update - If the user requests an update but the description entered is identical to the existing database value, inform the user that no changes were detected 29: F10 with Changed Criteria Handling - If PF10 is pressed to confirm a delete or update but the filter criteria or row selection has changed, treat the action as a regular Enter key press instead of confirming the action 30: Transaction Type List Display - Build and send the Transaction Type List screen to the user, showing up to 7 transaction type records with their codes and descriptions, along with page number, current date, current time, and action selection fields 31: Screen Attribute Setup for Actions - Set screen field attributes (color, protection, cursor position) based on the current action state: highlight selected rows for delete or update, protect rows when errors exist, mark invalid selections in red 32: Search Filter Display - Display the current type code and description filter values on the screen, applying appropriate colors and protection attributes based on filter validity and action state 33: Informational Message Display - Display context-sensitive informational messages to guide the user, such as instructions to type U or D to select actions, confirmation prompts for delete or update, success messages, or no-more-pages notifications 34: Error Message Display - Display error messages on the screen when input validation fails, such as invalid action codes, multiple actions selected, invalid filter values, or no records found 35: Next Page Existence Check - After reading a page of records, perform an extra fetch to determine if more records exist beyond the current page, setting the next-page indicator accordingly 36: No Records Found Notification - When a forward read returns no records on the first page, inform the user that no records were found for the current search conditions 37: Last Page Tracking - Track whether the last page has already been displayed to the user, and show an appropriate message when the user attempts to page beyond the last available page 38: Session State Persistence - Save the current program state including paging keys, screen data, selected row, delete/update flags, and filter values into the communication area to be passed back on the next user interaction 39: Function Key Aliasing - Map PF13 through PF24 keys to their equivalent PF1 through PF12 actions respectively, so that users on terminals with only upper-row function keys can perform the same actions as users pressing PF1-PF12 40: Informational Message Centering - Automatically center informational messages on the screen by calculating the trimmed message length and computing the midpoint offset, ensuring messages are displayed in a visually balanced position for the user
